Among these mines, N4E is not only the largest but also the oldest. Open pit mining operation with the use of trucks and shovels at N4E started in 1984. Ore is treated through crushing and screening. Generally, N4E contributes a significant amount to the total 25 Mt/y of run-of-mine production in the Carajas complex.

title: Mining and regional development in Peru
authors: Golte J.
abstract: Mining has a 4000 years old history in the Central Andes. In the time of the Viceroyalty of Peru the mining of silver and gold has been the centre of spatial organization of different types of production (agriculture and manufacture) and forced labour services of the indigenous population. The outdated colonial mining techniques led to a virtual collapse of the mining sector with the independence of Peru. After 1850 the mining sector recovered with labour intensive exploitation of silver, iron, copper and gold deposits. The salaries for the unskilled labour force recruited in surrounding Indian communities led to a slow development of the hinterland of the mining centres. The revenue for the Peruvian state on the other hand resulted in an increasing service economy in Lima depending on the redistribution of tax income through the state to a privileged sector of the population. Modern open pit mining in Peru is globally competitive and contributes to more than 50 % of Peruvian exports. Due to the consumption of the revenue by a privileged social sector and the increasing industrialization of the mining process (with a small and academically educated labour force) with little impact on the regional population the lucrative ore mines are nowadays surrounded by impoverished peasants. So the mining industry, technically efficient, is confronted ever more by social unrest.

title: Efficiency of a Bucket Wheel Excavator lignite mining system
source: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
authors: Kolovos C.
keywords: Bucket Wheel Excavator | Evaluation of equipment | Greece | Lignite surface mining | Macedonia | Selective mining
matched_open_pit_phrases: open pit mine; open pit mining
abstract: Bucket Wheel Excavator (BWE) based systems are used worldwide in open pit mining of soft to medium hard rock materials such as lignite, phosphate, etc. This paper presents a 15-year analysis of actual performance data of a Greek, medium-sized, lignite open pit mine. In this mine, BWEs are used for the continuous, selective mining of lignite. Conveyor belts are used for transporting the excavated material to stackers at the lignite stockyards or to the waste dumping sites. The basic excavation equipment had already been used in another mine. As a result, the BWEs examined are rather old machines and their combined service life has exceeded 40 years. Remarkably, no decrease in the overall performance was observed and further utilization of these BWEs is scheduled.

title: Tire Awareness Program
authors: Tattersall A.; Mine C.; Johnson B.
abstract: Tire awareness program, a program started by the Coeur Rochester company with the assistance of the Elite Tire Management System (ETMS) to improve the performance of tires is discussed. After using this program the improvement acheived in tire life over the haulage and loading fleets have ranged from 11% to 45% without any effect on quality. The efforts to improve tire performance are directed at all members of the tire team, including management and supervision. The program focuses on the tire use and abuse and is equally applicable to the full range of performances in open pit mining or in any other industrial operation.

title: The situation of the surface coal mines in Vietnam and their future development
source: World of Mining Surface and Underground
authors: Bui X.N.; Ho S.G.; Drebenstedt C.
abstract: The situation of the surface coal mines in Vietnam and their developments are evaluated. Open pit mining has been contributing a great deal to the total output of coal produced in Vietnam. In order to secure their stable position in Vietnam's coal mining sector, the surface coal mines will have to upgrade their technology, equipment, and management to meet demands, and adopt the proper strategy to develop in the future. The responsibility lies with not only the Vietnamese surface coal mines but also the Vietnam Coal Corporation and the ministries and the government.

title: Bauxite Mining Activities of Silver and Baryte Ores Mining Co. S.A.
authors: Peppas S.; Christou N.; Giamas A.
keywords: Bauxite | Mining | Reclamation | Reserves | Sales
abstract: Silver and Baryte Ores Mining Co. S.A has a long history in Bauxite mining starting back in 1933. Mining activities are located in the Parnass-Giona mountain range in Central Greece. A detailed picture is given of all the aspects connected with the exploitation of the Greek bauxite. These aspects are the geological-mineralogical conditions of the genesis of the bauxitic material, bauxite reserves, sales, underground and open pit mining, ore processing, reclamation, contractors, and a final outlook into the future.

title: Sizing equipment for open pit mining - A review of critical parameters
source: Institution of Mining and Metallurgy Transactions Section A Mining Technology
authors: Bozorgebrahimi E.; Hall R.; Blackwell G.
keywords: Open pit mining | Sizing equipment
abstract: Over the past century, open pit mines have steadily increased their production rate. Larger equipment and new technologies make it possible to mine larger batches of materials in a shorter time. Low commodity prices have forced companies to decrease their unit cost, by using new technologies and improving productivity. In the late 20th century, with companies facing low commodity prices and competing with strong rivals globally, larger equipment with lower unit costs ensured survival. As a result, mine geometry and mining equipment have dramatically increased in size. To date, in terms of productivity, the mining industry continues to adhere to the 'bigger is better' mentality. There are indications that this strategy may not always be advantageous. This paper will discuss on-going research into understanding the effects of equipment size on surface mining. The research includes investigation of mine and mill construction and operating costs, mine productivity, mine design, and economic optimisation. It identifies the significant variables that need to be considered and suggests an approach to quantify their impact on the mine. The paper also proposes a new view to mine planning and equipment selection with respect to the sensitivity to equipment size factors. © 2003 IoM Communications Ltd.

title: Quarrying and open pit mining
authors: Fernberg H.
abstract: Large quantities of raw material are produced in various types of surface operations. Where the product is rock, the operations are known as quarries. Where metallic ore or non-metallic minerals are involved, they are called open pit mines. There are many common parameters in design and choice of equipment, and in process of finding the best combination of drilling and blasting methods, Atlas Copco has the advantage of long experience in all types of surface drilling operations, with a product range to match. With its history of innovative engineering, the company tends to think forward, and is able to advise the user on improving design elements of the operation that will result in overall cost savings.

title: Reliability modelling of surface mining equipment: Data gathering and analysis methodologies
source: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
authors: Hall R.; Daneshmend L.
keywords: Data analysis | Maintenance | Reliability modelling
abstract: As the size and complexity of open pit mining equipment continue to increase, the implications of equipment failure become ever more critical. An unplanned failure can result in significantly higher repair costs than a planned maintenance or repair. Of even more importance is the loss of production associated with larger equipment failures. One method to mitigate the impact of failures is to improve the reliability of the equipment. A first step in reliability improvement is collection and analysis of the appropriate data. This paper will summarize relevant techniques for reliability analysis and identify data requirements and information sources.

title: Thermal rock fragmentation - Applications in narrow-vein extraction
authors: Poirier S.; Fecteau J.M.; Laflamme M.; Brisebois D.
keywords: Bulk sampling | Drilling | Narrow-vein extraction | Open pit mining | Rock breaking | Thermal rock fragmentation
abstract: This paper focusses on new developments regarding thermal rock fragmentation applications. The technology consists of a strong burner powered by diesel fuel and air. The thermal reaction that is created allows for the enlargement of 125 mm to 450 mm holes by breaking the rock in a spalling effect. It has been used for over 30 years in Russian open pit mining. Following an agreement between Dynamitage T.C.G. Inc. and the owner of the technology, major improvements have been brought to this technology, allowing for the fabrication of a prototype suitable for the Canadian industry. In Russia and the Ukraine, thermal rock fragmentation is actually used to drill large diameter holes in surface mining. Upon having acquired a better knowledge of this technology, it seems that it presents a great potential for selective mining in narrow-vein operations, for either surface or underground mining. Rocmec International Inc., a subsidiary of Dynamitage T.C.G. Inc., and Natural Resources Canada are technical partners in the evaluation of the operational parameters and environmental aspects such as gas, heat, dust and fog emissions. Furthermore, Canada Economic Development is a financial partner in this project. This paper presents the technology and its history. It also reports on the changes brought to the equipment to adapt it to North American environments. A summary of the tests carried out since 1995 is provided, along with the main conclusions obtained. The anticipated applications for the use of this technology in both surface and underground environments are described such as open pit mining, bulk sampling and narrow-vein ore extraction. An estimate showing a comparison between the thermal fragmentation mining concept and the long-hole mining method is presented and, finally, the future developments planned are listed.

title: Recultivation of gravel pits and quarries in Lower Saxony
source: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
authors: Fahlbusch M.
keywords: Consolidated rock | Environmental protection | Non-metallic minerals | Recultivation | Unconsolidated rock
abstract: The determination of the requirements for recultivation plays a crucial role in the statutory licensing procedure for the open pit mining of non-metallic minerals. In recent years, a working aid has been developed for the application of control regulations for environmental protection in raw material mining proposals in Lower Saxony. Since the licensing authorities of the individual counties proceeded very differently, the goal was to achieve a uniform state-wide regulation with regard to the scope of recultivation measures to be carried out. The plan of the working aid was submitted in 1999 by Lower Saxony's Department of Environmental Protection and subsequently revised over several years in a referendum process which included the industry. The paper should be valid for licensing procedures according to State Environmental Protection Law and State Water Law. The working aid should be regarded as a technical standard in licensing procedures which are carried out according to other specialized legislation such as the Federal Mining Law and the Federal Law for Emission Protection. The organization of the contents of the working aid and the steps to be carried out are illustrated within the framework of this paper. Using unconsolidated and solid rock mining as an example, the requirements for recultivation which result from the application of the working aid are explained.

title: The Grande Cache Coal project
authors: Cain P.; Martens B.
keywords: Coal mining | Grande Cache Coal project | Reclamation | Sustainable development
abstract: Grande Cache Coal (GCC), an investor-owned Alberta company, is in the final stages of the regulatory process leading to the resumption of coal mining in the Smoky River Coal Field of Alberta. Although many opportunities for low-cost, high-yield mining remained on the property, GCC opted for a long-term production plan that ensures stability for the local economy, sustainable use of the resources in the area, environmental responsibility and a satisfactory return for its investors. GCC entered the Alberta coal approval process in late 2000 with a public disclosure document. In October 2001, GCC formally submitted an application for mining approval and an environmental impact assessment (EIA) to the government and the public. The application covered the proposed Grande Cache Coal project, which includes the No. 7 underground mine, No. 8 surface mine and coal processing operations. The EIA provided a comprehensive investigation of environmental sensitivities in the project area, matched with environmental protection programs. The project is based on commencement of operations in late 2002. GCC's plans are founded on a commitment to sustainable development and has framed this commitment in the context of a long-range mine development plan that will sustain the community of Grande Cache over the next 25 years. The Grande Cache coalfields offer extensive coal reserves and opportunities, for both surface and underground mining. Combining highly productive U.S.-style room-and-pillar underground mining methods and conventional truck-and-shovel open pit mining, GCC's approach to sustainable development encompasses community involvement and reclamation of mine sites to productive land uses after mining.

title: Characterization of suspended particulate matter in mining areas in São Paulo, Brazil
source: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
authors: Almeida I.T.; Eston S.M.; de Assunçao J.V.
keywords: Air pollution | Characterization | Chemical analysis | Hi-vol | Particle size distribution | Particulate matter | Total suspended particulate
abstract: Atmospheric pollution aspects in mining are analyzed. Two types of environment have been selected for study: an open pit mining site and a quarry. In order to obtain a preliminary evaluation of the air quality in these environments, a sampling program was developed for each area. Three basic points were studied: 1. Concentration of total suspended particulate; 2. Chemical and 3. Physical characterization of the particulate matter. The concentrations of total suspended particulate (TSP) were obtained by the use of the high volume sampler method. The analytic techniques applied to the particulate matter were X-Ray Fluorescence (XRF) for chemical characterization, and Low Angle Laser Light Scattering (LALLS) for physical characterization. Physical characterization involved particle size distribution of the suspended particulate matter, whereas the chemical characterization involved determination of its composition.

title: Expert system for equipment selection
source: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
authors: Ganguli R.; Bandopadhyay S.
keywords: Database | Equipment selection | Expert system | Object oriented programming | Open pit mining | Uncertainty
abstract: An expert system was developed for equipment selection for various unit operations in open pit mining. For each unit operation, it considers a wide variety of equipment and ranks them based on their suitability. A major difference between this system and other published expert systems in the considered domain is that it incorporates the uncertainty that is an inherent characteristic of the factors affecting equipment selection. It also allows users to specify the site-specific relative importance of each of the governing factors. This makes the system relatively flexible and allows its adaptation to different mining conditions. The programming features of the expert system include uncertainty databases and object oriented programming. The expert system is validated with a case study (Malanjkhand Copper Mine, India).

title: Slide cam compound grease lubricant: Development and field evaluation
authors: Samman N.; Hetherington P.; Johnson S.
abstract: Walking draglines in open pit mining have unique lubrication requirements. The lubrication requirements of the Bucyrus-Erie (BE) cam and slide walking cam mechanism used on some walking draglines are considered. The evolution of walking cam lubricants is outlined. The development of summer and winter grade grease lubricants for the BE cam and slide walking cam mechanism is described. Slide rig testing and field trials with the lubricants are reported. The lubricants met the desired lubrication performance in mine site operations.

title: Rock fall in surface mining
authors: Brawner C.O.; Kalejta J.
keywords: Blasting | Catch fences | Rock mechanics | Surface mining
abstract: The classical approach to control rock fall and ravel in open pit mining has been to use catch benches. The width and volume of benches is most dependent on the bench height, size of loading equipment, blast damage to the face and mining regulations. This was compatible with open pit slopes of less than approximately 45 degrees. As our understanding of rock mechanics and blasting control has improved over recent years, much steeper rock slopes can be developed at many open pit mines. However, narrower benches result in less rock fall capacity. The transportation industry has been very successful in using catch fences to protect highways throughout North America and Europe for years. The authors recommend that cable and ring net fences have a potential major application in open pit mining to allow steeper rock slopes with significant economic benefit. This paper outlines the application, design and operation of catch fences in surface mining for specific conditions. Typical case examples are presented.

title: Ambient air quality in the bauxite mining area of Yercaud hills in Eastern Ghats
authors: Muthusubramanian P.; Jeba Rajasekhar R.V.
keywords: Ambient air quality | Mining area and its neighbourhood | NO2 | SO2 | Suspended particulate matter (SPM)
abstract: The Sheveroys also known as Yercaud hills, the presnt study area, are situated to the north east of Salem city in the state of Tamil Nadu of India and form a major hill range at the southern most point of the Eastern Ghats. The biosphere reserves of this region are threatened due to mining and deforestation acivities. The bauxite of Shevaroy hill is being exploited for aluminium production. Bauxite production is through open pit mining. The objective of this present study is to assess the impact of bauxite mining on the quality of air in the Yercaud hills for all seasons of the year 1997. For air sampling 4 vantage points were selected and fixed for the continuous monitoring of the air quality aid meteorological parameters, such as temperature, humidity, wind speed and wind direction, both inside and outside of mines for all the seasons in a year. The samples were collected weekly at all the 4 sites by drawing a known volume of air through a membrane of glass microfibre filter for 8 hr using a high volume sampler to estimate the concentration levels of sulphur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide and suspended particulate matter (SPM). It is found that at all the sites and seasons, the concentration levels of these air pollutants are within the permissible limits. The reasons for the variation of concentration levels of these pollutants with respect to sites and seasons are discussed.

title: Development of open pit mining CAD system using object ARX
source: Kuangye Yanjiu Yu Kaifa Mining Research and Development
authors: Jiang A.N.; Sun H.R.; Qiu J.P.

title: "Natura 2000" - Impact on the mining of deposits near the surface
source: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
authors: Fahlbusch M.
abstract: The European environmental protection legislation has had the effect of complicating mining of deposits near the surface in Europe. The Union's "Natura 2000" programme is a current topic of discussion. - The creation of "Natura 2000" brings with it nature conservation areas for certain ecosystems and animals as well as the conservation areas for certain birds. Additional nature conservation areas, based on the Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora and the Council Directive 79/409/EEC of 2 April 1979 on the conservation of wild birds, will further limit the surface area available for mining of raw materials. The large-area environmental protection intended by "Natura 2000" presents particular problems for the mining of raw materials, which depends on connected areas. - In some cases, mining of raw materials itself is fundamentally questioned through "Natura 2000". At the very least, "Natura 2000" means significant additional expenditure in the fields of project planning, operation and recultivation of open pit mining operations. - The effects of the "Natura 2000" should be avoided. In addition to the traditional geological, technical and economical restrictions of mining planning, new planning restrictions are added which, when left unconsidered, would force a mining project to be unauthorized.

title: Coalbed methane prospect of Jamalganj coalfield, Bangladesh
source: Arabian Journal for Science and Engineering
authors: Imam M.B.; Rahman M.; Akhter S.H.
keywords: Bangladesh | Coal Bed Methane | Gondwana Coalfields | Jamalganj
abstract: Five major Gondwana coalfields have been discovered in the half-graben type basins in the subsurface in the Precambrian platform area of northwest Bangladesh. The Jamalganj coalfield, with an estimated reserve of about 1053 million tons of coal, has seven coal seams in the depth range between 640 to 1158 m below the ground surface. Compared to the other coalfields of the area, with coal occurring at 150 to 500 m depth, Jamalganj coal is considered to be too deep to be exploited by conventional underground or open pit mining. Instead, developing coal bed methane from Jamalganj coalfield may be considered as a viable option for its exploitation. The positive factors of Jamalganj coal bed methane development include high net thickness of coal with at least one very thick (40 m+) and widely developed seam, coal seam burial depth within optimum range, large coal reserves, indication of significant gas content from drilling data, and poor permeability in the rocks above and surrounding the coal layers. The thickest seam III can be a primary target for CBM development especially where it combines with seam IV in the eastern part of the coalfield. However, there are a number of unknown factors like actual gas content of coal, the coal permeability, and in-seam pressure that need to be evaluated before deciding the viability of the project. An initial attempt to collect these baseline data should include drilling test well or wells in the primary target area where seam III is most thick and widely developed.

title: A simulative model for optimum open pit design
authors: Erarslan K.; Çelebi N.
keywords: Dynamic programming | Mine simulation | Optimum pit design | Profit maximization
matched_open_pit_phrases: open pit mine; open pit mining
abstract: Previous research in the area of open pit mine optimization has focused on profit maximization by optimizing pit limits or optimizing production schedules. However, these two approaches are interrelated and dependent on each other. Recent studies have recognized the limitation of this optimization approach. Consequently, there is a need for a more comprehensive modelling strategy. Such an optimization model should incorporate mining activities that are simulated (as they are expected to occur) as much as possible. Considerations should be given to such parameters as the cut-off ore grade, the starting location of mining, equipment selection, annual production rates, excavation sequence, and the synchronization of the mining plant operations during the planning stage of the mine. A change in any of these parameters will cause a concomitant change in other parameters. Therefore an efficient optimization system is one that attempts to simulate the mine in a comprehensive manner and thereby provides more realistic results. In this study, a new profit maximization model that determines optimum pit limit as a function of optimum production scheduling has been developed. The model allows for the progressive addition of new ore blocks as well as for process plant feeding. The model gives realistic estimates of the unit cost for each new condition of the pit as part of an overall economic analysis of the integrated mining and ore processing operation. Optimization of the entire mining operation is achieved through the minimization of idle times of the processing plant and through maintaining a uniform ore feed to the processing plant. The proposed model has been programmed in C++, and it has been used to analyze a number of typical open pit mining scenarios. The results obtained using the model have proved the validity of this new modelling approach.

title: Cover design for radioactive and AMD-producing mine waste in the Ronneburg area, Eastern Thuringia
authors: Gatzweiler R.; Jahn S.; Neubert G.; Paul M.
abstract: At the former uranium mining site of Ronneburg, large scale underground and open pit mining for nearly 40 years resulted in a production of about 113 000 tonnes of uranium and about 200 million cubic metres of mine waste. In their present state, these materials cause risks to human health and strong environmental impacts and therefore demand remedial action. The remediation options available are relocation of mine spoil into the open pit and on site remediation by landscaping/contouring, placement of a cover and revegetation. A suitable vegetated cover system combined with a surface water drainage system provides long-term stability against erosion and reduces acid generation thereby meeting the main remediation objectives which are long-term reduction of radiological exposure and contaminant emissions and recultivation. The design of the cover system includes the evaluation of geotechnical, radiological, hydrological, geochemical and ecological criteria and models. The optimized overall model for the cover system has to comply with general conditions as, e.g. economic efficiency, public acceptance and sustainability. Most critical elements for the long-term performance of the cover system designed for the Beerwalde dump are the barrier system and its long-term integrity and a largely self-sustainable vegetation. © 2001 Elsevier Science Ltd.

title: The Big Whopper rare metals pegmatite, separation rapids, Ontario
authors: Pearse G.H.K.; Taylor R.P.
keywords: Big Whopper | Geology | Industrial minerals | Pegmatites | Rare metals
abstract: The Big Whopper, one of only four giant economic rare metal pegmatites worldwide, is set to become a producer of the highly valued lithium mineral petalite (LiAISi<inf>4</inf>O<inf>10</inf>) used in glass, ceramics and the specialty glass-ceramics familiar as Comingware and the new ceramic stovetops. The deposit has a strike length of 1.5 km, a width of up to 80 m and a resource, open in all directions, of 11.6 Mt, grading 25% petalite. It is amenable to open pit mining and Avalon Ventures Ltd. holds a patent on a flotation process that produces an exceptional quality petalite product. The project will also produce: Superb quality Na-feldspar which, too, finds use in glass and ceramics; the unusual Rb-K-feldspar for high voltage porcelain insulators; tantalum, in high demand for electronics; lepidolite, an ore of rubidium; and mica and tin. A positive prefeasibility study has been completed and it remains only to undertake bulk sampling and a full feasibility study.

title: Optimising life of mine production schedules in multiple open pit mining operations: A study of effects of production constraints on NPV
authors: Ricciardone J.; Chanda E.K.
abstract: Life of mine scheduling involves sequencing and timing of ore and waste movement during the life of a mine and therefore, has a significant effect on the cash flow of a mining operation. Mine planners often seek to optimise the production schedule with respect to maximise net present value (NPV) of the cash flows. The complexity of mine production scheduling in practice entails a computer solution using mathematical programming as the optimisation technique. Linear and mixed integer programming techniques have been used to optimise long-term production schedules but most of the computer programs based on these make overly simplifying assumptions and lack the flexibility to handle practical considerations of mine scheduling. MineMax™ scheduling software is applied to long term scheduling for a multiple open pit operation. The effects of constraining production and the number of pits on the NPV are analysed. The greater selectivity allowed by unconstrained mine production is offset by increased operational costs resulting in insignificant changes to the NPV. Constraining the number of active pits per period limits the mine planner's ability to find ore of a specified blend. Although it is desirable to produce at constant rate and to limit the number of active pits per period, this strategy places limitations on the grade of ore that can be mined and milled, hence having a detrimental effect on the NPV. This study shows that allowing both the production and number active pits to fluctuate within practical limits improves the NPV of the project.

title: Environmental problems and policies in East Central Europe: A changing agenda
authors: Turnock D.
keywords: Education | Environmental policy | European Union | Health | Non-governmental organisations (NGOs) | Pollution | Quality of life | Sustainability
abstract: Considerable environmental damage occurred during the socialist era as a consequence of the rapid rate of economic growth with low priority for the quality of life. High levels of air and water pollution impacted negatively on human health as well as the physical environment. The rural areas did not escape because of soil and forest degradation, while open pit mining and associated tipping devastated large areas of countryside especially in former Czechoslovakia and East Germany. The Chernobyl nuclear disaster proved to be a turning point since public opinion was mobilised to the point that underground movements began to lobby for improvements and environmental quality became a factor in system change in 1989. Much has been achieved over the past decade, thanks in part to expertise and financial help from abroad, and the priority currently being given to membership of the European Union means that all the requirements of the environmental 'acquis' must be met over the medium term. However, the 1990s have also introduced the sustainability agenda and current challenges are much more extensive that those of the past. While many obligations now carry the full force of law, it is also evident that sustainability is a matter for interpretation nationally and locally in the light of economic pressures and cultural values, moderated through the education process and negotiation with both statutory bodies and environmental non-governmental organisations (ENGOs). This paper therefore serves as a context for the more local studies that follow.

title: Selecting a mining method for metalliferous orebodies
source: Monograph Series Australasian Institute of Mining and Metallurgy
authors: Kaesehagen F.
abstract: The selection of mining method is the major decision in the conversion of a mineralised resource into an Ore Reserve. It is important that the geologists and mining engineers work as a team in this selection process. This paper will cover the key issues that impact on this decision using projects that the author has worked as illustrations. These are orebody geometry, grade, geotechnical data and metallurgical response. All must be considered in selecting a mining system for a new orebody. The advantages of open pit mining over underground mining particular in the areas of costs, speed of development and safety are well illustrated. Environmental issues with waste storage is the only negative which will emerge. Consequently the majority of new large mine developments continue to be open pits. It will also be demonstrated that underground mining will continue to play an important role particularly for high-grade deposits at depth. The impact of recent developments in stabilised fill technology in underground mining on ore recoveries and hence ore reserves will also be highlighted. The importance of economics to the decision on mining method will be continually emphasised as maximising the resource value should be the prime objective of the planning team.

title: Geotechnical applications in open pit mining
authors: Bye A.; Bell F.
keywords: Geotechnical control | Open pit mine production | Slope stability
abstract: Detailed geotechnical data is often a major unknown factor in open pit design and mining, the lack of which constitutes a significant risk in any mining venture. As geotechnical data is accumulated so the risk of unforeseen conditions reduces, and so safety and productivity can be increased. Previously, most geotechnical work undertaken at open pit mines has focused on the slopes. The work done at Sandsloot open pit situated on the northern limb of the Bushveld Complex, 250 km north east of Johannesburg, however, has involved using geotechnical data for production, as well as slope stability benefits. Solutions to production problems encountered in a rapidly developing open pit are best formulated once some geotechnical control at the pit has been attained. At Sandsloot open pit this was achieved by delineation of geotechnical design zones from a detailed face mapping and drilling programme. Optimum design parameters then were assigned to these zones and geotechnically related problems assessed. This allowed slope management programmes to be initiated, as well as slope optimization of the hangingwall. The latter resulted in an improved slope configuration and an increase in the ultimate angle of the wall by 7°. This resulted in substantial savings, as well as an improvement in safety. In addition, the zones can be used for planning, costing and pit scheduling. The methods have proved successful in optimizing blast fragmentation and thereby loading, crushing and milling rates; in reducing secondary blasting and improving floor conditions; and in reducing drilling, blasting and comminution costs.

title: Practical application of computer models for controlling of open pit mining
source: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
authors: Oehmen M.
abstract: The paper describes a "living" deposit model which is updated continuously by the mine itself. It also can be regarded as an "interactive model". Topography data such as the mine situation as well as data of the deposit itself are added continuously and can be retrieved at any time, by any person interested in information of the model. In that case it will be possible to store, to visualize and to work on three dimensional data of the deposit directly by the mine people. In this way short and mid term mine scheduling and planning could be significantly improved.

title: Development of excavator of great unit power for unexplosive rock working
source: Fiziko Tekhnicheskie Problemy Razrabotki Poleznykh Iskopaemykh
authors: Mattis A.; Zajtsev G.
abstract: A bucket capacity and a basic model are substantiated for an excavator of great power for unexplosive working. A comparative estimate is made for the technical and technological indices of the new excavator and the machine for layer-by-layer cutting. It is concluded that introduction of the excavators EKG-12V in the open pit mining increases efficiency of mining-loading works and broadens the field of applications of unexplosive technologies.

title: Evaluating the effect of the initiation method on blasting by seismographic monitoring and image analysis
authors: Segui J.; Koppe J.; Costa J.
abstract: Explosives performance depend on how the chemical energy available in the explosive mass is released and consequently, transferred to the rock mass. The initiation method is one of the uttermost importance in this process. This paper analyses the influence of two distinct methods of initiation, i.e. top side and point initiation in the blasting results. Ammonium nitrate and fuel oil (ANFO) detonation is highly sensitive to the way it is initiated. As ANFO is the most common explosive in open pit mining, it was chosen for comparing the initiation methods. Different blasts were monitored using a triaxial electronic seismograph. Image analysis complements the monitoring program, providing the information to compare different shots. A case study illustrates the methodology used for data acquisition. Experimental results proved the superior efficiency of point initiation and showed a reliable method of evaluate explosive performance.

title: An averaging procedure for layered materials
source: International Journal for Numerical and Analytical Methods in Geomechanics
authors: Niemunis A.; Karcher C.; Theile T.
keywords: Averaging | Composite materials | Constitutive modeling | Finite elements | Laminate | Layered soils
abstract: In order to model thin-layered soils a special averaging procedure is proposed. It works with very few restrictions imposed on the constitutive equations used for individual materials. General considerations are followed by an example from open pit mining industry. Geometrical non-linearity is considered. The proposed method is not necessarily restricted to the problems of soil mechanics. It could also be applied on composite materials. Copyright (C) 2000 John Wiley and Sons, Ltd.

title: Industry briefs: Oilsands: Canadian Natural Resources Ltd.
abstract: Canadian Natural Resources Ltd, Calgary, will develop a $(Can)6.5 billion oilsands and heavy oil operation in the Fort McMurray region of northern Alberta. The Mic Mac project would be developed on leases from BP Amoco plc in 1999. The project, which would start production in 7 yr, pending regulatory approvals, would have initial production of 300,000 bpd from a combination of open pit mining and a heavy oil operation.

title: Automatic monitoring of slope deformations using geotechnical instruments
authors: Ding X.; Ren D.; Montgomery B.; Swindells C.
abstract: Monitoring the deformation and other useful physical parameters of slopes, either natural mountain slopes or those formed in open pit mining or construction, is one of the most effective methods to avoid or reduce the risk caused by landslides. The commonly used geotechnical instruments for slope monitoring in the Australian open pit mining industry are first reviewed briefly, then followed by the introduction of an automatic slope monitoring system that is based on integration of electronic geotechnical instruments with specialized software. The design and test results of the system at a mining site in Australia are given in detail. It is shown from the test and a critical assessment of the system that automatic monitoring of slopes offers a number of advantages over manual data-gathering approaches.

title: Effect of combined underground and open pit mining and deformation mechanism of slope
source: Yanshilixue Yu Gongcheng Xuebao Chinese Journal of Rock Mechanics and Engineering
authors: Sun S.; Cai M.; Wang S.
abstract: Because of the influence of combined underground and open pit mining, a part of two mining influence realms is overlapping. It would result in interaction and superimposition of the two kinds of mining effects. Therefore, a system of dynamic superimposition is constituted. The deformation and failure mechanism of slope rock mass are studied under combined underground and open pit mining system. The evaluation method of slope stability is developed on the basis of analysis of theory and case-history.

title: Numerical value analysis of slope rock mass deformation mechanism under combined mining influence
source: Beijing Keji Daxue Xuebao Journal of University of Science and Technology Beijing
authors: Sun S.; Cai M.; Qiao L.
keywords: Deformation mechanism | Mining effect | Slope rock mass | Superimposition
abstract: The change behavior of inner rock mass for combined mining on the basis of analysis of numerical value and actual deformation is explored. Because of effect under combined underground and open pit mining, mechanism about superimposition of deformation and change behavior depends on respectively amount of both mining methods. Deformation of rock mass would more present behavior of underground mining as slope dip angle is small. Therefore, under influence of the same amount in underground excavation, the range and depth of slope deformation are increased as slope dip angle is increased. Both amount of excavation directly influences quantity value and direction of vector. Change of each amount of excavation would make the different behavior of failure and moving mechanism for rock mass is produced.

title: Mining in the 21st century using information technology
authors: Peck J.; Gray J.
keywords: Computer applications | Control systems | Information systems | Monitoring systems | Open pit mining
abstract: For the next few years, open pit mining will see an increased use of monitoring, control and guidance technology on both mobile and stationary mining equipment. These technologies will be integrated with sophisticated communication systems to permit real-time, on-demand use of any information generated. These information systems will form the foundation for future autonomous equipment operation.

title: Reconstruction and modernisation of open pit mining equipment
authors: Schlecht B.
abstract: The bucket wheel excavators, conveyor systems, spreaders and other equipment used in the large open cast mines are investment goods with high procurement costs and a correspondingly long service life usually of more than 30 years. In addition to regular maintenance of the system, it is necessary to replace some individual components or even complete subassemblies from time to time to realize the full performance capabilities of the equipment. The currently most comprehensive program being run by a large-scale operator aimed at modernizing mining equipment is at present underway at the Neyveli Lignite Corporation (NLC) in the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu.

title: Estimation of large open pit haulage truck requirements
authors: Blackwell G.H.
keywords: Equipment | Mine management | Open pit mining | Operating costs | Production costs | Truck fleets
matched_open_pit_phrases: open pit mine; open pit mining
abstract: Open pit mine management must ensure that sufficient trucks are available and are being used effectively for production, and that operating costs are under continued control and review for improvements. This paper describes methods for estimating truck fleet requirements which have been used effectively at large- and medium-sized open pit mining operations. Applied to commonly available data, multiple regression analyses can indicate when mine plans should be revised toward optimizing the number of trucks required. Prediction of major cost items for budgetary purposes is addressed, along with an example of how readily available production data can be used to reduce costs systematically.

title: Economic significance of sub-cutoff grades in open pits operating with concentrator bottleneck
authors: Yi R.; Sturgul J.R.
keywords: Cutoff grade | Mineral economics | Open mining | Stockpiles
matched_open_pit_phrases: open pit mine; open pit mining
abstract: Mathematical models are built and a nonlinear algorithm is coded to determine solutions to cutoff grade, sub-cutoff grade and sub-grade stockpile sizes which optimise the open pit mining from an economic point of view. The purpose is to study the theory that it is more reasonable economically for an open pit mine to stockpile its low grade ores and treat them later, especially if the mine has a bottleneck condition at the concentrator.

title: Management of applications for open pit mining permissions by consultants
source: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
authors: Fahlbusch M.
abstract: Mining projects in countries with high-density population in most cases cause conflicts due to competitive utilization of the countryside and due to their environmental impacts. Project areas can be located near to or even within preserved areas or in the vicinity of settlements, highways or railway lines. The preparation of an application to get permission for an open pit mining project requires the expertise of specialists from different, fields, and is often done by consultants, not by the applicant itself. A team leader should be responsible for coordination and supervision of all activities. He has to take care that all areas of concern are covered in depth and answers to all questions are given. The result should be a comprehensive and conclusive application of high quality. However, the work of the consultants does not end here. In addition to the preparation of the application properly speaking, they have to explain plans and findings to government agencies and to the public during formal and informal meetings and discussions.

title: Pocketlift® - The innovation for steep incline and vertical conveying in the bulk material handling industry
source: Prace Naukowe Instytutu Gornictwa Politechniki Wroclawskiej
authors: Paelke J.
abstract: As previously reported in bulk solids handling [1] the most recent innovation in the field of continuous vertical conveying inthe bulk material handling industry is the POCKETLIFT* -system. This article describes the function and construction of the POCKETLIFT®-technology of the so called S-shape-system for shaft-conveying in the underground mining and tunneling industry, the inner conveyor-system for all types of bulk material in the mineral processing industry, the inner-conveyor concept installed in a mobile continuous ship unloader, as well as the pylon system for quarries and open pit mining.

title: The environment and its constraints in the project management, the integrated development and the case of Madagascar
authors: Raveloson E.; Rakotomaria E.; Ruiz J.
abstract: The Bemolanga tar sands field is in southern Madagascar, Toliary province, an area marked by intense drought, advance deforestation, and general poverty. The development of this tar sands field is associated with environmental constraints and the compatibility of a free trade system. A study based on ~ 3000 bpd production on a skid using a thermal process merits attention because it is the beneficiary of pilot plant tests and semi-industrial plant projects relating to synthetic oil production. To decrease the exploitation costs, a simple and small open pit mining is suggested. Transportation of crude will be only local, not requiring a heavy infrastructure. Products will be transported by medium size trucks. On their return trip, the trucks can bring coal from the Sakos field. This compliment of energy from the Sako field could be an acceptable solution for the province of Toliary. Use of this coal will also counter the intensive local deforestation.

title: Karst terminology in the open pit mining
authors: Nieć M.; Uberman R.
abstract: Barren karst filling deposits encountered in open pits of carbonate and gypsum rock deposits are commonly, but uncorrectly classified as waste or deposit losts. They should be considered as overburden and classified as external or true overburden in the case of the rock overlaying the deposit, and internal overburden in the case of selectively mined barren interlayers or karst filling rocks within the deposit. The mode of karst occurrence within the Borkow-Chwalowice gypsum deposit and its impact on mining was presented (Miocene, south of the Holy Cross Mts.

title: Underground gold ore mining in Nevada
source: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
authors: Helms W.
abstract: In 1996 about 7 Mio oz (216 t) gold have been produced in Nevada from 34 mining operations. 14 underground mines were producing in 1997 with increasing production from underground operations. These mines are developed for extracting reserves below open pits resp. in depths, which are not economic for open pit mining. Access is in most cases by adits and ramps (often from pits), and only for depths of more than about 300 m by shafts. Mines are designed for trackless operation. Drifting is done with electrohydraulic jumbos, LHD units and dumpers. For support mostly split-set rock bolts, rebars and shotcrete are used. Main mining methods are open stoping (from sublevels) with backfill, drift-and-fill and underhand-cut-and-fill mining. Cemented rockfill is used to a large amount, so far hydraulic fill and pump/paste fill have not been tested. The fill is prepared from crushed rock and cement/fly ash in mixing stations located on surface or underground. It is transported with dumpers into the slopes and pushed tight to the roof with so-called jammers. Despite of skip-hoisting in shafts, ore is transported to surface by dumpers and transferred to central mills with large dump trucks.

title: Design and selection criteria of surface continuous miners for open pit mining, using Turkish coal mine as example
source: Prace Naukowe Instytutu Gornictwa Politechniki Wroclawskiej
authors: Bilgin N.; Balci C.; Acaroǧlu O.; Tunçdemir H.; Eskikaya S.
abstract: The use of surface continuous miners enables the effective design of selected mining operations. Since the cutting depth of operational drums can be changed, it is possible to mine seams with different characteristics, i.e. different calorific values, ash content etc. The size of the material cut and the dust generated during excavation are sometimes very important factors in selecting the right type of an excavating machine and the type of a mining operation. This paper, which is a result of a research project sponsored by NATO Science for Stability Programme (TU-Excavation Project), discusses the main design parameters of cutting experiments carried out on coal samples taken from Mil-Ten Coal Company. The physical and mechanical characteristics of the coal samples were first determined and then the samples were subjected to cutting tests in an excavation laboratory. The cutting depth and spacing of cutting tools were changed and the tool forces in three directions and specific energy values were measured using a shaping machine, a force dynamometer and an advance data acquisition system. Finally, the cut material was subjected to a sieve analysis and the results were analysed to see if a surface continuos miner could be used in a coal mine situated in the Istanbul area.

title: Sampling density and grade control
authors: Marcotte D.; Groleau P.; OTavchandjian
abstract: In open pit mining, each small mining unit (SMU) is selected for mill processing based on an estimate of its true grade. The estimation is usually done using analyses of cuttings from blast holes within that SMU. One common estimator used for selection is the arithmetic average of within-SMU samples. This estimator is conditionally biased. The effect of a conditional bias is to overestimate the profit really recovered from the deposit. For this reason, a conditionally unbiased estimator is preferable. Increasing the number of samples generally improves the accuracy of the estimation (and diminishes the conditional bias, if present, of most estimators). However, there exists a practical limit where an additional sample does not improve the estimation sufficiently to cover the expense of making the analysis. This limit is specific to each deposit and depends on geostatistical parameters, economic factors, and mining parameters. This study examines how the number of samples affects the recovered reserves and the resulting profit. Also, the effects on optimal profit of varying the different factors are examined. Globally, the number of samples required increases with the selectivity of the operation. For a given ore deposit, the greater the number of SMUs selected for processing, the fewer samples are required and vice-versa.

title: Groundwater monitoring and isotope investigation of contaminated wastewater from an open pit mining lake
authors: Eccarius B.
keywords: Contamination | Germany | Groundwater monitoring | Hydrogeology | Isotope | Mining
abstract: In an open pit mining lake in the Central-Gennan lignite district, untreated pyrolysis water from lignite smouldery was disposed of for >15 years. The water is highly contaminated with phenols, ammonium, and polyaromatic hydrocarbon, resulting in an extremely high dissolved organic carbon content. Several aquifers are in danger of being polluted by leaking wastewater. Since 1993, the water in up to 24 wells around the lake in different Quaternary and Tertiary aquifers was monitored two to six times per year for organic and inorganic pollutants. Isotope data (deuterium, oxygen, tritium, nitrogen) and hydrochemical investigations were used to assess the influence of lake water on groundwater. Data gathered to date shows <5% of contaminated lake water in the downstream groundwater. Nevertheless, this leakage water has a sustainable influence on the groundwater quality at least locally. Furthermore, isotope data suggest lower flow velocities within the underlying aquifer than was expected. © 2008, AAPG/DEG.

title: Spatial diagnosis of site properties for recultivated soils using bioindication and airborne remote sensing
authors: Selige T.
keywords: Bioindication | Image processing | Land evaluation | Open pit recultivation | Optical airborne scanner | Soil-plant system | Subclass classification
abstract: A procedure has been developed to evaluate soils on arable land over large scale and extended areas. The suitability of optical airborne scanner data to detect quantitatively different crop stand conditions, using image processing and transfer functions has been tested. By investigating soil properties and plant parameters, a bioindicative causal model of the soil-plant system has been developed. This model can be used to infer soil properties, by diagnosing crop stand conditions, using remotely sensed imagery. Parameters of remotely sensed crop stand conditions for sugar beet fields, have been correlated with soil properties, to facilitate the analysis of the major cause-effect relationships in the soil-plant system. The principle of bioindication has been used to develop transfer functions, to categorise soil properties from remotely sensed airborne scanner imagery. The author has assessed the suitability of soils for crop yield production and the amelioration feasibility. The recultivated soils of the brown coal open pit mining area near Cologne, have been evaluated focusing on water storage capacity, biomass and yield potential. For the purpose of this research, the crop stand sugar beet has been used as this has been found to be a sensitive bioindicator for the aforementioned parameters.

title: The innovation for steep incline and vertical conveying in the bulk material handling industry
authors: Paelke J.
abstract: As previously reported in bulk solids handling [1] the most recent innovation in the field of continuous vertical conveying in the bulk material handling industry is the POCKETLIFT®-system. This article describes the function and construction of the POCKETLIFT®-technology of the so called S-shape-system for shaft-conveying in the underground mining and tunneling industry, the inner conveyor-system for all types of bulk material in the mineral processing industry, the inner-conveyor concept installed in a mobile continuous ship unloader, as well as the pylon system for quarries and open pit mining.

title: Metasediment-hosted tin mineralization in the Indian Queens area, mid-Cornwall
authors: Camm G.; Dominy S.
abstract: Tin mining in the Indian Queens area was initially based on placer deposits around Goss Moor and Gaverigan and later from shallow underground workings (Figures 1 and 2: Dines, 1956; Camm and Hosking, 1985). Historical records (Boase, 1832; Henwood, 1843; LeNeve Foster, 1876) indicate that the metasediment-hosted hardrock deposits had an unusual character, not being of the classical vein-type. Geochemical soil sampling, float mapping and soil microscopy were undertaken in the 1980s and identified a number of Sn anomalies striking east-west and north-south (Camm, 1982-1984). The soil sampling was followed up by trenching and diamond drilling at Gaverigan [SW 930-590] and Treliver [SW 903 605]. Targets sought were those suitable for open pit mining with a potential of 4-7 million tonnes at 0.3-0.4% Sn. The results of this activity demonstrated that the metasediment-hosted tin mineralization was unusual and probably associated with hydrothermal metatourmalinite breccia bodies and tourmaline sheeted vein systems. This contribution presents a preliminary report on these studies and describes the styles of tin mineralization encountered.

title: The environmental impact of the Rosia Poieni Quarry, Romania - landscape changes and rehabilitation premises
source: Engineering Geology and the Environment Proc Symposium Athens 1997 Vol 3
authors: Mihai M.; Martac E.; Gabrion F.
abstract: With the expansion of copper and coal operations, open pit mining in Romania increases in importance and requires harmonisation of the quarry design and environmental impact analysis in order to establish appropriate incentive schemes and to promote better management. The design and development of the quarry site, the complex effects on the environments, and rehabilitation feasibility are illustrated by the analysis of the impact on the mountainous landscape generated by the huge quarry of Rosia Poieni and its adjacent works.

title: Recording on degradation of living environment caused by open pit mining
source: Engineering Geology and the Environment Proc Symposium Athens 1997 Vol 3
authors: Krstovic S.; Dimitrijevic S.
matched_open_pit_phrases: open pit mine; open pit mining
abstract: Mineral exploitation has proved to have adverse influence on the living environment. One of the greatest injuries caused by mineral exploitation is degradation of the living environment. This paper points to the necessity of record keeping on degradation of the living and proper environment caused by open pit mining. Along the border area of the open pit mine a series of harmful occurrences has been noticed (degradation of surfaces under crops, damage of residential and other facilities, occurrences of land slides etc. The character of damage depends on its very location, namely on its distance from the open pit mine (noise, pollution of both surface and groundwaters, change in groundwaters flow, aero-pollution, seismic processes etc.). Having this in mind, the eco system as a natural and antrophological environment would be registered within the record-keeping on damages caused by mining exploitation, as the same could be reduced to minimum.

title: State of miners’ health in germany
authors: Piekarski C.; Seyl G.; Bardeleben J.
abstract: Underground mining has a long tradition in Germany. While the mineral royalty created the basis for government mining inspectorates in the Middle Ages, the medical care of the miners and their families is also documented as early as 1225 in the Iglau Mining Act. In the last 20 to 30 years, iron ore mining has stopped in western Germany, only hard coal, salt, potassium, and clay are still mined underground, in addition to some isolated mining of rare minerals. The main activity consists of hard coal mining, with 100,000 miners underground in the Saar and Ruhr coalfields. In eastern Germany, uranium mining employed approximately 400,000 to 600,000 miners between 1945 and These mines are no longer active, but the high incidence of lung cancer in this mining population calls for specific medical supervision and care. The former copper mines of the Mansfield area in eastern Germany have created similar health problems for the miners involved. The medical care of all German miners is regulated by the Miners’ Health Protection Act of 1992 (Gesundheitsschutz-Bergverordnung), which covers all branches of underground and open pit mining. This article explains the health care procedures, as well as the legal basis and the exposure-related job rotation system of the underground mines under the supervision of the mine inspectorates. An overview of typical occupational diseases and die development of accidents in the mining industry in Germany is presented, as well as a short description of the handling of occupational diseases in eastern German mines after die unification. © 1997, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

title: Application of phase selective and sequential extraction methodologies in surficial geochemistry
source: Bulletin of the Geological Survey of Canada
authors: Kaszycki C.
abstract: Phase selective and sequential extraction techniques have been used to identify the residence sites of metals in a variety of surficial materials and to characterize different types of surficial geochemical anomalies. Based on analysis of C-horizon till, B-horizon till, and humus samples collected at each of approximately 65 sites in the Chisel Lake area, three different types of geochemical anomalies have been characterized. Firstly, mineralogenic anomalies, created by glacial erosion and transport are typified by uniformly high concentrations of Zn, Cu, Fe, and Mn in all crystalline mineral phases of the B- and C-horizon tills, except exchangeable metals and carbonate. Secondly, hydromorphic/biogeochemical anomalies are characterized by elevated concentrations of Zn, Cu, Fe, and Mn within the exchangeable metal and Fe/Mn hydrous oxide phases of B-horizon till and "insoluble organic" residue of humus. These metals are also highly concentrated within the soluble organic phase of humus. Thirdly, surface contamination is reflected in anomalous concentrations of Zn in the sulphide phase within the insoluble organic residue of humus. The presence of sulphide within this phase suggests airborne contamination related to mine dust from tailings and open pit mining operations.

title: Use of an in-the-wall ramp for open pit mining at Three Mile Hill
source: Diversity the Key to Prosperity Proc Conference Perth 1996
authors: Morris F.
abstract: This paper details successful implementation of a revolutionary pit access system involving excavation of an 'in-the-wall' ramp at Three Mile Hill open pit operated by Gold Mines of Coolgardie, Western Australia. Three Mile Hill is a medium-size, open pit, gold operation typified by hard, competent, fresh rock conditions from near surface. The project involved construction of a haulage tunnel or decline access located in the wall of an open pit in place of a conventional pit access ramp. Works undertaken as discussed herein included excavation, support, ventilation, dewatering, services installation, commissioning and monitoring. The paper deals with the successful implementation and operation of the in-the-wall ramp haulage as well as an economic evaluation that is aimed at drawing some general conclusions on favourable conditions for implementation in other mining scenarios.

title: An overview of surface mining in India
source: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
authors: Singh V.; Dhar B.
abstract: In the last two decades, surface mining has witnessed significant expansion. Currently, it contributes for more than 70% of the mineral production volume. A number of large and deep open pit mines have come up which are highly capital-intensive. All efforts should be made to increase the productivity by economies of scale, equipment utilisation, optimum slope design and by the adoption of suitable reclamation techniques to avoid environmental degradation. The paper discusses the present scenario in open pit mining and also suggests the ways and means to improve the productivity in the present liberalization period.

title: Selection of mining systems for large open pits
authors: Schroeder D.; Schwier U.
abstract: A comparison between continuous and discontinuous systems in open pit mines is presented. Various considerations are cited which can serve as indications for outcomes of detailed feasibility studies. General tendencies for all open pit mining projects can be derived from calculations for capacities of more than 2000 t/h and/or transport distances of more than 3000 m. The continuously operating system proved to be more economical in the long term.

title: Global Positioning Satellite (GPS) systems in open pit mining
source: Prace Naukowe Instytutu Gornictwa Politechniki Wroclawskiej
authors: Szymanski J.; Planeta S.; Partika J.; Karami A.
abstract: The Global Positioning System represents the most significant advancement in mining technology this decade. Not many people recognize its full potential, but it will be a main component in revolutionizing the way traditional open-pit mining operations function. Although GPS technology is not new, its application to mining has been limited due to a lack of centimeter precision and a high speed location determination. With the implementation of more advanced monitoring, control and locating systems in surface mines, there is an ever increasing need for their mine-wide integration towards achieving overall optimization. Presently, specialized companies are developing the basis for a comprehensive real-time monitoring, control and information system called the Total Mining System or TMS. The TMS system is being designed to address both current and future needs of open-pit mines towards improving productivity and minimizing costs, through better two-way information flow between each component in the operation. At a basic level, feedback from equipment and process monitoring will enable decision-making to be based on quantitative, on-demand information, thus permitting proactive rather than reactive planning. Dynamic planning would be a valuable tool as market conditions fluctuate, equipment fleets age and variations in the grade, quality, geometry and hardness of the mined material all contribute to either changing production targets or levels of achievable performance.

title: A simulation analysis model of the ore truck haulage system in open pit mining
source: Prace Naukowe Instytutu Gornictwa Politechniki Wroclawskiej
authors: Karami A.; Szymanski J.; Planeta S.
abstract: A SLAM II computer model was developed to simulate the open pit truck transportation system. The simulation model is capable of realistically predicting the operating performance of the complex mining and providing a valuable aid in the development and understanding of the behavior of the total system, and in the evaluation of alternative configurations and operating strategies. When such a tool was used in conjunction with bench marking, drivers of a system, that lead to superior performance were easily determined. Transportation process included in the model consisted of eight 50 tonne trucks which were assigned to each of the three shovels. The loaded trucks travel to a single crusher where they unload and travel back to the shovels, according with the complex allocation rules completing the system. The results from the study show that computer simulation is an excellent tool for evaluating various transportation system configurations, and for gaining a better understanding of the system's performance.

title: A scheduling algorithm for open pit mines
authors: Tolwtnski B.; Underwood R.
abstract: An open pit (opencast) mine can be described by a three-dimensional array of blocks, each of which is assigned a number of values defining its characteristics. Scheduling an open pit consists in finding a sequence in which the blocks should be removed from the mine in order to maximize the total discounted profit from the mine subject to a variety of technical and economic constraints. This paper proposes to model the mine-scheduling problem as one of sequential optimization, and develops an algorithm for its solution. To overcome the difficulty caused by an extremely large number of states in the problem at hand, we consider a technique which is related to dynamic programming but avoids the complete enumeration of the state space. Our algorithm is a combination of this technique with powerful heuristics derived from the specific properties of open pit mining. © 1996 Oxford University Press 1996.
