abstract: Conversion from trucks to conveyor belts is a possibility to reduce production costs. In two projects, coal is conventionally loaded for truck transportation to transfer points at the stopes where it is belt-conveyed to dumps. Caterpillar-mounted crushers with prescreening units and mobile conveyor belts follow extraction from stope to stope. The conveyor belts are suitable for coarse and abrasive material.

title: SANDWICH BELT HIGH ANGLE CONVEYORS - APPLICATIONS IN OPEN PIT MINING.
authors: Dos Santos J.
abstract: High angle conveyor (HAC) systems in open pit mining offer many advantages over the traditional, truck only, haulage systems. The present paper introduces the Continental Conveyor sandwich belt HAC as the vital link to optimization of in-pit conveying systems. Discussion continues with the HAC systems to suit the various open pit mining operations and the corresponding characteristics of the system components, particularly the high angle conveyor.

title: CHALLENGING DREDGE MINING PROJECT UNDERWAY IN THOMPSON, CANADA.
authors: Anon
abstract: The purpose of this project is to expose an orebody for Inco's open pit mining scheduled to go into production in early 1986. Thompson Open Pit is Inco Limited's largest mining development project currently underway at any of its worldwide locations. The project involves mining a portion of the Thompson orebody from the surface at a location near the company's processing complex at Thompson.

title: HYDROLOGIC SITE SELECTION FOR MINING OF DEEP BASIN LIGNITE IN TEXAS.
source: Technical Report University of Texas at Austin Center for Research in Water Resources
authors: Charbeneau R.; Wright S.; Shackelford C.; Talley A.; Yeh H.
matched_open_pit_phrases: open pit mine; open pit mining
abstract: Texas lignite will be the fuel preferred by many of the state's utilities and industries. Near surface lignite reserves are adequate to meet the needs of the early decades of the 21st century. Meeting the demands of the decades beyond will require the recovery of deep basin lignite or a transition to alternative energy fuels. The subject of this research is the hydrological and geomechanical feasibility and impact of open pit mining and underground coal gasification for recovery of deep basin Texas lignite. Of major concern are the quantities and uses of water from site dewatering and depressurizing operations, the stability of open pit mine slopes and how it is influenced by water, and the regional hydrologic impacts of lignite mining. Refs.

title: WEST GERMAN OPEN PIT MINING TECHNOLOGY FOR AUSTRALIAN HARD COAL MINE.
authors: Anon
abstract: The first giant bucket wheel excavator system for the Bowen Basin coalfields in Queensland (Australia) has been commissioned at the Goonyella mine owned by Central Queensland Coal Associates. The excavator has a theoretical output of 5200m**3/h (loose) and a guaranteed output of 1500m**3/h (bank). The bucket wheel has a diameter of 12. 25m with ten buckets plus ten pre-cutters, each bucket having a nominal capacity of 1. 8m**3.

title: USE OF AIRCRAFT IMAGERY IN EVALUATING GROUND STABILITY AT OPEN PIT URANIUM MINES IN GAS HILLS, WYOMING.
source: Informational Report U S Department of Labor Mine Safety and Health Administration
authors: Stahl R.
abstract: This report presents an approach used by Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) and mine operators to evaluate ground stability in open pit mining operations in the Gas Hills, Wyoming. The approach uses aircraft imagery to identify geology features, such as fractures and faults, that can affect ground stability in surface mines. Operators in the Gas Hills are using this technology as a mine planning and design to avoid or to minimize the effects of fractures and faults on ground stability. This remote sensing tool is appealing because it is inexpensive, accurate and one that permits rapid evaluation of a mining area on a local and regional scale.

title: OPTIMIZATION OF PRODUCTIVITY OF MINING EQUIPMENT SYSTEMS.
authors: Dickerson A.W.; Shanks D.H.; Marshall G.; Williams R.; Thomas I.R.
abstract: The operation of equipment in a mine produces a complex system which requires monitoring, simulation, analysis, and reconciliation to insure optimum production. The work described in the paper represents the initial step in an overall program to enable optimization of production and equipment usage. Two areas of investigation are covered in some detail. The first concerns large haul trucks which accomplish much of the movement of minerals and wastes in many open pit mining operations. The monitoring of trucks in normal operation is described along with some of the results of such work. The second concerns draglines which are similarly important in moving overburden in many coal mines. A program of computer simulation of draglines is described.

title: DEVELOPMENT TRENDS IN THE CONSTRUCTION OF SPREADERS FOR OPENCAST MINE DUMPS: PART 1. SPREADERS IN AROUND-THE-PIT PRE-STRIPPING SYSTEMS.
authors: Bartsch D.
abstract: A survey of the current methods in excavation of overburden in open pit mining operations is given. The article highlights the output which may be achieved by one machine or system, depending upon specific conditions such as geologic or climatic constraints.

title: QUINTETTE OPERATION REQUIRES CAREFUL EQUIPMENT SELECTION.
authors: Pelley M.H.; Crichton J.; Howe R.
abstract: Over the next twenty years, the Quintette project will involve the development of the McConkey, Frame, Shikano and Babcock open pit mining areas. To facilitate the selection and sizing of the mining equipment, all waste and coal types were identified and quantified based on materials handling requirements.

title: Tar Sand Mining in Canada - a Technological Challenge.
source: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
authors: Boehm F.; Golosinski T.
abstract: The deposits consist of 180 multiplied by 10**9 m**3 bitumen in situ and cover an area of 70,000 km**2. Only 7% are classified for open pit mining. The climate with temperatures of minus 45 degree C during the winter and plus 35 degree C in summer, wind, ice and snow are a challenge for men and machine. The abrasiveness and oily characteristics of the sand cause material problems which could only be overcome through research and development programs. Two companies are presently mining in open pits. Both operators have to move high volumes of sand, bitumen and water. The mining methods are different - in one case using bucket wheel excavaters and in the other a combination of dragline and bucket wheel reclaimers. Both methods are described.

title: ENERGY CONSUMPTION IN OPEN PIT MINING.
authors: Nilsson D.; Reddy N.
abstract: This article evaluates energy consumption in overburden stripping using draglines, shovels and trucks, and scrapers in a hypothetical open pit coal mine. The dragline gives the lowest cost, at 0. 43 per ton. However, no account has been taken of capital costs, wages, etc.

title: COMBINED GEOTECHNICAL AND HYDROLOGIC STUDIES OF THE YANKEE DOODLE TAILINGS DAM.
authors: Poindexter D.; Holmes G.
abstract: The Yankee Doodle tailings dam is a massive rockfill embankment adjacent to the Berkeley Pit mine, which is one of the largest open pit mining operations in North America. The mine, tailings retention pond, processing plant, water supply system, and all appurtenant facilities necessary to produce copper concentrate at the Butte, Montana site are operated by the Anaconda Copper Company. The original structure was designed 20 years ago, and the purposes of this study were to determine present conditions within the dam, to evaluate the capacity of the hydrologic system, to investigate the seismicity of the area and determine the resistance of the dam to earthquake loadings, and to study the effects of operational techniques including continuous construction and leaching operations near to, and on, the dam. Monitoring and observation of project variables are recommended concurrent with continuing enlargement of the dam to the final design height.

title: Increase of Holding and Carrying Capacities of Cars for Open Pit Mining.
authors: Sheshko E.; Rymar' L.
abstract: The design of dump cars with the holding capacity of up to 200-250 m**3 and the carrying capacity of up to 400-500t is considered. Hopper-type cars on two-axle paired bogies, capable of withstanding loads of up to 350 kn per axle, traveling on a 4-rail track having a total width of 5620 mm, are proposed for the Ekabastuz open pit mines.

title: LARGE ROCK CONVEYING SYSTEMS AND THEIR APPLICATION IN OPEN-PIT MINES.
authors: Martin T.W.; Goris J.M.; Crocker T.J.
abstract: Two large rock conveyor concepts have been developed and a test facility investigation designed and fabricated. The USBM will test these concepts along with loading and transfer points for handling material up to 1. 5 m (4. 9 ft) in size. An evaluation of open pit mining systems using large rock conveyors documents cost savings compared to truck haulage.

title: NEW DEVELOPMENTS IN VERTICAL CONVEYING WITH SPECIAL EMPHASIS ON THE TRANSSHIPMENT OF BULK MATERIALS.
authors: Paelke J.
abstract: A new vertical conveying method based on the FLEXOWELL-technology is introduced, which lends itself to vertical and inclined bulk solids conveying in deep shafts, in open pit mining, in processing plants and blast furnace charging, in filling silos and dumps, and especially for unloading of ships.

title: Investigation of Humidity and Friability of Coals from New Kuzbas Deposits.
authors: Novitskii N.; Belosel'skii B.; Lopaeva N.; Martynova M.
abstract: Data on moisture content and friability of coals from newly discovered coal fields in the Kuzbas (Talda, Urop, Karakan, Novokazanskoye, etc. ) are presented. These fields will have to be developed in the future by the open pit mining method. Each mine will have up to 30 Mt capacity. Many coals have high moisture content and poor friability.

title: TRANSPORT WITH LARGE CONVEYORS IN SURFACE MINES.
authors: Lubrich W.
abstract: An attempt is made to differentiate between the criteria usually required for the design of conveyor systems under ordinary operating conditions and those with which open-pit planners will be increasingly concerned in the future. Based on the well-known relationship between lifting power requirements, the calculation of the power requirement for conveyor equipment is shown by calculating the local belt pull. Finally, attention is drawn to the dynamic behavior of the transport of single large lumps and the possibility of assessing the respective forces is indicated, in view of the growing importance of handling these lumps in hard rock and also in soft rock open pit mining.

title: CONTINUOUS CONVEYING IN OPEN PIT MINES.
authors: Glanz W.; Weissflog J.
abstract: Various open pit mining systems with hard rock and unconsolidated overburden are analyzed and the main differences between discontinuous, semi-continuous and fully continuous mining and transportation methods are outlined. It is demonstrated that future open pit mining systems will tend to use continuous or semi-continuous haulage and mining operations in which detailed, long-term economic and technical planning and evaluation with the help of computer programs will play a major role.

title: A New Concept for Wheel Loaders in Open Pit Mining.
authors: Gradenegger H.; Schruf H.
abstract: A new type of wheel loader is described which is distinguished by a favorable payload-to-weight ratio, low fuel consumption, high stability and low turning radius (ensuring good loading and transport performance), good driving characteristics, and driving comfort. These qualities are achieved by designing the wheel loader as a rigid frame, which also ensures low-cost construction.

title: A study of radiation parameters in an open PIT mine
authors: Leach V.A.; Lokan K.H.; Martin L.J.
matched_open_pit_phrases: open pit mine; open pit mining
abstract: Radiation parameters associated with the open pit mining of a small (10,000 tonnes), but high grade (2) uranium deposit at Nabarlek, N.T., have been investigated in detail. External radiation levels, radon emanation rates and radon daughter levels were measured systematically during the development of the mine, and are correlated with ore grade, properties of the host rock and atmospheric conditions. Significant radon daughter concentrations were observed only under stable atmospheric conditions, usually during the night and were invariably associated with thermal inversions. The mean cumulative exposure to radon daughters was estimated from the measured levels to be 0.065 Working Level Months for employees working in the pit for the entire four and a half months of mining. The mean cumulative external gamma ray exposure for the same employee group was measured using thermoluminescent dosimeters to be 2.3 mSv (230 mrem). For most other employees, however, exposures were much lower. Data on long lived radionuclides in dust and on particle size distribution are also presented. © 1982 Health Physics Society Pergamon Press Ltd.

title: Recovery of Metal Values from Low Grade Copper Sulfide Ores
authors: Wadsworth M.E.
abstract: In the United States approximately 12 percent of the new copper produced comes from dump leaching of low grade waste rock from open pit mining. While this amount of copper is significant it is unusual, even for massive dumps, for steady-state recovery rates to exceed 20 percent. Basic physical and chemical features important in leaching typical copper porphyry waste rock have been determined in laboratory studies in tests involving up to several tons of waste rock. The important findings of such tests including chemistry of extraction, laboratory modeling, energy implications, and recovery from dilute streams are presented. Special emphasis is given to important rate limiting features of waste rock leaching including the role of autotrophic bacteria in the oxidation sequence. Difficulties in scale up from the laboratory to practice are discussed. Copyright © 1981,, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

title: Tailings disposal concepts in oil sands open pit mining.
authors: Mittal H.
abstract: This paper presents a state-of-the-art description of the procedures currently used which have evolved in this industry for the design and operation of these tailings disposal schemes. Some of the innovative techniques presently being considered for further design optimizations in terms of cost effectiveness, environmental concerns and resource conservation aspects are also discussed. (from paper)

title: Practical experience with centrifugal pumps in mine dewatering application.
authors: Kosyna G.
abstract: This paper shows typical installations of dewatering pumps in underground and open pit mining and gives a brief introduction to mine dewatering problems. Environmental conditions as well as the urgency of cost reduction of mine dewatering systems impose design objectives on pumps for mine dewatering. (A)

title: LODEVE - A NEW URANIUM MINE IN FRANCE.
authors: Anon
abstract: A mine and concentrator recently constructed by Compagnie generale des matieres nucleaires (Cogema) is situated near Lodeve in Herault, where a series of uranium bearing beds was discovered in 1957. Open pit mining started in 1978. An underground mine has been developed and a concentrator will be ready to start up early in 1981.

title: Raw material extraction in open pit mining considerations of environmental compatibility
authors: Thiede H.

title: TRUCKS VERSUS HIGH-ANGLE CONVEYOR HAULAGE IN OPEN PIT MINES.
authors: Frizzell E.; Mivissen E.; Siminerio A.
abstract: Under contract with the U. S. Bureau of Mines, Dravo Corp. made a study to evaluate the technical and economic feasibility of using a high-angle conveyor system as an alternative to truck haulage in metal and non-metal open pit mining. Such a system includes an in-pit mobile crusher. In order to determine performance specifications, four copper mines, two taconite mines, two phosphate mines and one gold mine were inspected.

title: ENERGY SAVING IDEAS FOR OPEN PIT MINING.
authors: Rixen W.; Benecke K.
abstract: The use of semi-mobile crushing plants in open pit mines makes a combination of trucks and conveyors economical and energy efficient.

title: OPEN PIT MINING AT SYNCRUDE OIL SANDS PLANT.
authors: Regensburg B.
abstract: The article describes construction and operation of the Mildred Lake operation of Syncrude Canada Ltd. in Alberta.

title: OPODEPE MOLY PROSPECT: DISCOVERY AND EXPLORATION.
authors: Ordonez G.
abstract: Opodepe is located in the state of Sonora. There is preliminary evidence of molybdenum mineralization in such quantities so as to suggest a possible large scale open pit mining operation.

title: OXIDE AND SULPHIDE COPPER MINING AT TONG LU SHAN.
authors: Argall G.
abstract: 4,000 tons per day of copper ore are mined using underground and open pit mining methods. Twelve ore bodies have been identified, seven are producing, and exploration is currently underway.

title: SURFACE MINING. PART 3. QUARRYING AND GENERAL STUDIES (CITATIONS FROM THE ENGINEERING INDEX DATA BASE).
abstract: Worldwide research dealing primarily with methods, equipment, and explosives used in drilling, blasting, and open pit mining is cited. Topic areas cover air blast and ground vibration, open pit equipment selection and maintenance, slope stability, and optimization of open pit mining using computerized simulation techniques. This updated bibliography was prepared by searching the 1970-November 1979 data base of Engineering Index. It contains 219 abstracts, 40 of which are new entries to the previous edition.

title: MINING IN THE NEXT DECADE.
authors: Kostuik J.
abstract: The author identifies 13 major highlights of the industry over the last 10 years. He discusses current trends in mining techniques, open pit mining, underground mining and ocean mining.

title: IMPACT OF MINING ACTIVITIES ON WATER QUALITY IN WESTERN NORTH CAROLINA
source: Jawra Journal of the American Water Resources Association
authors: Duda A.; Penrose D.
keywords: aquatic biology | mining erosion | nonpoint source pollution | sediment transport | water quality monitoring
abstract: ABSTRACT: An intensive water quality investigation was conducted in western North Carolina to determine whether water quality problems existed from point and nonpoint source inputs of sediment from surface mining activities. Depth integrated measurements of sediment transport and biological sampling of benthic communities indicated that very serious water quality problems were caused by erosion from a concentrated area of open pit mining for mica, kaolin, and feldspar. The erosion occurred on haul roads, active mines, inactive mines, and tailings disposal piles. The need for using specific “Best Management Practices” for erosion control on the mining operation is discussed. These practices need to be implemented to restore populations of trout to the degraded reaches of the river. Additional monitoring data are presented that indicate that the biological integrity of surface waters can be preserved in the vicinity of point source mining discharges when the operators utilize proper practices in settling and neutralizing their effluent. While much has been done to abate the point source discharges, attention now needs to be focused on the nonpoint sources of sediment from mining operations. Copyright © 1980, Wiley Blackwell. All rights reserved

title: On the theoretical accuracy of photogrammetric volume determination.
source: International Archives of Photogrammetry Vol 23 Part B4 Commission IV
authors: Jacobi O.; Kubik K.; Jensen J.
abstract: Photogrammetric methods are used in volume estimations for open pit mining in the mining industry, and for volume estimation of water reservoirs in irrigation works. Height values of a set of terrain points or contour lines are determined by photogrammetric strip and block triangulation and from these the volume enclosed by the terrain surface and a reference level is estimated. There are two error sources in this volume determination, namely photogrammetric triangulation and the terrain roughness. The influence of the photogrammetric triangulation on volume estimation is studied. -from ITC Bibliography

title: LARGE-DIAMETER BLAST HOLE DRILLS.
authors: Nelmark J.
abstract: Rotary drilling has become effective as an open pit mining tool for blast holes from 6 through 17 one-half -in. diam. Rotary drills are adaptable to drill in clays, soft shales and limestone, and unconsolidated sediments. Production and cost estimates for representative coal, copper and taconite applications are given.

title: New and newsworthy. Hydraulic shovel
abstract: It is claimed that the RH300 is the biggest and most powerful hydraulic shovel in the world. It was developed by O & K to meet the demand for large capacity, high performance open pit mining machines to remove overburden and to extract underlying minerals and ores. The features of the hydraulic shovel are described. (from paper)

title: ANALYSIS OF EQUIPMENT REQUIREMENTS FOR ANTHRACITE OPEN-PIT MINING.
authors: Manula C.V.; Mohibatsela T.S.; Ramani R.V.
abstract: The Mineral Engineering Department of The Pennsylvania State University has developed a suite of computer models for anthracite open pit mining. Individual subsystems have been developed to (a) interpolate geologic field data to obtain coal tonnages, waste volumes, and strip ratios; (b) simulate equipment performance on selected pit profiles to generate data required to choose coal and waste removal equipment; and (c) evaluate selected cost factors to determine either a rate of return for a specified selling price or vice-versa. This paper describes the application of two of these subsystems, namely the Reserves Model (GEOL) and the Open Pit Materials Handlng Simulator (OPMHS), and how these may be applied for the selection of equipment for a prime anthracite mining site.

title: Increase of water temperature and its effect upon a power plant cooling pond
authors: Gerking E.
abstract: For over 20 years a lake created by open pit mining has served as a cooling water resource for the brown coal power plant at Wolfersheim in Upper Hesse and has been the recipient for the recycled heated water. Cooling towers are non-existant. The impact upon temperature dispersion, chemical balance and ecology within the lake is a substantial part of the report. Recommendations are given to adapt adequate regulations in future water management.

title: Luzenac's Talc.
authors: Py L.; Grange J.
abstract: France's Societe des Talcs de Luzenac is mining a major talc deposit in the Pyrenees at an altitude of 1800 meters. This article provides some interesting information about the company's mining operation, describing the key features of open pit mining, the aerial cableway and the ore cleaning.

title: OIL MINING, FINAL REPORT ON TASK 014, 1979.
source: Journal of the American Ceramic Society
authors: Reed W.F.
abstract: This ESCOE task report covers the production of oil by open pit mining of oil sand deposits in the United States and surface extraction of the oil. A companion area is application of the same technology to shallow oil fields in lieu of other means of enhanced oil recovery. The report surveys possible mineable domestic sites and suggests candidates for developmental projects. Possible extraction techniques including those used in Canada, solvent extraction and retorting are discussed. It is pointed out that separation of fines and recovery of solvent are the two major extraction problems. The report points out that ability to comply with environmental requirements placed on mining and process operations will be a major factor slowing development; another will be the problems in leasing Federal lands. A review of cost ranges is also presented. There is a discussion of the one United States project now in the engineering stage together with a prediction of possible future development and production levels. The report includes recommendations as to government actions to bring the technology on stream. These include tax credits and research aimed at developing relatively small (10,000 barrels-a-day or less) extraction plants to fit the U. S. sites.

title: How to protect the natural environment - possibilities and limits
source: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
authors: Zepter K.
abstract: The open pit mining of deposits undoubtedly means an encroachment on the natural environment, which, in contrary to other industrial projects, does not permit to turn to other locations for reasons of environmental conservation. In view of this the enterprises do their utmost to minimize the environmental effects of quarrying and processing of raw materials. Examples are provided to show, that with the planning of mining, after the last exploitation of a deposit, preparatory steps are to be taken in order to achieve subsequent use of the location.

title: ASPECTS OF DEVELOPMENTS OF THE COAL INDUSTRY IN THE SINGLETON-MUSWELLBROOK AREA, NEW SOUTH WALES.
authors: Lauder R.
abstract: Coal resources of 45 thousand million tonnes of which 15 thousand million tonnes lie at a depth of less than 200 m have been estimated. The area is destined to become the largest coal producing area in New South Wales. Coal is being won by strip mining, open pit mining and by underground means. The techniques involved are described. Production of both coking coal and steaming coal is expected to rise within the next 25 years.

title: SYNCRUDE BEATS TAR SANDS, COLD WITH MODIFIED EQUIPMENT.
authors: Watson L.
abstract: The 7000 acre mine site, located on lease NO. 17 in the Athabasca tar sands, represents the largest and most comprehensive open pit mining operation ever attempted. The mining equipment is described.

title: GIANT MINE AND MACHINERY MAKE HISTORY.
authors: Anon
abstract: In 1978, the German lignite mining company, Rheinische Braunkohlenwerke AG, (Rheinbraun), started work on what will become the world's biggest open pit mining operation near Hambach. Over the next 50 years, the company will extract 2. 5 billion tons of lignite from 300-foot-thick seams, working to a depth of 1200 feet below the surface.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF BUCKET WHEEL EXCAVATORS (BWE).
authors: Benecke K.
abstract: Nearly all excavators, such as shovels, draglines, wheel loaders, scrapers, have only one digging tool, so that all parts of a working cycle have to be performed separately and consecutively. This intermittent cycle operation distinguishes them from the bucket wheel excavator. The development of open pit mining equipment for higher capacities described here was favoured by geological conditions of West German lignite deposits. Despite its low thermal value, lignite has become the cheapest raw material for power generation.

title: OPEN PIT MINING AND MAINTENANCE AT THE CLIMAX MINE.
authors: Brown C.; Gould J.; Hoffman C.
abstract: The Climax mine is located 120 km west of Denver Colo. on the Continental Divide at Fremont Pass. Production is divided between the underground operation, providing 27,000 mtpd and the open pit, providing 16,000 mtpd. Open pit mining in the high Rockies, with a major underground mine immediately below, causes many problems that tax the ingenuity of the underground, the open pit and plant engineering staffs.

title: OFF-HIGHWAY BRAKE PERFORMANCE DIFFICULT TO PREDICT.
authors: Anon
abstract: New and more stringent codes are evolving for the braking performance of off-highway open pit mining trucks. A series of actual truck performance tests was conducted to learn whether stopping performance was predictable, to determine fade characteristics of available linings, and to compare actual with theoretical brake performance under various conditions. Tests were carried out with a 152 tonne (170 ton) WABCO Haulpak truck equipped with Rockwell Stopmaster shoe brakes. A series of stops at maximum brake operating pressures were run on level, 6%, and 10% grades, empty, half loaded, and fully loaded. Two different lining mixes were studied.

title: OPEN PIT EQUIPMENT: GIANT DOZERS, LARGEST CRAWLER MOUNTED ELECTRIC SHOVEL.
authors: Kennedy B.
abstract: Equipment developments for open pit mining in 1977 were generally aimed at improving the performance and productivily of existing equipment lines. The uncertainty of the world economy and its effect on the mining industry has evidently not provided much incentive for extensive development of new equipment. Some companies, however, did introduce new products.

title: Technological Measures for Environmental Protection in the Planning and Operation of Open Pit Mining.
authors: Lechner E.
abstract: Measures for reducing the acoustic and dust emissions from open pit mining are reviewed, as well as measures for planning stone quarries so as to cause the minimum amount of environmental damage, and measures for the reclamation of disused open fit mining areas.

title: Development of Coal Industry in Central Asia.
authors: Leleko A.
abstract: Coal deposits in Soviet Central Asia are located in the territory of three Union Republics: Uzbekistan, Kirghizia, and Tadjikistan. So far 8 coal districts have been explored, comprising 40 deposits. The total coal reserves suitable for open pit mining amount to 1. 87 billion t, including 1. 5 billion t at Angren deposit. In 1977, coal output amounted to 10. 4 Mt (including 5. 6 mt from open pit mines). output from Angren deposit is about 4. 6 Mt per annum.

title: SESSIONS PAPERS - AMERICAN MINING CONGRESS, MINING CONVENTION, 1977.
authors: Anon
abstract: Proceedings contain 70 papers which are grouped into 16 sets, each of them dealing with a specific aspect of minig or mineral processing. Main subjects covered include: Use of public lands; productivity, reclamation, slurry transportation and mechanization in coal mining; impact of environmental controls on mining; minerals availability; underground and open pit mining; education of mining engineers; undersea mineral resources; safety and health in mines; mineral processing. Selected papers are indexed separately.

title: MINING ACTIVITY IN THE WESTERN WORLD.
authors: Anon
abstract: This survey covers the Western World's major producing mines classified on an ore-production basis. Data are derived primarily from a study of 22 metals and minerals. These include iron, copper, lead, zinc, tin, bauxite, gold, diamonds, platinum, manganese, nickel, uranium, chrome, mercury, molybdenum, asbestos, boron, potash, phosphate rock, tungsten, titanium and silver. Tables A, B and C in the survey mainly relate to underground and open pit mining.

title: MATCHING LOADERS AND TRUCKS FOR OPEN PIT MINING
authors: Cummings B.
abstract: For large scale surface mining operations, a variety of excavating equipment is available for different needs. Each type has its advantages. The power shovel has long life and large capacity. The rubber-tired front end loader has mobility and high cycle rates. To get the best production from any type of equipment requires the proper matching of equipment to the mining operation. The author takes a copper mine as an example.

title: SLOPE STABILITY INVESTIGATION AT GASPE COPPER MINES.
authors: Hucka V.; Levaque J.; Allard M.
abstract: In view of the extensive open pit mining operation at Gaspe Copper Mines Limited, Murdochville, Quebec, Canada, a study of an optimum slope design was felt necessary. This paper describes the different steps of the slope stability project: origin and organization to achieve an optimum design. The various phases of the project were: survey of the ore body and topography, investigation of physico-mechanical properties of rocks, structural geological mapping, ground-water study, and detailed study of structural weaknesses. The results were subsequently used to analyse different modes of possible failure of rock mass. The information obtained is being used in redesigning the Copper Mountain pit. Refs.

title: NOVA SCOTIA PLANS BIG COAL PROGRAMS.
authors: Anon
matched_open_pit_phrases: open pit mine; open pit mining
abstract: Major developments in the Nova Scotia coal industry, including a new open pit mine in Pictou County, a series of drilling and exploration programs, and conversion of some Nova Scotia Power Corporation generating plants from oil to coal, have been announced by Premier Gerald A. Regan. The area of interest lies west of the town of Stellarton and includes seven seams of coal. A diamond drilling program carried out in co-operation with the Department of Regional Economic Expansion indicated a potential of up to 10,000,000 tons of coal accessible by open pit mining. Work will commence on engineering feasibility including detailed diamond drilling, hydrologic studies and design.

title: GLIMPSE AT OPEN PIT MINING IN 1976.
authors: Anon
abstract: The article reviews developments in costs, personnel training, equipment trends and specific activities in copper, iron ore, molybdenum, phosphate, silver, gold, and uranium.

title: ROCK MECHANICS.
authors: Ross-Brown D.
abstract: Problems in open pit mining, underground design, use of numerical methods, and rock classification, are discussed. New research methods and techniques such as a pneumatic borehole packet for falling head tests in artesian conditions, are described.

title: AMC (AMERICAN MINING CONGRESS) MINING CONVENTION, 1976.
source: AMC Am Min Congr Min Conv
authors: Anon
abstract: Proceedings contain 61 papers dealing with various issues and problems that must be solved if the U. S. mining industry is to continue to supply America's mineral and fossil fuel demands in the quantities which will be needed in the next two decades and beyond. Key topics covered include: the importance of minerals to U. S national economy; environmental controls; use of public lands; mineral processing; coal mining; communications; exploration; finance; management; underground mining; minerals availability; undersea mineral resources; open pit mining; and safety and health in the mining industry. Selected papers are indexed separately.

title: Hydraulic rock drills - their role in open pit mining.
authors: Durk R.
abstract: The author aims at outlining the present status of the hydraulic drill in the mining industry, both surface and underground. The operating principles of both the pneumatic percussion rock drill and the hydraulic rock drill are described and compared. It is considered that the advantages of the hydraulic rock drill are (i) better performance (ii) greater efficiency (iii) reduced specific energy requirements compared with the pneumatic drills (iv) reduced fuel requirements (v) less capital cost (vi) lower maintenance costs and reduced downtime (vii) better environmental conditions - reduced noise and other pollution. Hydraulic drills manufacturwd by Dresser Industries , Ingersoll-Rand , Eimco-Secoma and Atlas-Copco are described, together with performance characteristics. Applications of such hydraulic drills include road construction, open-pit mining activities (secondary blasting operations).

title: BIG HOLE BLASTHOLE AT INCO.
authors: Green G.
abstract: For nearly two decades, Inco's Ontario Division has researched methods and equipment to improve the blasthole stoping technique. The potential of larger diameter, longer holes in underground mining has been recognized since earlier experiences with large blastholes in open pit mining. ITH (in-the-hole) drilling equipment, with 4-in. hammers, was tried unsuccessfully as early as 1962. New develop; ments in drills and button bits prompted a further investigation into the possibility of using ITH drills in underground applications. As a direct result of tests, Inco's efforts were directed toward promoting and developing drills of suitable design for caging and transporting to the drill sites without dismantling. ITH big blastholes underground are now a major source of production.

title: ALASKA - MINING'S CHILLY FUTURE IN THE LAND OF THE MIDNIGHT SUN.
authors: Carter R.A.
abstract: History and present status of operations in gold and coal mines, underwater open pit mining, and gold dredging are reviewed. Exploration of titaniferrous magnetite, copper, and nickel is described, and minerals inventory growth and marketing problems are noted. Oil well exploration is surveyed.

title: REGIONAL ASPECTS AFFECT PLANNING OF SURFACE MINING OPERATIONS.
authors: Anon
abstract: Conventional stripping methods are giving way to more sophisticated operational planning as mining costs and environmental regulations continue to grow. This article reviews certain specific improved mining techniques employed by the coal industry in four distinct regions of the United States. Region I was conventional contour mining methods, haulback or lateral movement operations, mountain-top removal, longwall stripping and multi-seam mining. Region II chiefly relies on box-cut contour mining, modified block-cut and block-area mining. Region III uses modified area mining, tandem-dragline operations and bucket wheel operations, while Region IV employs area mining, open pit mining and steeply dipping multi-seams.

title: ESTIMATE OF THE ECONOMICS OF URANIUM CONCENTRATE PRODUCTION FROM LOW GRADE SOURCES.
authors: Klemenic J.
abstract: Typical costs for both open pit mining and underground mining of uranium ores for 0. 01 to 0. 10 percent of U//3O//8 content are given in numerous tables. There have been significant changes in the uranium market. In 1972, under a buyer's market, prices for even the long term were seldom above 8 per pound of U//3O//8. Now, it is a seller's market. The price has been as high as 41 per pound in 1976. Because of great interest in lower grade ores, due to higher prices, a study of typical earnings was made.

title: OPEN PIT MINING EQUIPMENT FOR VERY HIGH RATES OF PRODUCTION.
authors: Krumrey A.
abstract: The development of the bucket wheel excavators and stackers of the 240,000 bank m**3/day capacity class posed many problems. These could be solved, thanks to the experience gained in the building and operation of the former 110,000 bank m**3/day capacity class. The cranes, hoists, and component handling devices were designed to facilitate all maintenance and repair work. New approaches were also adopted in evolving the conveyor drive terminals. The new principle of transfer crawlers reduces relocation work as well as investment costs. The coal will be available at moderate cost, thus helping to stabilize West Germany's energy and raw material supplies.

title: Environmental Impact of Open Pit Mining in the Conclusions of ″Bergbau '76″.
source: Gluckauf Die Fachzeitschrift Fur Rohstoff Bergbau Und Energie
authors: Schmidt G.
abstract: Water resources protection reports from various countries and air and soil pollution control measures are discussed. A device for pyrite separation from coal shown at the Exposition is described.

title: COPPER OXIDE TO COPPER CATHODE: NEW CYPRUS JOHNSON OPERATION.
authors: Argall G.
matched_open_pit_phrases: open pit mine; open pit mining
abstract: Arizona's newest copper mine - Cyprus Johnson - is pollution free from pit to cathode copper. Cyprus Johnson has a low capital investment per ton of cathode copper, 1,140 (7,200,000 capital cost for 5,000 annual tons of copper metal). By comparison, the current capital required to bring a major porphyry copper open pit mine, flotation mill, smelter, and refinery into production is from 5,500 to 6,500 per ton of copper produced. Cyprus Johnson is mining an oxide ore body, so there is no sulphur problem. Copper metal has been produced since March 1975 by open pit mining, dump for leaching, LIX64N solvent extraction, and electrowinning. Johnson is also one of the few copper operations in the world where ore is mined and placed in leaching dumps for ultimate copper recovery by LIX-electrowinning.

title: DESIGNING 240,000 DAILY CUBIC METER MINING SYSTEMS.
authors: Anon
matched_open_pit_phrases: open pit mine; open pit mining
abstract: In the West German brown coal mining industry, developments have been characterized by the concentration of production in a limited number of large-scale open pit mines. This situation led to the development of bucket wheel excavators, belt conveyor systems and stackers of the 110,000 bank cubic meter per day capacity class. A new class of open pit mining equipment, capable of handling 240,000 bank cubic meters per day, is now required for the intended production increase at Fortuna, Garsdorf as well as for the handling of 320,000,000 bank cubic meters and tons per year from a depth of nearly 500 meters in the future Hambach open pit mine. These volumes correspond to a handling rate of 5. 3 cubic meters (bulk) per second. The main design and operating characteristics of the new generation of 240,000 daily cubic meter excavator and handling systems are described.

title: Method of Selection of an Optimal Variant of Working Particular Sectors of a Deposit.
authors: Yumatov B.P.; Bunin Z.V.; Papichev V.I.
abstract: Open pit mining of nonferrous metal deposits is sometimes carried out at particular sectors. A complex method is proposed for selecting an optimal variant of working such deposits. The method is based on investigating the conditions of the mining work and plotting special graphs that establish relations between the volumes of extraction work and the output of metal, thus enabling evaluation of the efficiency of production. The method is illustrated by the example of a mining enterprise.

title: Growing Interest in Open Pit Mining of Brown Coal in Poland.
source: Gluckauf Die Fachzeitschrift Fur Rohstoff Bergbau Und Energie
authors: Tilmann W.
abstract: In German.

title: OPEN PIT MINING.
authors: Smith F.
abstract: Among factors influencing open pit mining in 1975 were the continuing low price of copper, inflation, the energy shortage and the legalization of gold ownership in the United States. While the traditional problems of mining still must be solved, it appears one of the most serious problems facing the free enterprise system in mining is government. Countries that have traditionally had a favorable climate are rapidly changing their attitudes. In the United States various governmental agencies are managing to withdraw huge tracts of land from mining and making restrictive laws, rules and regulations so that it is difficult and in some cases prohibitive to start new ventures.

title: Problem of Priority of Introduction into Service of New Iron Ore Deposits.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Bastan P.P.; Muratov K.S.; Samsonov G.A.
abstract: The article describes how different areas of the USSR are provided with resources of iron ore. Based on an analysis of the present-day state of affairs and of the prospect of development of ferrous metallurgy, a method of economic evaluation of iron ore deposits is given. In accordance with the proposed method, an evaluation of the deposits in the Urals, Siberia and the Far East, envisaged for open pit mining, is carried out. It is concluded that the most economic would be development of mining at the Siberian deposits: Nizhne-Angarskoye, Neryudinskoye, Ishimbinskoye, Anzasskoye, and Rudnogorskoye. In the Urals, the most economic would be the development of mining at the Shikhanskoge, Malo-Kuybasskoye, Techenskoye, and Kachkanaz deposits.

title: GULF MINERALS TUNING UP NEW URANIUM OPERATION.
authors: Anon
abstract: Canada's first new uranium mine in 25 years has been completed by Gulf Minerals Canada Limited, operator, in partnership with Uranerz Canada Limited. The mine and mill are located 510 miles north of Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, three miles west of Wollaston Lake. The orebody itself is located under and south of what was Rabbit Lake. That lake has now been drained to allow open pit mining of the deposit. The mill has a rated production capacity of 4. 5 million pounds of U//3O//8 annually using the acid leach solvent extraction process.

title: COMPARATIVE ASBESTOS MINING AND PROCESSING COSTS - ALASKA VERSUS YUKON TERRITORY.
authors: Bottge R.
abstract: Hard rock mining has grown in importance in the Yukon Territory during the last 10 years while Alaskan hard rock mining has declined. One asbestos deposit in Alaska is dormant, but an asbestos deposit 55 miles to the east in the Yukon Territory is being mined by the Clinton Mine Div. , Cassiar Asbestos Corp. , Ltd. In this Bureau of Mines report, the economics of mining in the two locations were derived using the Clinton mine as a model. Both deposits were assumed to be of equal size and mined by similar methods. Conventional open pit mining and processing methods were assumed, and capital and operating costs were derived using flowsheets and standard costing methods. The estimated cost for the mine, mill, and support facilities in Alaska was about 30 percent more expensive than that in the Yukon Territory. The higher labor rates in Alaska were the primary contributor to the higher construction costs; freight rates added only slightly to the total costs. Approximately two-thirds of the additional annual costs of operating in Alaska were for wages and fringe benefits. The price required for the Alaskan asbestos fiber was 356. 65 per ton compared with 287. 44 for Yukon fiber, plus or minus 20 percent. A 12 percent discounted cash flow rate of return, 100 percent equity financing, and a rapid writeoff of assets were assumed.

title: Maps of human perturbations in the environment (Polish)
authors: Leszczycki S.
abstract: Maps of pollution levels in Poland were made in 1971. The air pollution map illustrates total pollution in terms of thousands of tons of dusts and gases per year. The map on water surface pollution charts the main annual water flow in m<sup>3</sup>/sec and categorizes pollution in 4 levels of severity. The pollution of Baltic bays and coastal waters is also shown. A third map identifies areas where the earth's surface has been deformed by open pit mining or industrial waste deposits, areas of ground water disturbance, and areas in danger of radioactive contamination. The following map illustrates the destruction of vegetation, particularly forests, in 4 levels of severity. A fifth map concerns transport noise disturbances and air pollution caused by internal combustion, steam and electrical engines. On this map are shown the most important railway lines, junctions and shunting stations, the busiest highways, the most important concentrations of motor vehicles in towns, the busiest waterways, the main sea ports and airports. A sixth map refers to the erosion of soil and the use of artificial fertilizers and pesticides. A seventh map deals with refuse dumps, municipal sewage systems and industrial wastes. The eight map classifies the standard of housing in towns. A general map of human effects on the environment was constructed by superimposing the other 8 maps.

title: Main Lines of Intensification of the Making of Large Open Pit Mining Machines.
authors: Daskovskii V.
abstract: At present, the Soviet stock of open-pit mining machinery includes rotary bucket excavators with the capacity of 5000 m**3/h and with the mass of 4850 t; walking dredgers with 100 m long jibs and with 25 m**3 buckets, with the mass of 2200 t; mechanical spades with 65 m long jibs and 35 m**3 bucket, with the mass of 2700 t; open jet excavators with 12. 5 m**3 buckets. It takes from 50 to 65 months to design and make a 2000-3000 t machine. The article considers the problem of how to speed up the designing and making of large machinery for open-pit prices in order to save costs. Examples from the assembly site at the Nikopol manganese ore mining basin are given to illustrate the problems involved.

title: DEVELOPING AND OPERATING A MAMMOTH QUARRY.
authors: Yeoman J.
abstract: The Foster Yeoman company started quarrying in Somerset back in 1922, the quarry occupying a central position in the 30-mile length of the Mendip Hills. The whole range of Mendip is from Weston-super-Mare to Frome, all Carboniferous limestone with markets then and now away to the south and south-east. The article considers the application of the concepts of open pit mining to the quarrying industry.

title: OPEN PIT MINING AND THE DREDGE.
authors: Turner T.

title: DIGGING DEEP FOR COPPER.
authors: Anon
abstract: Rio Tinto's Edward Hunt is convinced that most future mineral discoveries will be deeper than those found in the past. When open pit mining ceases in about 17 years from now, the plan is to go underground with a production rate of 50 000 t a day. Nothing like this has been attempted before in South Africa. The proposed method will be a form of sub-level open stoping with delayed pillar recovery, giving a high overall extraction. At the projected mining grade and recovery, 50 000 t a day would yield about 90 000 t of copper a year which is comparable with present production. The article is an interview.

title: AIR BLAST AND GROUND VIBRATION IN OPEN PIT MINING.
authors: Andrews A.B.
abstract: Using the basic timing guidelines for blast design given, results of this experimental work using sequential initiation to provide timing flexibility showed the following: The peak particle velocity and frequency of ground motion were unaffected by changes in timing over the range investigated. Blasts of short duration produced ground motion of shorter duration and less energy. The shorter duration of the motion reduces public annoyance. The smaller amount of seismic energy was accompanied by an increase in burden displacement. Air blast was associated with the transmission of a portion of the stress wave into the air upon reflection at the free face from the firing of the first row of holes. The absence of air blast from subsequent rows was noted. Superposition of air blast pulses can be minimized by controlling the rate of blast progression along the free face. The simultaneous firing of opening holes is to be avoided if air blast is a problem.

title: Basic Concepts of Automated Open Pit Mining System Projects.
authors: Kusnezow K.
abstract: A man-machine system aimed at higher technology and effectiveness is offered. Better projecting and calculating procedures are suggested to cut costs. Diagrams show improved methods.

title: Open Pit Method of Mining Ferruginous Quartizites in the Krivoi Rog Basin.
authors: Statkevich A.A.; Sinarenko I.A.; Solov'ev M.I.; Serbin V.I.; Alekseev F.K.; Panov V.A.; Tereshchenko A.A.; Polishchuk A.K.; Bondar' S.A.; Drizhenko A.Y.
matched_open_pit_phrases: open pit mine; open pit mining
abstract: Between 1955 and 1968 five ore-dressing combines have been built in the Krivoi Rog basin. They treat ferruginous quartzites mined from 9 large open pit mines whose projected depth reaches 300-500 m and annual capacity from 5 to 36 million t of crude ore. The annual capacity of the combines is: 135 Mt of crude ore and 60 Mt of concentrate with the iron content of 64-65%. The article gives a brief description of all the combines of the open pit mining methods, transportation, waste disposal and recultivation of the stripped soil. Plans to deepen open pit mines to 450, 500 and even 800 m are outlined. A project of construction of a super-ore-dressing combine with the capacity of 150-180 Mt of crude ore per annum with an open pit mine 900-1000 m deep is mentioned.

title: USE OF BELT CONVEYORS IN OPEN PIT MINING.
authors: St. John C.; Kronke J.
abstract: The use of belt conveyors in one of the largest stripping operations in the history of mining, at Twin Buttes near Tucson, Arizona, is described. The present alluvium handling system consists of two 60-in. belt conveyors, 2,400 and 3,000 ft. long each, designed to handle 8,000 tph. The conveyors will be extended and a new one added in 1975. This new belt is to be both shiftable and extendable. Designed with modular construction in mind, it will be extended 20 times in increments of 256 ft each and will be moved 25 times in its 10-year life span. A new 11,500 ft conveying system planned for the mine is described. There are also a few miles of conveyors handling crushed ore bearing rock.

title: OPTIMIZING OPEN PIT MINING WITH COMPUTER SIMULATION.
authors: Butler J.; Fouts R.
abstract: The Wabco simulation program is described which provides an approach to solve open pit mining production and planning problems by using the computer to simulate the thousands of events that take place simultaneously in the pit. Program inputs and outputs, such as those concerning information about shovels, trucks, dumps and crushers, haul profile, etc. and program mechanics are explained. Several examples of application are given.

title: OPEN PIT MINING.
authors: Anon
abstract: A survey is given of the developments in the field of open pit mining in 1974. The use of computers in the area of mine planning, new drilling hardware, blasting products, large-capacity tracks for haulage, tractor shovels, mining shovels and draglines is reviewed. some new projects are discussed briefly.

title: PLAN GEOMETRY AND OTHER FACTORS RELATING TO NATURAL ROCK SLOPE STABILITY APPLIED TO DESIGN OF DE BEERS MINE.
authors: Piteau D.F.
abstract: As part of a major study relating to the stability of rock slopes of De Beers Mine, a detailed investigation was made of the natural slopes of De Beers Mine and four other mines in Kimberley. Attempt was made to determine the controlling factors which either lead to or detract from the stability of the slopes, the main objective being to assess whether the natural breakback of the slopes would jeopardize the main railway line located in close proximity to the pit. Current theories of slope stability all deal with a slope as a two-dimensional problem, i. e. a slice of unit length of an infinitely long slope is considered for a condition of plane strain. In this the tacit assumption is made that the plan radii of the crest and toe of the slope are infinite. This is not the condition encountered in practice, particularly in open pit mining where these radii of curvature have important effects on the safe slope angles. To determine these and other effects a study was made of the slope breakback and other related factors in the four big holes of the diamond mines in the Kinberley area. Other forms of analyses of the basic radius of curvature and breakback data are conducted. It is shown that the major dimensions of the pipes are also important factors for the stability of these slopes. Based on simple experiments the mechanics of failure are determined and also factors such as comparison of effects of plan radius of curvature on the upper and lower parts of the slopes and possible effects of regional stress are assessed.

title: ROCK MECHANICS IN OPEN PIT MINING.
authors: Brawner C.O.
abstract: The majority of information contained in past International Rock Mechanics Conferences has dealt with rock mechanics as applied in the field of civil engineering. In reality, more than 80 percent of all rock excavated throughout the world is associated with mining projects. During the past decade the mining industry has recognized the economic and safety implications of the application of rock mechanics to mining. As a result, numerous advances have been developed and implemented in data collection, property determination, theoretical analysis and field instrumentation. This supplementary report outlines briefly the general approach now being taken to assess the stability of rock slopes on mining projects. The most important factors which influence stability are the presence, orientation and shear strength of structural geologic discontinuities, groundwater pressures and influence of seismic acceleration forces due to frequent blasting. To illustrate the importance of typical variables, five case examples are described. They include two coal mines, one uranium mine, one copper mine and one asbestos mine. On the latter project a slide involving 35,000,000 tons was stabilized.

title: SCALE DEPOSITS UPSET BALL MILL WATER SERVICE.
authors: Anon
abstract: Heavy scale deposits within control valves at one of the world's largest open pit mining operations increased maintenance, and affected mill production until operations staff found an economical valve solution. The scaling on the discharge end of the ball mills caused critical production interruptions within three months of the mine's opening.

title: Experts' Evaluation of the Development of the Techniques and Technology of Iron Ore Open Pit Mining in the USSR by the Year 2000.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Shtukaturov K.; Kazantsev S.; Volegov B.
abstract: The role of experts' evaluation in compiling long-term forecasts is pointed out, the principles of composition of the questionnaries are formulated, and the mathematical tools for the treatment of answers are presented. Results of an opinion poll carried out in 1971-72 among open-pit mining and mining engineering specialists about the development of the techniques and technology of open pit iron ore mines in the USSR by the year 2000 are discussed.

title: From the Experience of Operation of the Sokolovsko-Sarbayskiy Ore-Dressing Combine.
authors: Pap
abstract: A series of 18 articles published on the occasion of the 20th anniversary of the iron-ore dressing combine describes the achievements of the combine over the two decades, the growth of output, open pit mining works, the technical progress, the mining and ore separating machinery, mechanization of auxiliary works, automation and centralized traffic control, ore separation, economics and organization of production, and introduction of automatic control systems. The output of the combine is 28 million t of crude ore per annum and the output of marketable ore is 15 million t, i. e. over 7% of its total output in the USSR. The ore is mined by open pit methods from the depth of between 35 and 120 m. The total ore resources are estimated at 2 billion t. The newly built mining city of Rudnyy has 100,000 inhabitants.

title: Future of Mining.
authors: Mel'nikov N.V.
abstract: Future developments in ore mining methods in the USSR are considered and various predictions are made. Increases in the share of open pit mining, and in the capacities of coal mines to 1. 5-2. 0 million t, and of iron ore mines to 8-10 million t and more, are envisaged. Increase of the depth of underground iron ore mines to 1500 m and of open pit mines to 500-600 m, and problems of ventilation, safety, transportation are outlined. Mining technology and mining machinery, application of geotechnological methods, offshore mining, waste disposal, recultivation of soils, etc. are considered and technological forecasts are made.

title: LU-CJA-TO COAL MINE.
authors: Lezon M.
abstract: With an annual output estimated at some 400 million mtons, the Chinese People's Republic is the world's third largest producer of coal after the U. S. S. R. and the U. S. A. The country's reserves are believed to total well over 1 multiplied by 10**1**2 mtons and the country is more reliant on coal as its major fuel source than perhaps any other. Most of the known deposits are comparatively close to surface, and both underground and open pit mining methods are used, but on balance, the mines tend to be smaller and less technologically advanced than their Western counterparts. In many of the underground properties there is little mechanization, but some of the larger underground units are hydraulic method, both in actual mining by water jet and in underground transportation of coal.

title: HAMERSLEY IRON.
authors: Anon
abstract: Hamersly is currently Australia's largest iron ore producer with operations at Mt. Tom Price and Paraburdoo in the Pilbara area of Western Australia. Within 10 years from the initial discovery of the deposit, the company's iron ore output capacity had reached 22. 5 million ton/year and with the opening of the new Paraburdoo deposit, capacity is scheduled for 40 million ton/year by end-1974. A monographic description discusses: the geology of the deposit; open pit mining operations; haulage; comminution at Mt. Tom Price and Paraburdoo; pelletizing; transportation of ore by a 244 m long railway to Port Dampier; port facilities and further expansion program.

title: Some Experience of the Operation of the Kachkanarskiy Ore-Dressing Combine.
authors: Rev
abstract: Under the above general title, a series of 13 articles by many authors present a review of various aspects of the operation of the Kachkanarskiy ore-mining and ore-dressing combine in the Middle Urals, which was put into operation in 1964. Design capacity of the combine was 33 million t of raw ore, 5. 8 million t of the concentrate, 2. 7 million t of agglomerate, 2. 8 million t of pellets, and it was achieved approximately in 1973. A second combine for 45 million t of raw ore is planned, and the existing combine is to be expanded to handle 40 million t of raw ore. The raw material base of the combine, the development of open pit mining, explosion work, equipment of the combine, maintenance of diesel-electric locomotives, power supply, control and automation of technological processes, improvement of separation technology, production of the agglomerate and pellets, scientific organization of labor, chemical analysis of ores, etc, are dealt with in different articles.

title: Materials Handling at the Leipzig Spring Fair 1973.
authors: Engels H.
abstract: Review and description of some of the recent eshibited machinery in the field of materials handling. Considered are: equipment for open pit mining, container reloading equipment, and cranes.

title: COMPUTER SIMULATION OF TRACTOR-SCRAPER OPERATIONS IN WASTE STRIPPING.
authors: Thieme M.; Spokes E.
abstract: A simulation model developed to analyze scraper-pusher utilization in open pit mining systems is described. The mining simulator discussed was developed as a tool to aid management in evaluating alternative open pit haulage schemes and to reduce the risk involved in the selection of equipment.

title: PHOSPHATE IN THE KOLA PENINSULA, USSR.
authors: Woodrooffe H.
abstract: Physical conditions of underground and open pit mining and flotation concentration from large reserves on Russia's Kola Peninsula north of the Arctic Circle are described. Current production capacity and future expansion figures are given.

title: Automatic voltage regulation in mine networks
source: Izv Vyssh Ucheb Zaved Gorn Zh
authors: KOMLEV VP
abstract: The use of thyristors for voltage regulation in open pit mining network is demonstrated. The booster substation circuits are described.

title: Stability in open pit mining. Proceedings of the 1st International Conference, Vancouver, BC, Nov 23- 25 1970
source: Soc of Mining Eng of AIME
authors: BRAWNER ED CO; MILLIGAN ED V
abstract: Proceedings contains 11 papers, minutes of a panel discussion, and a conference summary. Covered in papers topics were- slope stability in the economics, design, and operation of surface mines; geologic factors controling slope stability; influence of rock structure, groundwater, blasting and earthquakes on stability of rock slopes; method of analysis of rock slopes and field instrumentation; design and construction of tailings dams; and case studies of stability in mining projects. Individual papers are provided with bibliographic references.

title: Contribution to the general theory of open pit mining parameters
source: Izv Vyssh Ucheb Zaved Gorn Zh
authors: ONISHCHENKO YUA
abstract: Analysis of geophysical, and of other factors to be taken into consideration for planing operations in mining, is presented.

title: How a computer was used in evaluating the Vuonos nickel deposit in Finland
authors: PELTOLA E; KUPIAS P; VOUTILAINEN P
abstract: Outokumpu Oy, Finland's largest mining company is developing an open pit adjacent to the old Outokumpu Mine, Vuonos deposit, containing only 0. 20% sulfide nickel. Vuonos will be the largest mine in the country, designed to produce annually 300,000 tonnes of Cu- , and 1,500,000 tonnes of Ni ores. Paper describes how a computer program was used to evaluate the marginal ore body and plan open pit mining.

title: Ptolemais, Greece's largest lignite mine trebles production
authors: KULLIK E; THORMANN D
abstract: Open pit mining operation, located in northern Greece at the altitude of 2200 ft above sea level exploits a lignite seam of a thickness varying between 160 and 210 ft. Total reserves are estimated to amount to 350 million tonnes. Two grades of lignite are selectively mined- '%'A'%' suitable for briquetting with maximum 9% ash; and '%'B'%' with up to 13% ash, used for generation of electric power. In order to increase annual production of 2 million tonnes threefold, large bucket wheel excavators and steel cable reinforced, rubber belt conveying system of total length exceeding 10 mi. have been installed.

title: Geology and mining operations at Palabora Mining Company Limited, Phalaborwa, N- E Transvaal
source: Journal of the South African Institute of Mining and Metallurgy
authors: KUSCHKE OH; TONKING MJH
abstract: A description is given of the general geology, structure and minerals of economic significance of the Loolekop copper orebody at Phalaborwa. The open pit mining method is described with details of drilling, blasting loading, hauling and primary crushing operations. A brief description is given of mine planning and its relationship to the control of the mining operation.

title: Statistical methods of determining calculated loads of industrial plants, (Metody statystyczne wyznaczania obciazen obliczeniowych w zakladach przemyslowych)
authors: CZAJKOWSKI Z
abstract: Methods are discussed of determining calculated (peak) loads in industrial plants of open pit mining. Numerical values of calculation coefficients for various electric loads in brown coal strip mines are given.

title: Underground Coal mining, 1970
authors: ANON
abstract: Review of mining and minerals processing industries encompasses 21 articles covering- impact of Federal Coal Mine Health and Safety Acto of 1969 on underground coal mining; developments in coal preparation; underground mining; open pit mining; mineral exploration; bituminous coal economics; world metallurgical coal in 1970's; European coal report; the economic future of western fossil fuel; uranium requirements for light water reactors; phosphate- emergin trends; new markets for tomorrow's sulfur; copper- vital metal in an era of change; aluminum; outlook for world commerce in nonferrous metals; outlook for silver; strategic minerals of the future; ferroalloys- a billion dollar industry; and Japanese search for raw materials.

title: ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT FOR THE BELT CONVEYOR SYSTEMS USED IN THE PTOLEMAIS (GREECE) OPEN-CAST MINING OPERATIONS, (ELEKTRISCHE AUSRUESTUNG DER FOERDERBANDANLAGEN IM GRIECHISCHEN TAGEBAU PTOLEMAIS
authors: BOMMER R; MUELLER RR
abstract: At this open pit mining site using trains, five bucketwheel excavators and one stacker are supplied with power through a 3km overhead line. Excavators and stackers had to be converted from train to conveyor systems without major hold-ups. The equipment had to be interlocked with the belt conveyor system while follower control gear and safety devices were incorporated. Power supply to the drives was arranged through a central main switch station and kiosk type steel-clad stations.

title: GROUND PREPARATION BY RIPPING IN OPEN PIT MINING
authors: ATKINSON T
abstract: The advent of relatively inexpensive explosives such as ANFO and metallized slurries have resulted in considerable reductions in blasting costs so that some of the traditional roles of ripping are being challenged. S%At the same time more powerful and efficient machines are being developed and experience gained in ripping techniques so that continuous appraisal of ripping is appropriate. Ripper types and selection are analyzed. Rock qualification from the viewpoint of rippability and fracture index is discussed. Comparison of costs between ripping and blasting is discussed.

title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF KATANGA COPPER. GECOMIN'S OPEN PIT MINES ACHIEVE RECORD PRODUCTION
authors: WYLLIE RJM
abstract: General Congolaise des Minerais (Gecomin), nationalized successor of the former Union Miniere du Haut Kagangta, is responsible for the entire output of copper that with the 1969 production of 400,000 plus reached an all-time record. The individual five mining properties, the open pit mining methods and heavy equipment used are described. Trends of further development of production are discussed.

title: The pine point lead-zinc deposits, N.W.T., Canada introduction and paleocology of the presqu'ile reef
authors: Jackson S.; Folinsbe R.
abstract: The zinc-lead deposits at Pine Point, N.W.T., comprise known ore reserves of 42.5 million tons averaging 7% Zn and 2.6% Pb in a 20 by 4 mile belt of barrier carbonate of Middle Devonian age, now exposed or at shallow depths amenable to open pit mining. Fore reef, reef and back reef facies in the Middle Devonian Pine Point, Presqu'ile and Sulphur Point Formations are recognizable in an elongate platform bounded on the north by the Mackenzie Shale basin and on the south by the Elk Point evaporites. During the development of this carbonate buildup the barrier platform was subject to periodic exposure, followed by renewed reef growth; ultimately late Middle Devonian and Upper Devonian transgressions of the sea caused the barrier buildup to be succeeded by carbonates of a more open marine character. The ore bodies that form an integral part of the upper Pine Point and the Presqu'ile formations are elongate lens shaped bodies ranging from a few hundred thousand to 10 million tons in size. Margins are sharp, most of the ore was deposited in open cavities and vugs. Colloform and crystalline sphalerite and galena are the only ore minerals; abundant marcasite, pyrite, calcite and dolomite comprise the gangue. Evaporites, deposited in a supratidal (Sabkha) environment, appear to have played a major role in the development of porosity that governed later dolomitization and ore emplacement. © 1969 Society of Economic Geologists, Inc.

title: TURKISH IRON ORE
authors: GUNEY M
abstract: S urvey of geographical location of known iron ore deposits in Turkey includes characteristic data about analysis of ore and reserves; most important deposit is that of Divrigi, located in NE province of Anatolia and containing magnetite and hematite ores of contactmetamorphic origin in mezozoic limestones, reserves of 40 to 45% Fe ore are estimated at 45 million tons; open pit mining produces about 900,000 tons/yr used by state owned Karabuk Iron and Steel Plant, located in vicinity of coal mines; trends of further expansion are indicated.

title: SOME DEVELOPMENTS IN POLISH OPEN PIT MINING
authors: ANON
matched_open_pit_phrases: open pit mine; open pit mining; opencast mining
abstract: In parallel with underground mining, during past ten yrs rapid development of opencast mining has taken place in Poland; at present nearly 200 million tons of ore and minerals are mined by opencast methods and approximately 150 million tons by underground mining; steadily increasing depth of mined mineral deposits, increasing productive capacity of single mine up to 50 million t/yr and introduction of large capacity belt conveying are main developments illustrated in case of sulfur open pit mine near Tarnobrzeg in Central Poland, producing presently 400,000 t/yr of pure S and Turow mine, near Czechoslovakia and East German borders, producing 15 million t/yr of lignite, with installed total length of belt conveyors amounting to 100 km.

title: CASE STUDIES OF SURFACE MINING. PROCEEDINGS OF II INTERNATIONAL SURFACE MINING CONFERENCE, MINNEAPOLIS, MINN, SEPT 18-20 1968
source: Am Inst of Min Met Petroleum Engrs New York Ny
authors: HARTMANED HL
abstract: Proceedings includes 21 papers discussing surface mining techniques in selected coal and lignite-, iron- , copper- , industrial minerals-, and other metallic ore mining operations; dredging techniques are also examined. Following papers presented- Australia-recent developments in surface mining; W. A. WEIMER; Garsdorf lignite strip mine-operations to unusual depths; E. H. E. GARTNER; Central Ohio Coal Company's mine expansion program; P. D. MARTINKA, C. A. KEFFLER; Captain Mine-total team effort; D. E. WALKER; Open cast coal mining in the USSR (Methods and technology); V. SOBITSKY; Thunderbird mine of Eveleth Taconite Company; R. H. HOLGERS, C. W. BAXTER, W. G. FETZER; LKAB's iron ore operations in the Svappavaara mine near the Arctic Circle in Sweden; M. MALINIEMI, L. O. PETTERSSON, H. NORDEFORS; Lac Jeannine mining operations of Quebec Cartier Mining Company; J. E. KORSKI; Open pit mining in mountainous terrain-Lamco's iron mine in Liberia; J. B. ERKKILA; Survey of current open pit practices in Florida phosphate; T. V. FALKIE; Open pit mining of Arkansas vanadium deposits; I. R. TAYLOR; Lucky Mc mine; D. C. ANDERSON; Evolution of floating dredges for mining operations; C. M. ROMANOWITZ, M. J. CRUICKSHANK; Questa Mine; R. I. WILLIAMS.

title: CLAY MINERALOGY, FABRIC, AND INDUSTRIAL USES OF SHALE OF DECORAH FORMATION, SOUTHEASTERN MINNESOTA
authors: PARHAM WE; AUSTIN GS
abstract: The Decorah shale varies both vertically and laterally in its clay mineral assemblages. It is principally an illitic shale in Minnesota, but kaolinite is approximately of equal abundance in the basal part to the southwest, reflecting nearness to the source area. Clay mineral data suggest that the Decorah shale may be satisfactory for use in ceramic products such as face brick, sewer pipe, light weight aggregate, structural tile, and drain tile. Numerous areas along the shale's outcrop belt in southeastern Minnesota would be satisfactory for open pit mining .

title: SULFUR MINING IN POLAND
authors: SINGHAL RK
abstract: Deposit, discovered in mid 1950's in Central Poland, on left bank of Vistula River extends over area of 11 sq mi and contains pure S reserves exceeding 100 million tons; S occurs in miocene limestone layer 5 to 10 m thick, covered by overburden 14 to 100 m thick; main problem facing open pit mining was purification of 2300 cu m/hr of contaminated with hydrogen sulfide, drainage water which could badly affect Vistula River vegetation; problem has been solved by aeration and recovery of elemental S from contaminated air; present production of ore, containing 21 to 24% S amount to 3 million tons per year, scheduled to reach in a few years 15 million tons per year; flowsheet of S production is included; excess of S over local consumption is exported in form of 99. 98% pure S.

title: BOUGAINVILLE COPPER WILL BE GIANT PIT IN HIGH MOUNTAIN RAIN FOREST
authors: ANON
abstract: Low grade Panguna porphyric orebody known to contain over 550x10**6 tons of ore assaying 0. 51% Cu and 0. 2 oz Au/ton is being developed by Australian mining interest for open pit mining designed to produce, beginning in 1972, 80,000 to 100,00 tpd of ore; about 13,100 ft long, 3900 ft wide and 1000 ft plus deep orebody is covered by up to 50 ft thick clayey type volcanic ash; access, heavy rainfall (up to 200 in. /yr), adequate tailing storage areas present some of many problems.

title: HOW ENGINEERING, EXPERIENCE, HIGH CAPACITY EQUIPMENT COMBINE TO MAKE ORE AT SIERRITA
authors: JANCIC T
abstract: Duval Sierrita Corp, subsidiary of Duval Corp is developing about 35 mi southwest of Tucson, Ariz, copper molybdenum ore body to be mined in open pit operation; deposit containing over 414x10//6 tons averaging 0. 35% Cu and 0. 036% Mo is covered by 634x10//6 tons of rocky overburden being removed from open pit designed with 45//0 final slopes; initial stage of development for production of 72,000 tpd requires removal of 105x10//6 tons of overburden; thereafter waste to ore ratio will gradually decline during first 10 yr of operation from 2. 25 to 0. 59; equipment required for open pit mining of 200,000 tpd ore and waste combined is listed; on straight copper basis, calculating Mo as Cu equipvalent, Cu grade of ore will average 0. 54%.

title: TRENDS IN TECHNICAL AND TECHNOLOGICAL DEVELOPMENT OF SURFACE COAL MINING IN USSR,
authors: KUSNEZOV KK
abstract: In 1966 141x10**6 tons of coal, or about 25% of total coal production, has been produced in open pit mines; total proven reserves of strippable coal in Soviet Union are estimated to amount to 140x10**9 tons; ratio of overburden in cu m to coal in tons rose from 3. 0 (1950) to 3. 75 (1965); mean production of 62 surface mines amounted in 1966 to 2. 4x10**6 tons/yr; output per man and month is given as 275. 2 tons against 40. 2 tons in underground mines; excavating equipment used in open pit mining is described.

title: MOROCCAN PHOSPHATE. UNDERGROUND AND OPEN PIT MINING, SOME ORE IS BENEFICIATED BY WASHING, DRY BEFORE SHIPPING
authors: ARGALL GO; JR
abstract: Description of Khouribga Mining Complex operated by Morocco's Office Cheriffien des Phosphates (OCP); reserves of phosphates calculated at 40x10//9 tonnes mined by mechanized open pit and underground methods of permitted OCP to become in 1967 largest exporter of phosphates in world with 9. 8-million tonnes exported; presently top bed 1. 2 to 2. 5 m thick, laying at depth of 120 ft is mined underground by continuous retreat room and apillar stoping, recovering about 80% of ore, containing about 34% P//2O//5; open pit ore is washed, all ore is dried down to about 15% of moisture; ore treatment plants are described.

title: SURFACE SUBSIDENCE WITHIN RANGE OF LIGNITE OPEN PIT MINING AS EFFECT OF WATER TABLE LOWERING,
authors: RUDOLF H
abstract: Effect has been investigated in two lignite open pits in East Germany; equations have been developed to anticipate magnitude of subsidence and actual measurements have been found to vary about 33%; it has been ascertained by regression method that proposed method to figure out in advance amount of subsidence is sufficiently accurate if geological structural data, probable drawdown of water table and soil mechanical characteristics, are available.

title: STRUCTURAL GEOLOGY AS BASIS FOR PLANNING OF OPEN PIT MINING OPERATIONS,
authors: WEBER H
abstract: Exploitation of knowledge of structural characteristics of rock masses can be used as potential contribution to decreasing cost of mining; to accomplish that purpose it appears to be necessary to- collect structural measuring data prior to beginning of mining, measuring behavior of rock masses during maining and, experimenting in situ and with models; measuring instruments are described.

title: Identification of Methane-Bearing Coal Seams in Borehole Sections of the Karaganda Basin Using Geophysical Logging Data
authors: Sergeevich P.V.; Vasilyevich G.A.; Kanatovna D.G.; Nurbol K.; Akanovna K.A.; Mukhammedrakhym R.; Hou P.
keywords: coal suites | ecology | forms of methane occurrence in coals | gas content | geomechanics | metamorphism physico-mechanical characteristics of coal and host rocks
abstract: The Karaganda coal basin is one of the most gas-bearing in the world. Its feature is that there are no large accumulations of free gas in it, while the natural gas content reaches up to 25-30 m³/t; this is confirmed by a large volume of gas sampling, gas logging data, and gas survey data in operating mines. Methane from coal seams enters the atmosphere through natural migration through overlying rocks, as well as at the places where seams outcrop under overburden and through the shafts of closed mines.
