abstract: The Yichun Ta-Nb-Li mine is situated within a small, sheetlike body of topaz-lepidolite granite which is the most fractionated phase of the Yashan batholith. Volumetrically, the most important phase in the batholith is a coarse-grained, protolithionite-muscovite granite which has a finer grained, muscovite granite margin. The protolithionite-muscovite granite is intruded by small bodies of muscovite granite which form the locus of a tungsten vein system at the Xin Fang tungsten mine. Two sheetlike bodies, a lower Li mica granite and an upper topaz-lepidolite granite intrude the upper contact between the protolithionite-muscovite granite and the host metasediments. The granites are crosscut by unmineralized porphyry dikes that are exploited as a source of kaolin. The topaz-lepidolite granite is a major, low-grade Ta-Nb-Li deposit which is exploited via open-pit mining. The mineralogy and geochemistry of the ore deposits are described. -from Authors

title: Towards the 30th anniversary of West-Siberian Iron and Steel Works
authors: Kustov B.
abstract: A review is made on development and advances of the West Siberian Iron and Steel Works since its inception. The Works pioneered in application of flame guniting for converter lining, thermal hardening of shaped sections from the rolling temperature, cast-iron melting with high-alumina and high-magnesia slags, coke production from the coal of open-pit mining. Among other things mixing ladles and blast-furnace chargers were mastered along with production of rolled metal, metal cord, alloy welding wire etc.

title: Automatic design and planning system for the open-pit mining of coal deposits
authors: Tanaino A.S.; Botvinnik A.A.; Tetenov E.V.

title: Geology and geochemistry of Summitville, Colorado: an epithermal acid sulfate deposit in a volcanic dome
authors: Gray J.; Coolbaugh M.
abstract: Geologic studies during recent open-pit mining at Summitville, Colorado, have provided new information on an epithermal acid sulfate Au-Ag-Cu deposit formed in a volcanic dome. Geologic mapping, geochemical studies of whole-rock samples from blast holes, and geologic and geochemical traverse studies refine the details of the evolution of the Summitville deposit. Six distinct events followed emplacement of the quartz latite volcanic dome and define the development of the Summitville deposit: 1) an early stage of acid sulfate alteration, 2) subsequent Cu sulfide and gold mineralization, 3) widespread hydrothermal brecciation, 4) volumetrically minor, base metal sulfide-bearing barite veining, 5) volumetrically minor, kaolinite matrix brecciation, and finally, 6) supergene oxidation. -from Authors

title: Computerized mine planning for medium-size open-pits
source: Transactions of the Institution of Mining and Metallurgy Section A Mining Technology
authors: Blackwell G.
abstract: Sequences in open-pit mining must be planned and regularly revised to incorporate changes in the variables that affect profitability. Interactive computer planning with colour graphic facilities is an effective tool for this purpose in the short and medium term. Hardware for such purposes, in the form of personal computers, is readily available, and the techniques have been shown to contribute significantly to planning effectiveness and profitability. Successful planning requires skilled personnel who are familiar with all aspects of mine operations and related matters. Their decisions can be input into expert-system databases to educate and assist less experienced personnel. Within limits fluctuations in well-defined, short-term grades can be smoothed by using linear programming to adjust the mining sequence. In the longer term the lack of sampling data precludes detailed planning, and broad adjustments to monthly or quarterly sequences are required to ensure a continuously developing, practical mine plan.

title: Computer-based optimization of open-pit mining sequences
source: Transactions of the Institution of Mining and Metallurgy Section A Mining Technology
authors: Huang S.
abstract: An interactive model and corresponding computer software for optimization of the open-pit mining sequence have been developed at the Institute of Mining Engineering, Technical University of Berlin. The model is supported by graphics software and consists of three linear programming systems and a simulation module. With this model an optimum mining sequence for a multi-level open-pit mine can be determined under a criterion selected by the planner.

title: Stratigraphic evidence of a pre-wisconsinan interglaciation in the Adirondack Mountains, New York
authors: Muller E.; Sirkin L.; Craft J.
abstract: Multiple tills separated by interbedded lake sediments were temporarily exposed during open-pit mining at Sanford Hill, near Newcomb, in the central Adirondack Mountains of northeastern New York. Radiocarbon ages of wood fragments from brown clay between two tills at that site indicate an age older than 55,000 yr B.P. A pollen profile in the brown pond clay (Tahawus clay) records a transition from initial domination by pine, spruce, and birch to an oak pollen zone. The upward disappearance of spruce and decrease of pine and birch are accompanied by diversification and increase in hardwood pollen. This assemblage includes several warm-climate hardwood species that are not represented in the postglacial flora of the region, suggesting that the biota existed during an interglacial or interstadial interval that was warmer and/or longer than postglacial time. Accordingly, the Tahawus clay is tentatively assigned to the Sangamon interglaciation, and probably to marine oxygen isotope substage 5e. Truncation of the Tahawus clay by glacial erosion may account for the absence of a Sangamon paleosol. © 1993 University of Washington.

title: Acquisition and signal processing of ground-penetrating radar for shallow exploration and open-pit mining
authors: Baker P.; Cull J.
keywords: Australia | Ground-penetrating radar | Mining | Signal processing
abstract: The Australian Mineral Industries Research Association (AMIRA) has sponsored Monash University to investigate the acquisition and signal processing of ground-penetrating radar (GPR) for shallow exploration and open-pit mining. This project had three objectives: (1) to acquire high-quality GPR data sets for shallow exploration and surface mining applications under a variety of geological conditions; (2) to develop signal-processing techniques to enhance radar profiles prior to detailed interpretation; (3) to assess the accuracy of GPR and associated processing techniques through comparisons with independent measurements. Over one hundred kilometres of data were recorded at the various sponsors sites in a wide variety of geological conditions for different economic targets. Several examples are presented to demonstrate: 1) the hand-carried and vehicle-towed acquisition techniques, 2) target detection at depths down to 25 m, 3) the benefits of signal processing for good and poor quality data, 4) the use of dielectric measurements, petrophysical modelling and frequency-dependent synthetic radargrams, 5) the application of seismic interpretation concepts. The project has demonstrated commercially acceptable rates of GPR data acquisition where the penetration is satisfactory. Some of the unfavourable Australian geological conditions for radar have also been identified. Although signal processing techniques have extended the applicable range of the radar technique, additional hardware enhancements have been identified to improve the commercial application of radar. The next stage is to assess the economic feasibility of radar by comparison with competing techniques such as drilling. © ASEG 1992.

title: On a number of spare haulage units for the shovel-truck system in open pit mines
source: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
authors: Czaplicki J.M.
abstract: Shovel-truck systems are widely applied in open-pit mining. In these systems spare haulage units are employed as a rule. Recommendations and rules which are used to determine the reserve truck fleet size can give significant difference in estimation of a number of units needed for a given system. The paper consider the problem of proper selection of a spare haulage unit fleet size taking into account economical and technical parameters of trucks, their exploitation process as well as the reliability indices. © 1992, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

title: Structure and age of the Cerro de Pasco Cu-Zn-Pb-Ag deposit, Peru
authors: Cheney E.
abstract: The world-famous Cu-Zn-Pb-Ag deposit at Cerro de Pasco, Peru, consists of texturally massive pyrite, texturally massive sphalerite-galena-pyrite, and veins containing pyrite and enargite. Historically the deposit has been considered to be the hydrothermal product of the adjacent Miocene volcanic and intrusive complex (locally known as the "Vent"). However, both the texturally massive sulfides of the deposit and the pre-Miocene strata are cut by the Longitudinal fault, one of the largest faults in the district, but the Vent is not. Imbrication by the Longitudinal fault zone (duplex structures) has thickened the deposit so that it is amenable to open-pit mining. Dikes and pyrite-enargite veins pass from the Vent into the massive sulfides; fragments of massive pyrite occur in the Vent. Thus, no matter what their origin, the texturally massive sulfides are older and, therefore, genetically unrelated to the Vent. © 1991 Springer-Verlag.

title: German reunification brings cleanup tasks
source: Forum for Applied Research Public Policy
authors: Michel J.
abstract: Among the recently freed communist nations of Eastern Europe, East Germany probably was the most prosperous. It had the highest gross percapita income and was self-sufficient in food, energy, and most manufactured goods, yet by Western standards, East Germany's economy was fragile. Since reunification, much of its industry has been shut down because of inefficiencies, and unemployment could reach 50% of the work force. This paper details the grave environmental abuses that accompanied East Germany's former prosperity and that today present a united Germany with a massive cleanup chore. In energy, for example, extensive open-pit mining and burning of lignite - the primary energy source for the former republic - created major problems in land use, water quality, and air pollution control. Of particular concern is the high levels of sulfur dioxide emissions that need to be reduced by 1993 to meet treaty obligations. Pollution levels, closely guarded under the communist regime, are believed responsible for damage to 65% of East Germany's forests. Among other major environmental problems are contaminated tap water, toxic waste discharges from chemical plants, "wild' garbage dumps, and traffic congestion. -from Author

title: Extraction of non-traditional types of hydrocarbon resources by application of electromagnetic energy
authors: Makogon Y.F.; Sayakhov F.L.; Khabibullin I.L.
abstract: Recently, there is a significant interest in prospecting for and developing non-traditional types of hydrocarbon resources, as petroleum bitumens, gas hydrates, oil shales, and ozokerite. Significant reserves of such resources exist, and they constitute an energy and raw-materials alternative to oil and gas. Also, natural bitumens contain significant quantities of valuable minerals and compounds. Under formation conditions, these alternative hydrocarbon-containing substances completely fill the pore space and exist in solid, crystalline or amorphous state. Their extraction by familiar oil-and-gas production techniques is therefore impossible. There is a need for new techniques of hydrocarbons extraction by open-pit mining and in wells. One such method involves the application of electromagnetic energy, which is injected into the formation in the form of high-frequency electromagnetic waves. The interaction of electromagnetic waves with the rocks generates heat sources and ponderommotive forces and physicochemical surface phenomena, electrocapillary and electrosurface effects which could be useful in their production.

title: A methodology for the optimum control of shovel and truck operations in open-pit mining
authors: Li Z.
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for the optimum control of shovel and truck operations in open-pit mining. Particularly discussed are the problems of material flow planning, truck dispatching, and equipment matching. The linear programming technique is used for planning material flows along paths in the haulage network, the maximum intertruck-time deviation rule of truck dispatching is proposed for facilitating implementation of automated truck dispatching systems, and the least square of intertruck-time deviation is suggested as the criterion for optimally matching trucks with shovels. © 1990 Elsevier Science Publishers B.V.

title: The Industrial Landscape of Rio Tinto, Huelva, Spain
authors: Willies L.
abstract: Rio Tinto has the largest deposits of pyrite and copper pyrite and associated minerals in Europe. It was exploited by the pre-Roman Iberians for silver and copper, and later by the Romans. The greatest change to the landscape came with open-pit mining or quarrying by the British Rio Tinto Company in the late nineteenth century and the first half of the twentieth century for pyrite for sulphur and copper. Even this will be obliterated by current mining projects — the Cerro Colorado project of 1973 was started by the Spanish successor company, Rio Tinto Minera (though still associated with the RTZ multi-national company), and more recently there has been an intensification of gold and silver extraction from the gossan which overlies the pyritic deposits. Damage to the industrial archaeology is also resulting from a large scale reclamation programme, and an attempt to develop a Museum Park on the site largely failed. This report briefly considers the remains at Rio Tinto, and includes photographs recording pre-1950 features of the mines. © 1989 Maney Publishing.

title: Geology of the Vulture mine
authors: White D.
abstract: The Vulture mine near Wickenburg, Arizona was a major gold producer from 1863 to 1942, having yielded about 11t(12.1 st) Au and 8t(8.8st) Ag. Gold occurs as coarse native metal and electrum in quartz veins and also finely disseminated within a quartz monzonite sill and its silicified wall rock. The sill is semi-conformable within a Proterozoic volcaniclastic-dominated sequence, all dipping north about 35°. Early mining focused on the vein-hosted gold, particularly in the immediate hanging wall and footwall of the sill. Later efforts included some open-pit mining of the outcropping sill and adjacent altered and mineralized rock. Two sets of post-mineral faults have complicated the orebody geometry. The Proterozoic rocks are notably lean in precious metals except where altered in proximity to the Creataceous stock and still. Circumstances dictate an interpretation of epigenetic mineralization related to the Laramide intrusion.

title: Dumping of other than mining waste in mining cavities - Basic legal and mine-engineering conditions
authors: Furer G.
abstract: The amount of waste produced by an industrial and consumer society such as that of the Federal Republic of Germany is enormous. A vital objective of legislation is to avoid and recycle wastes, but this is still in the initial stages. Consequently, many waste materials with ecologically objectionable properties must be eliminated at geologically and hydrologically suitable disposal sites. Such dumps include cavities resulted from mining activities, such as open-pit mining, underground mining, and caverns produced by leaching. The general legal as well as technical waste-disposal and mining conditions which currently have to be satisfied in the Federal Republic of Germany are discussed.

title: Influence of blasting techniques on open pit economics
authors: Singhal R.K.; Naidu H.G.; Singh S.P.
abstract: The economics of open-pit mining depend heavily on the cost of overburden removal. It is necessary to maintain a pit slope as steep as possible. Several factors affect the stability of pitwalls. This article deals with one such controllable factor - drilling and blasting. The economics of steeper pit slopes is discussed, followed by a record of drilling and blasting practices in western Canadian surface mines. Microprocessor-based instrumentation and its application to blasthole drilling is also described.

title: Development of a route determination system on open-pit mining using personal computer
source: Waseda Daigaku Rikogaku Kenkyusho Hokoku Bulletin of Science and Engineering Research Laboratory Waseda University
authors: Hagiwara Y.; Yamazaki J.
abstract: The authors have developed a haul road determination system for shovel and dump truck method hauling on open-pit mining sites. Under this system, the optimum haul road (or route) should provide the highest possible safety to the travelling dump truck as well as the shortest possible cycle time. Uncertain conditions and indefinite factors inherent to designing an open-pit mine have been simplified in order to put a personal computer into practical use. A simulation test has revealed that the use of this system has practical value up to 80 × 80 mesh data by translating BASIC to ASSEMBLER language.

title: Development work continues for open-pit mining at Red Dog
authors: Hodgson S.
abstract: The Red Dog zinc/lead deposit in northwest Alaska is the second largest zinc deposit ever discovered. Being developed by Caminco Alaska, with startup scheduled for early 1990, it will ultimately be the largest zinc mine in the Western World. The article describes proposed mining operations and ore treatment. The partnership between Cominco and NANA is unique. It is the first major resource development in Alaska in which a native corporation has had direct participation.

title: Finite element modeling of the Rurscholle multi-aquifer groundwater system
source: Computational Methods in Water Resources Vol 1 Proc 7th Conference Cambridge Ma 1988
authors: Dorgarten H.
abstract: In order to simulate the impact of open-pit mining, a complex finite element multi-aquifer groundwater model was developed. Special algorithms were included to describe the progressing excavation and refilling of the pits. As the groundwater drawdown causes both wide-ranging depressions and steep gradients, extended project-areas and relatively small elements are required, resulting in extremely large meshes. Thus, simulations can only be performed by highly vectorized models on today's super-computers. -from Author

title: The discovery of the Brouzils antimony deposit in the Vendee, Massif Armoricain, France: prospection, description of deposit, proposed exploitation
authors: Le Fur Y.; Allon A.; Biron R.; Lequertier M.; Roussel M.
abstract: The country rocks of the veins are Lower Palaeozoic greywackes and grey to green shales with intervals of volcanic material. The have been deformed during the Early Devonian and Late Devonian/Early Carboniferous (Bretonian), with the formation of N100° to N135° trending folds accompanied by schistosity, and of shears and slides of the same trend. They have also been affected by N-S, E-W and NE-SW extension and fracturing. The Vendee antimony vein field was detected by bedrock Sb geochemistry and electromagnetic survey, followed by trenching and drilling. The veins, including those of Rochetrejoux and Brouzils, occupy tension gashes and shear fractures related to major phases of activity of the South Armorican faults. The vein field developed at the intersection of two fracture systems and includes N-S structures recognised discontinuously over distances of 2-3km, and a main NE-SW bundle dipping NE at 75°-80°. This structure is 6-7m wide and has been recognised over a length of 800m and down to depths of 50-100m. Five richer columns ranging from 30 to 120m long have been distinguished within the bundle. Chalcedonic quartz and stibnite in variable proportions are the main vein-filling minerals, with very minor carbonates, pyrite and arsenopyrite. The geological reserves are estimated at 6000 t of Sb metal, of which 3000 t can be extracted by open-pit mining, in an ore containing 6-7% Sb. The ore can be processed to give excellent commercial concentrate with no impurities or penalising elements. The Gagneraud-BRGM mining project involves open-cast mining of the first 20m at a rate of 100 t Sb per month, protecting the deeper levels. -from English summary

title: SURVIVAL STRATEGY: EVERY BIT COUNTS.
authors: Garg O.
abstract: The Iron Ore Company of Canada (IOC) operations in Labrador and Quebec among the largest open-pit mining complexes on a world basis. Since the 1981-82 recession, IOC has embarked on a cost reduction and productivity improvement program in order to survive in the world iron ore market. This paper outlines the approach used in prioritizing the cost reduction items.

title: Considerations Concerning the Effect of the Grain Size of Blasted Material on Hard-Rock Open-Pit Mining.
authors: Lechner E.
abstract: The character of blasted material with respect to its grain size can properly be demonstrated by its grading curve on the RRS-diagram. For different grading curves the quantity of boulders and the relative digging resistance are investigated as functions of the bucket capacity. These results form the fundamentals for determining the character of the blasted material with respect to its loading properties. Subsequently the connection between the character of the blasted rock and the production capacity, as well as the cost for the hydraulic shovel and track system, is investigated. Blasted material of poor character leads to significant increases in cost.

title: IN-THE-WALL HAULAGE FOR OPEN-PIT MINING.
authors: Hustrulid W.A.; Seegmiller B.; Stephansson O.
abstract: As open pits become deeper and ore grades become lower, there is a great need for innovation in surface mining. A suggestion made by Henriksson in the early 1970s was for the consideration of in-the-wall haulage systems in conjunction with or in place of the conventional in-the-pit ramp system. Since then, few, if any, mines have adopted such a system. This paper has reexamined the concept and attempted to describe some reasons why mine planners might consider it in the future. The authors believe there are ore bodies/ pits for which this method should be strongly considered. A combination of an in-the-wall haulage system with a program of rock reinforcement and ground water depressurization would be a major innovation in mining because pit slopes could possibly be safely steepened from the conventional 40 degree -50 degree to 60 degree -70 degree . This could save millions of tons of stripping.

title: SETTLEMENT INSTRUMENTATION TO OBSERVE OPEN-PIT MINE BACKFILL AND A PROTOTYPE FOUNDATION IN WESTERN CANADA.
authors: Thomson S.; Sonnenberg R.
abstract: The settlement of the spoil from one open-pit mining operation west of Edmonton, Alberta, was monitored by a series of magnetic extensometers installed in boreholes. Time-settlement plots indicated that self-weight settlement occurs within a 3-5 year period. Tests of individual small footings pointed out the necessity of placing shallow foundations on beneficiated soil. The results of a second series of small footings led to the founding of an 8 multiplied by 10 m prototype instrumented, reinforced foundation on a 1 m thick soil - flyash mat. Observations to date indicate an entirely acceptable settlement pattern.

title: THE LONG‐TERM EFFECTS OF A TOKEN ECONOMY ON SAFETY PERFORMANCE IN OPEN‐PIT MINING
authors: Fox D.K.; Hopkins B.L.; Anger W.K.
keywords: long‐term effects | miners | safety | token economy
abstract: A token economy that used trading stamps as tokens was instituted at two dangerous open‐pit mines. Employees earned stamps for working without lost‐time injuries, for being in work groups in which all other workers had no lost‐time injuries, for not being involved in equipment‐damaging accidents, for making adopted safety suggestions, and for unusual behavior which prevented an injury or accident. They lost stamp awards if they or other workers in their group were injured, caused equipment damage, or failed to report accidents or injuries. The stamps could be exchanged for a selection of thousands of items at redemption stores. Implementation of the token economy was followed by large reductions in the number of days lost from work because of injuries, the number of lost‐time injuries, and the costs of accidents and injuries. The reductions in costs far exceeded the costs of operating the token economy. All improvements were maintained over several years. 1987 Society for the Experimental Analysis of Behavior

title: CRITERIA FOR THE MATERIAL SELECTION FOR AIRCRAFT STRUCTURE.
source: Transactions of the Iron and Steel Institute of Japan
authors: Anon
abstract: A comparison of numerical evaluations of the H. K. Taylor and Zwiagin formula with the use of data from underground coal mines shows that the former predicts higher optimum output levels for reserves in excess of about 60,000,000t. For smaller reserves the two methods are more or less comparable. When applied to open-bit lignite mines with reserves of 20,000,000-160,000,000t it appears that the upper limit of the Taylor relation provides a better approximation of optimum output than the usual formulation. This is explained by the facts that in open-pit mining it is possible to use highly efficient mining equipment, transport facilities are more flexible and better working conditions reduce the accident rate. The data are based on a mine in Turkey.

title: BASIC STAGES IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF ELECTRIC LOCOMOTIVE PRODUCTION AT THE NOVOCHERKASSKY ELECTRIC LOCOMOTIVE PLANT.
authors: Duvarov V.
abstract: The Novocherkassky Electric Locomotive Plant (NEVZ) is a major enterprise in the field of heavy transportation machinery construction with an electrical equipment profile. The Plant is now turning out mainline (road) ac freight locomotives, diesel-electric traction units for open-pit mining operations, vehicles for the Toilisi Electric Locomotive Plant (TEVZ), and motors for the Dnepropetrovskii Electric Locomotive Plant (DEVZ). More than 80% of the freight moving over the electrified mainline railways of the USSR is hauled by locomotives manufactured at the NEVZ. The history of the Plant is recalled and the main stages in its development are described. Recently, the development of a new generation of twelve-axle two-section electric locomotives has commenced on the basis of the VL85 locomotive.

title: ADVANCES IN OVERBURDEN BLAST-CASTING.
source: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
authors: Gupta R.N.; Adhikari G.R.; Singh B.
abstract: The paper presents an overview of the global development in the field of overburden blast-casting. Parameters to be considered for a successful casting of overburden by blasting are discussed. The economical and environmental aspects of explosive casting are detailed. In India, where more than 60% of coal production is expected from opencast method, blast-casting is anticipated to be a cheaper alternative to conventional stripping operations. For open-pit mining of developed coal seams in Indian coalfields, blast-casting is likely to offer special technological advantages.

title: DESIGN AND CALCULATION FOR A SLURRY EXPLOSIVE CHARGING VEHICLE.
source: Changsha Kuangshan Yanjiuyuan Jikan Quarterly of the Changsha Institute of Mining Research
authors: Sun Z.
abstract: In China, a variety of industrial explosives are being rapidly developed. The slurry explosive is one of the major blasting agents used in open-pit mining. Nevertheless, its charging technology is rather primitive. This paper offers a systematic description of a slurry explosive charging machine, as well as its design and calculation.

title: Computer-Aided Planning of an Open-Pit Mine in Unconsolidated Rock.
authors: Moser M.; Vegh P.
abstract: The solution of certain planning tasks connected with open-pit mining in unconsolidated rock is not only made easier by the computer but in some cases only first becomes possible with the aid of the computer. In order to be able to execute the large mass movements of this type of operation at low cost, the crucial points of the planning, such as winning and the depositing of waste in the course of regular operation, are optimized with the aid of a computer on the basis of a planning example, and the operations required are discussed. The presentation of the results of seven essential working steps makes it possible to evaluate the quality of computer-aided planning of open-pit mining.

title: GOLDEN GLOW AT BATTLE MOUNTAIN.
authors: Argall G.
abstract: By all standards, Nevada's Battle Mountain Gold Co. (BMG) is a rare species as a mining company. Hatched December 1984 as a spin-off vehicle by a parent oil company disenchanted with the mining industry, BMG was literally born with a gold bar in its treasury. As of January 1, 1985, measured and indicated gold and silver reserves were 7,723,000 st assaying 0. 154 tr oz/st gold and 0. 831 tr oz/st silver in the main orebody - the Fortitude. The nearby Northwest Extension orebody has 693,000 st of demonstrated reserves assaying 0. 102 tr oz/st gold and 0. 346 tr oz/st silver. In addition to the precious metals reserves, BMG inherited (all but free of short and long-term debt) a 50,000-st/d open-pit mining fleet; a 3,600-st/d-capacity grinding/cyanidation/carbon-in-pulp milling plant; spare equipment inventories; mine buildings; and all other facilities to support the operation. All Battle Mountain mining claims and interests in several exploration projects were included.

title: Seismic attenuation spectra in rock mass characterization: a case study in open-pit mining.
authors: Young R.P.; Hill J.J.
abstract: The application of engineering geophysics to the characterization of rock masses is exemplified through a case study of 3 phases of a research project into the design of efficient blasting systems in open-pit mining. Seismic experiments are used before and after in blasting to monitor the efficiency of explosions in terms of rock fragmentation. Spectral analysis of seismic signals, after they have been used to interrogate rock masses, is used to compute preblast and postblast attenuation and velocity parameters. The results show that fragmentation efficiency of a mine blast and fracture anisotropy of a rock mass can be quantified in terms of 3-D attenuation spectra and polar anisotropy diagrams.-from Authors

title: Modeling the explosion of a system of borehole charges in a scarp
authors: Neiman I.B.
abstract: On the basis of the mathematical model here proposed for the action of the explosion of two cylindrical (borehole) explosive charges in the scarp of a rock mass, the scope for investigating the correlation between wave propagation parameters with scarp rock cutting in a pit is expanded. This offers the possibility of solving a series of problem associated with the correction of wave propagation parameters and their optimization in conditions of open-pit mining of minerals. © 1987 Plenum Publishing Corporation.

title: OPEN-PIT MINING AND ITS MAIN ENGINEERING GEOLOGY PROBLEMS IN CHINA.
source: Yu Se Chin Shu Nonferrous Metals
authors: Yao Baokui; Liu Zhunhua
abstract: Problems of deformation and failure of the slopes of open-pit mines are abecoming more serious in China. The engineering geology problems of the open mine mainly include: the geostress condition, which has an overall control over the stability of slopes of the open pit, especially the regional geological tectonic stress field; properties of the complex rock mass constructin and the construction of medium complexity of the rock formation associaton; open mining problems of moving rock masses which are affected by underground mining and open mining problems in karst rock masses; and the underground water problem, which evidently affects the stability of slopes of th eopen pit.

title: HINDUSTAN COPPER LIMITED: INDIA'S COPPER PRODUCER.
authors: White L.
abstract: Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL), a Government of India enterprise and the nation's only producer of refined copper, operates three divisions: the Malanjkhand open-pit mine in Madhya Pradesh, the Indian Copper Complex (ICC) in Bihar, and the Khetri Copper Complex (KCC) in Rajasthan. Corporate headquarters is in Calcutta. Current copper reserves in India stand at 566 million mt in 74 deposits at an average grade of 1. 1% Cu. Estimates for Malanjkhand approach 1 billion mt of 0. 84% Cu. A working group in the Ministry of Mines, including HCL representation, formulates policy for management of these resources. Future investment is expected to focus on low cost production, and for that reason, Malanjkhand, with large reserves accessible to open-pit mining, is expected to attract the most attention.

title: CONTINUOUS EQUIPMENT: AN IMPORTANT TREND.
authors: Krumrey A.
abstract: Modern open-pit mining is characterized by ever greater volumes of material, and operation at ever greater depths. The limits of mining economy are thus shifted to increasingly less favorable overburden-to-mineral ratios so that open-pit technology becomes primarily a matter of overburden stripping while extraction of the pay mineral is a secondary consideration. The continuous method was developed in Germany, with bucketwheel excavators for mining, conveyors for onward transport, and boom stackers for overburden dumping.

title: MODERN OPEN-PIT MINING TECHNOLOGY.
authors: Ringleff H.
abstract: This paper describes two types of opencast mining technologies, which have been developed for more efficiency and reliability with regard to continuous bulk material handling. The conceptual design of a phosphate mining system is a combination of continuous bucket wheel operation, dragline strip mining, reclaiming by means of bucketwheel, and pumping the phosphate slurry in pipelines. Shiftable and mobile crushing units are special opencast systems used for hard rock formations.

title: Characteristics and mechanisms for the formation of structurally thickened coal deposits, southeastern Canadian Cordillera.
source: 9e Congres International De Stratigraphie Et De Geologie Du Carbonifere Washington Et Champaign Urbana 1979 Compte Rendu Vol 4
authors: Bustin R.M.
abstract: Structural thickening of coal seams of the Late Jurassic-Early Cretaceous Kootenay Formation in the southeastern Canadian Cordillera enables open-pit mining of otherwise marginally economic deposits. In some areas, coal seams are structurally thickened by as much as an order of magnitude in response to thrust faulting, normal faulting, and folding. Predicting the distribution of structurally thickened coal requires a closely spaced drilling program, a well-planned trenching program, and an understanding of the structural style of the coal measures. -from Author

title: IN-PIT CRUSHING AND TROLLEY-ASSISTED TRUCK HAULAGE IN HARD ROCK OPEN-PIT MINES.
authors: Mueller-Roden H.
abstract: The International Conference on 'The Planning and Operation of Open Pit and Strip Mines', organized by the University of Pretoria, the South African Institute of Mining and Metallurgy, and the University's Mining Alumni Society, was held at the University of Pretoria Campus from April 9 to 13, 1984. The conference consisted of four parts, of which one dealt with new developments in open-pit mining, such as in-pit crushing, trolley-assisted truck haulage, and computer applications. This article presents a critical discussion on the experience gained from that conference and a visit to several mines in the Republic of South Africa.

title: Seismic hazard and risk in open-pit mining.
source: Transactions Institution of Mining Metallurgy Section A
authors: Skipp B.
abstract: Even with an elaborate hazard study the confidence that can be assigned to the estimate of the hazard at a particular location will never be very high. In mining operations this may impose expensive and unwarranted demand on a system that may need to work near to failure. With the seismic hazard evaluation techniques that are now available and where a first guess puts the intensity of the design earthquake at >VIII the evaluation of the hazard to be used in dynamic mine slope or dam design should be at least to the standard of the second level identified above, commensurate with the static pit slope design method. If the pit slope is to be designed with the aid of advanced numerical techniques-in particular, with probabilistic analyses-the hazard study should be of a commensurate nature.-from Author

title: MAMUT MINE.
authors: Fumoto N.
abstract: The Mamut mine which is the first porphyry copper type mine in Malaysia started its open-pit mining in May 1975. The mine is managed by Overseas Mineral Resources Development (OMRD) Sabah Bhd, a joint venture company organized by and between Malaysia and Japan. To support this project, Mamut Mines Development Co. , Ltd. (a consortium of seven major japanese non-ferrous mining and metallurgical firms), was established in Japan, and has been engaged in sales of concentrates as well as offering funds and technology assistance. The Mamut mining operation had to adopt the multi-stage narrow bench system under such situations as (1) steep topography, (2) the ore deposit being incised beneath a high hill, (3) necessity of blending the various kinds of crude ore, (4) much rainfall, (5) reduced amount of pre-stripping due to depressed initial costs and so forth. As a result, the operation needed small and medium mining equipments which had high mobility. The actual work was carried out mainly by combining wheel loaders and 40T-45T dump trucks. The various difficult problems encountered at the initial stage were overcome, and the current operation is in good progress on 500 th. T/month ore and 610 th. T/month waste basis.

title: INCREASING PRODUCTION WITH LOADERS AND TRUCKS.
authors: Anon
abstract: Efficient cycle time in loaders and trucks can mean increased production for any open-pit mining operation. The article gives costs and production capacities for various shovel/truck fleet sizes.

title: Policy analysis model for open-pit mining enterprises.
source: Transactions Institution of Mining Metallurgy Section A
authors: Coyle R.; Montaldo-Cancela D.
abstract: Apparently good policies at one level must not conflict with those at another. Analysis of the model shows that well-designed management policies can produce noticeable improvements in economic performance. -from Authors

title: COMMERCIAL PRODUCTION OF U3O8 BEGINS AT KEY LAKE.
authors: Todd J.
abstract: The start-up process at Key Lake Mining Corp's (KLMC) uranium mine and mill in the Athabasca sandstone basin, 640 km north of Saskatoon, Sask. , Canada is briefly described. Key Lake ore is excavated by open-pit mining. The ore is crushed in a gyratory unit and further broken by impact crushing. Grinding is carried out by ball milling. A primary leach takes place in four downstream pachucas with the assistance of sulfuric acid and air.

title: Environmental Problems during Blasting Operations in Open-pit Mining and Quarrying - Possibilities of Reducing These Problems.
source: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
authors: Wild H.
abstract: The author investigated measures to avoid or reduce blasting vibrations. Such measures include proper charge sizing of the drillhole diameter, use of detonators with short time intervals, breakdown of the charge into smaller portions, proper wall height, firing method, and avoiding mud caps in block holing.

title: PRODUCTIVITY IN THE NONFERROUS METALS INDUSTRY.
authors: Michal E.
abstract: Changes in productivity in the nonferrous metals industry have been both positive and negative. Open-pit mining operations show improved productivity, while capital-intensive milling, smelting, and refining operations show only slight improvements. Underground mining is retrogressing. The article discusses the major factors influencing productivity which are: labor management attitudes, capital investment, resource and energy availability, technological improvement, product quality requirements, and regulatory actions.

title: Technology of Crusher Utilization in Hard-Rock Open-Pit Mining in the German Democratic Republic.
authors: Strzodka K.; Piatkowiak N.; Steinmetz R.
abstract: The use of stationary and mobile crushers in open-pit mining is discussed. The various types of mobile crushers used in the GDR are reviewed, and the equipment required for hard-rock open-pit mining with mobile crushers and belt conveyors is indicated. The results obtained from the use of these crushers are evaluated.

title: Development of Mining Work at Ekibastuz Deposit.
authors: Tynterov I.; Vagin E.; Anpilogov A.
abstract: The plan of 600m deep open-pit mining operations adapted at the initial stage of the development of the huge Ekibastuz deposit in Kazakhstan is criticized as having a number of essential shortcomings on particular deconcentration of mining operations and wrong choice of priority working sections. Some ways to correct the situation are considered.

title: QUEBRADA BLANCA, CHILE: AN ENRICHED PORPHYRY COPPER DEPOSIT.
authors: Hunt J.P.; Bratt J.A.; Marquardt L J.C.
abstract: The Quebrada Blanca copper/molybdenum prospect lies in the high Andes of Chile. The Superior Oil-Falconbridge Group began exploration in 1977 under a joint venture foreign investment agreement with the Chilean government. A successful exploration program has developed an open-pit mining reserve, provided samples for bulk metallurgical testing, and located supplies of water for future operations. The main orebody is amenable to conventional metallurgical treatment and contains more than 400 Mt (441 million st) of recoverable ore at about a 1:1 stripping ratio. The average millhead grade during the first six years of operations will exceed 1. 5% Cu, plus recoverable molybdenum values. Several hundred million tons of additional reserves are available.

title: BULLMOOSE MINE PROJECT.
authors: Drozd R.
abstract: The Bullmoose Mine is currently under construction in the north east coal area of British Columbia and approximately 300 million will be spent. This paper covers the history and exploration work on the property, the geology, open-pit mining plans and equipment, the preparation plant flowsheet from breaker station to clean coal silo, the 35 km highway truck haul, railroad loadout system, manpower requirements, construction progress, approvals and permits, and financial arrangements.

title: Recents Developments in Open-Pit Mining.
authors: Gurs P.
abstract: Spectacular progress has been made in open-pit mining during the last 20 years of industrial expansion, both from the point of view of technical advances in equipment and in mining and management methods. The purpose of the present article is to review the current trends in open-pit mining methods and equipment and to indicate some recent achievements and the size of equipment available for future projects.

title: OPTIMUM SCHEDULING OF OVERBURDEN REMOVAL IN OPEN-PIT MINES.
authors: Qing-Xia Yun; Yegulalp T.
abstract: This paper formulates optimum production scheduling in open-pit mining as an inventory problem and develops a solution using dynamic programming techniques.

title: COST CONSIDERATIONS FOR IN-PIT CRUSHING/CONVEYING SYSTEMS.
authors: Huss C.
abstract: This article focuses on continuous materials handling systems used in the hard rock open-pit mining industry. Guidelines for mine planning with continuous systems are outlined. Key parameters affecting capital and operating costs are identified. Commonly encountered trade-offs between operating and capital costs are discussed. A typical range of costs is presented based on average operating conditions.

title: OPEN-PIT LIGNITE MINING IN SPAIN.
authors: Anon
abstract: The article discusses examples of solid-rock open-pit mining in the mining regions of Teruel Sur and Tereul Norte-Mequinenza, 90km south-south-west of Zaragoza.

title: MATERIALS MANAGEMENT AT BRENDA MINES LTD.
authors: Sperlins G.
abstract: Brenda Mines Ltd. is a low-grade open-pit mining and milling operation located near Peachland, B. C. The plane treats an average of 30,000 tons per day of an ore that contains 0. 130% copper and 0. 030% molybdenum. The objective of the materials management progam is to solve problems relating to materials from a total organization or system viewpoint.

title: DETERMINING THE OPTIMAL DEPTH OF AN OPEN PIT.
authors: Nilsson D.; Burgher K.
abstract: To determine the optimal depth of an open pit, the Office of Surface Mining, US Department of the Interior, is sponsoring a research project at Michigan Technological University titled ″The effects of increasing energy costs on the future relation between open-pit and underground mining.″ This article analyzes the economic value of various pit depths for one hypothetical example from the project. The conclusion is that with a price of 5/ton of ore, the deposit can be mined with open pit methods down to a depth of 200 m, with future underground mining being unprofitable. With a price of 10/ton, open-pit mining can proceed down to a depth of 300 m. It would be more profitable, however, to change over to underground mining at 250 m depth.

title: DEVELOPING AND EVALUATING PIT TRUCK SAFETY DEVICES.
authors: Yates W.
abstract: Driver visibility is restricted in large, rear-dump haulage trucks used in open-pit mining. Analysis shows the need for an alarm to warn of vehicles in blind spots. Anaconda developed an electromagnetic system whereby smaller vehicles transmit a signal to haulage truck operators to alert them to their presence. The system has been field-tested at the Twin Buttes open-pit mine near Tucson, Ariz.

title: SIMULATED OPEN-PIT MINING CONDITIONS USED TO TEACH DRAGLINE OPERATORS.
authors: Eschman C.
abstract: The Dragline Training System uses a dragline simulator to provide a skills development program for training and retraining dragline operators.

title: SURFACE MINING - PAST, PRESENT AND FUTURE.
source: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
authors: Atkinson T.
matched_open_pit_phrases: open-pit mining; surface mine; surface mining
abstract: The article reviews the history, current state-of-the-art and future trends of development in the field of surface mining. The main topics discussed cover the limits of scale of surface mining operations performed by walking draglines and bucket wheel excavators; mine design and planning for strip, terrace and open-pit mining; ground preparation including drilling and blasting operations; loading and haulage equipment; and surface mine electric power systems.

title: Hydraulic excavators solve economic and operational problems in open-pit.
abstract: The use and servicing of hydraulic excavators in open-pit mining operations in France is discussed.

title: BUCIM COPPER PROJECT: YUGOSLAVIA'S NEW 85 MILLION MINE AND FLOTATION CONCENTRATOR WILL PRODUCE 100,000 MT/YR OF COPPER CONCENTRATE.
authors: Westergard A.
abstract: The Bucim Copper Project in Yugoslavia, in operation since mid 1979, uses conventional open-pit mining and ore processing methods and includes some of the largest mining and processing equipment in the world. After a historical summary, the article deals with ore genesis, the process design criteria, mining and crushing, grinding and flotation, filtration and tails handling, and instrumentation.

title: Public policy for the management of groundwater in the coastal plains of North Carolina.
authors: Sherwani J.
abstract: The need for management is emphasized by the fact that in some parts of the region, the aquifer system is reaching its production potential to permit open-pit mining for phosphate ore. The areas of large concentrated withdrawals and extensive lowering of the potentiometric surface have created conditions for possible water quality deterioration. The projections of water needs for municipal, industrial, and agricultural uses to the year 2000 are developed. -from US Govt Reports Announcements, 24, 1980

title: Costs of Learning about the Environmental Damage of Mining Projects
authors: CAMPBELL H.; SCOTT A.
abstract: Two ways of gathering information about and mitigating the impact of a large‐scale mining project are briefly described and contrasted:one way involves postponing the construction and operation of the project while attempts are made to forecast, evaluate and prepare for its impact; the other way involves commencing immediately with a small‐scale, or attenuated, project with a smaller impact and by studying the effects of this project inferring the impact of a large‐scale project. The costs of the two alternative policies of postponement and attenuation are defied as reductions m the present value of the project in question. A model of open‐pit mining is perished which allows these costs to be calculated for any degree of postponement or attenuation. The model is applied to three uranium mines in the Northern Territory of Australia to estimate for each mine the costs of the two policies. The model is then used to estimate the costs of sequences of mine development in the Northern Territory involving various combinations of postponement and attenuation policies. The costs of these policies are then compared with the reduction in the impact of the industry using the population of a mining town site as a proxy for impact. This comparison is a first step towards a benefit/cost analysis of the two policies. Copyright © 1980, Wiley Blackwell. All rights reserved

title: Economic evaluation of the damage caused to natural and economic features by the iron-ore industry of the KMA.
authors: Forafontova V.I.
abstract: The growing iron-ore industry of the Kursk Magnetic Anomaly in central Russia causes heavy damage to the environment because of heavy reliance on open-pit operations. The damage includes the transfer of fertile chernozem farmland to mining uses, the razing of settlements and the need for resettling the displaced population, the transfer of land in industry to mining uses, and the cost of restoring the regional water-management balance after disruption by open-pit mining. Formulas for calculating the replacement cost of the disrupted features are proposed, and the resulting reduction of the cost-effectiveness of the mining operations is calculated. The transfer of farmland to nonfarm uses is found to be the greatest factor reducing the cost-effectiveness of the mining operations. The restoration of the water balance is less of a factor, and the compensation for the razing of settlement and industry is found to be negligible, possibly because some aspects were not considered in the calculations.- from Soviet Geography

title: Kyanite mining in Virginia.
authors: Dixon G.
abstract: Reserves of kyanite in Buckingham County, Virginia, will last several decades, especially at the open-pit mining operation at Willis Mountain. This short review considers the history, mining, processing, and economic uses of kyanite. -R.S.M.

title: HOW BLASTHOLE SHOCK ABSORBERS REDUCE COSTS.
authors: Work J.
abstract: Spiraling costs in every segment of the open-pit mining cycle is a fact of life that every operator must reckon with. The introduction of various shock absorbing devices for rotary drilling is one recent innovation that may significantly reduce overall drilling cost, increase drill availability, and lower maintenance requirements. A shock absorber is simply a device installed between the rotary drive head and drill steel that cushions the two. It functions in the same manner as springs and shocks on an automobile. The article discusses benefits of shock absorbers, including minimizing vibrations, extending bit life, and lowering maintenance needs.

title: FIELD TESTING AND EVALUATION OF SERVICE BRAKE CAPABILITY FOR LARGE-SIZE DIESEL-ELECTRIC HAULAGE TRUCKS.
authors: Sahay H.
abstract: This paper describes the main testing procedures that should be carried out to evaluate the capacity and capability of the service brakes on the large-size diesel-electric trucks now in common use at open-pit mining operations. Brake testing programs in general are described, then consideration is given to different techniques of service brake testing, brake performance evaluation, braking energy and typical performance characteristics.

title: QUINSAM COAL PROJECT.
authors: Barnstable D.
abstract: Quinsam Coal Ltd. is assessing the potential of developing a thermal coal deposit near Middle Quinsam Lake on Vancouver Island in British Columbia, Canada. The coal reserve outlined is classified as a high-volatile, bituminous ″A″ steam coal and is composed of four separate seams of varying quality within the Late Cretaceous Comox Formation. Open-pit mining methods will utilize a walking dragline and a truck/shovel module as the primary stripping tools. Following washing and mechanical drying in a Baum jig preparation plant, the coal will be transported to the proposed dock at Campbell River for shipment via 55,000-DWT vessels to world markets. The paper outlines the development and status of the project to date.

title: Geology of the Athabasca oil sands
authors: Mossop G.D.
abstract: In-place bitumen resources in the Alberta oil sands are estimated at 1350 billion barrels. Open-pit mining and hot water extraction methods, which involve the handling of huge tonnages of earth materials, are being employed in the two commercial plants now operating. In situ recovery methods will be required to tap the 90 percent of reserves that are too deeply buried to be surface mined. Development of in situ technologies will be painstaking and expensive, and success will hinge on their compatibility with extremely complex geological conditions in the subsurface. Copyright © 1980 AAAS.

title: KRUPP TRANSPORT CRAWLERS - A NEW AID IN OPEN-PIT MINING.
authors: Krumrey A.
abstract: A heavy-load crawler for transporting loads of up to 1,000 tons has been designed and built. The principal technical data of four designs are shown.

title: Creation of Safe and Healthy Condition of Labor for Soviet Coal Miners - A Most Important Social Task.
authors: Nikitin V.
abstract: The measures taken in the USSR to improve the state of safety engineering and to make the conditions of work at the coal industry undertakings safer are described. Mechanization of mining work and conveyor transport reduce the number of injuries. So does open-pit mining which will constitute 36% of total output in 1980. Underground mining encounters increasing difficulties owing to greater depths and more complicated geological conditions. Degassing is carried out at 196 mines, with extraction of 1. 3 billion m**3 of methane per annum. Measures to prevent and control coal, rock, and gas bursts are described.

title: INNOVATIVE TECHNIQUES EMPLOYED TO CONSTRUCT SLURRY CUTOFF TRENCH FOR SYNCRUDE'S BEAVER CREEK DAM.
authors: Brown M.
abstract: Syncrude Canada Ltd. recently completed construction of its ambitious tar-sand mining and processing facilities at Mildred Lake, Alberta. The Syncrude operation involves the open-pit mining of approximately 270,000 tonnes (300,000 tons) of tar sand daily using draglines and a conveyor system. The peat deposits and high groundwater levels at the site combine to make the excavation and construction of a conventional rolled clay cutoff impractical. For these reasons, the slurry cutoff trench technique described here was utilized to produce an efficient and effective seepage cutoff under various sections of the Beaver Creek Dam.

title: The Bingham copper deposits, Utah, as an exploration target: History and pre-excavation geology
authors: James L.P.
abstract: The Bingham mining district was discovered in 1863, shortly after Caucasian civilization reached the Great Basin. For many decades argentiferous galena-sphalerite ores were produced from steeply dipping veins and bedded replacement deposits. Copper occurrences were known, but largely uneconomic. Recognition of the copper- rich mineralized porphyry body at the center of the district had occurred by the end of the 19th century. Breakthroughs in mining technology were required to make the deposit minable, but once begun the mine rapidly became the largest in the northern hemisphere. Large contact metasomatic copper deposits also were developed in limestone units adjacent to the Bingham stock. A number of careful workers, both famous and forgotten, contributed to the general knowledge of base metal deposits at Bingham. A major lawsuit led to careful studies of the replacement deposits by noted experts. Prior to mining, the Bingham porphyry copper deposit was characterized by a leached, iron oxide-rich capping, typically containing several tenths of one percent copper and also traces of gold. Telluride minerals were present locally. Coarse placer gold and boulders of ferruginous conglomerate occurred in adjacent drainages. The larger high-grade veins of the district radiated from or occurred near the boundaries of the mineralized portion of the stock. Deep underground workings followed lead-zinc ores to 5,000 feet vertically beneath the surface and work is now in progress to mine copper ores below the 3,300-foot level of the old underground mines. Open-pit mining has reached depths of 2,500 feet below the original outcrops. The district contains a very barren pluton (Last Chance stock) and a metal zoning pattern that extends only relatively short distances outward into country rock. A few square miles of gravel cover could have effectively concealed the highly economic copper-rich center of the district.

title: Athabasca tar sands: Occurrence and commercial projects
authors: Spragins F.
abstract: This chapter focuses on the Athabasca tar-sand deposit of northeastern Alberta, Canada, and the commercial developments going on there. The Athabasca tar sands are the major deposit of oil in a viscous-oil trend, stretching across Alberta, from the Alberta-Saskatchewan border near Cold Lake to a point near the town of Peace River. The Athabasca tar sands are divided into two zones: one where oil deposits are covered by oil-barren surface deposits of from 0 to 150 ft and one where these overburden deposits range from 150 ft to more than 2000 ft in thickness. A number of oil companies have undertaken several commercial projects in the area. The Syncrude project has been designed to produce 125,000 bbl/day of synthetic crude oil. In the Syncrude mining scheme, two parallel open-pit mining faces will be opened and actively mined, advancing away from each other, throughout the life of the project. Fina, representing a group of companies, has also submitted an application to the Energy Resources Conservation Board (ERCB) for a permit to produce 122,500 bbl/day of synthetic crude oil by means of a scheme based on mining wheels, hot-water extraction, and fluid coking. © 1978, Elsevier Science & Technology. All rights reserved.

title: GEOLOGY.
authors: Hewett F.
abstract: The geological setting and the development of the Cassiar Asbestos Mine in British Columbia are detailed here, and estimates of the ore reserves contained in the Cassiar orebody are presented. Present information indicates an orebody of approximately 16,277,000 tons amenable to open-pit mining, but continued diamond drilling will be needed to accurately define total tonnage and grade. A program has been developed at the mine to provide the required information on a daily basis, and work is continuing on more effective dollar-value prediction methods.

title: Calculation of the External Field of Natural Grounding of Complex Shape.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Mitropol'skaya S.O.; Sapozhnikov V.M.; Bagautinov G.A.
abstract: The advantages and disadvantages of the earlier methods of calculation of external fields and groundings of complex shape are considered. A new method of calculation of the external field of a grounding in the shape of a rectangular plate is proposed. The possibility of utilizing theoretically calculated external fields around mathematical models of complex groundings to predict electric safety conditions at open-pit mining works is demonstrated.

title: JACOBS RANCH SELECTS OPEN-PIT MINING PLAN.
authors: Jackson D.
abstract: Kerr-McGee Coal Corp. 's open-pit mining project is featured that calls for production of 14. 5 million tons per year by the mid-1980's from the three seams at the company's Jacobs Ranch mine in Wyoming's Powder River Basin. The project will provide flexibility demanded by multiple seam mining, quick access to seams and lower reclamation activities and costs. Stripping, overburden removal, pit advances and reclamation steps are detailed.

title: LONG-RANGE MINE PLANNING AT GIBRALTAR MINES LIMITED.
authors: Milner T.
abstract: This paper discusses the package of computer programs implemented at Gibraltar Mines Ltd. (an open-pit copper mine) for the development of long-range mine plans. A Lerch-Grossman three-dimensional pit design program is used for pit design and sequencing of interior-stage pits. A mine simulation program is used to produce production schedules and open-pit mining equipment requirements. Discounted-cash-flow techniques are used to evaluate alternate mine plan schedules. Areas under consideration for further expansion of the computer mine design package will also be discussed.

title: PP&L'S PIT CONCEPT AIDS ANTHRACITE.
authors: Chironis N.
abstract: Open-pit coal mining may be coming to the eastern U. S. under a new walking version that could make anthracite the ideal low-sulfur fuel for Pennsylvania. Power and Light Co's (PP&L) next generating plants. The firm's engineers, devising improvements in the conventional open-pit techniques, have come up with a walking version of open-pit mining in which land is reclaimed automatically behind the operation as the pit moves along in the direction of mining. Open land is thus kept to a minimum yet the pit is large enough to allow recovery of coal deeply from the multiple anthracite seams that generally exist in the area of the deposit.

title: APPLICATION OF THE METHOD OF QUEUEING THEORY TO DETERMINE THE DUMP-TRUCK CAPACITY FOR OPEN-PIT MINING OPERATION.
authors: Yamaguchi U.; Shimotani T.; Tsuzaki M.
abstract: In the open-pit limestone quarry which produces 6200 tons of limestone each day using the Caterpillar 988 (bucket capacity 4. 59 m**3) and 15 ton dump-trucks haulage system, queueing technique was applied to analyze the haulage operation. The suitable number of trucks for a 1000 meter haulage distance to the crusher from the working face of the quarry is 3 to 4 trucks to obtain the lowest haulage cost per ton of limestone.

title: HIBBING TACONITE STARTS UP PHASE I WITH NOTABLE MINING AND MILLING FEATURES.
authors: Sisselman R.
abstract: Key features of Hibbing Taconite Co. 's ongoing construction program in the Mesabi Range, Minn. , which will raise the initial design capacity of 5. 4 million ltpy of pellets to 8. 1 million ltpy by 1979, are briefly described here. The expansion project calls for some large open-pit mining equipment (most notably 170-ton ore haulage trucks and electric shovels equipped with 16-cu-yd dippers); single-stage, closed circuit crushing; single-stage, closed circuit grinding in 36-ft-diam, fully autogenous mills; and traveling grate pelletizing systems.

title: Opencast Mining of Coal in France.
authors: Iooss R.
abstract: The opencast mining method consists in removing the overburden situated above a coal deposit in order to exploit this deposit by the open-pit mining method. The author briefly examines the history of open cast mining of coal in France, and then describes the French coal deposits workable by this method. Proved reserves of these deposits, total 12 million tons, whereas possible reserves are estimated at 8 million tons. Technical details are given on the open cast mining method with particular reference to the type of machinery used, transport, land reclamation and minig costs.

title: LARGER ELECTRIC MINING SHOVEL OF THE FUTURE, TODAY.
authors: Burns S.
abstract: Shovels of 18 cubic yard capacity and larger are described which incorporate advanced technology and techniques providing performance and operation tailored to meet the needs of open-pit mining. To achieve the goals of increasing production at lower cost with consideration of maximum availability, lower energy consumption per ton and low impact on pit power, Harnischfeger Corporation developed a solid-state drive system ( ″Electrotorque″ - P&H trademark) and applied unique transmission methods. This paper discusses the electrical features and touches briefly on some mechanical features of this new shovel.

title: Reclamation: A Challenge to Open-Pit Mining in Canada..
authors: Zahary G.; Murray D.; Hoare B.
abstract: Open-pit mine reclamation criteria of legal, technical and esthetic nature are reviewed. The types of solid wastes resulting from mining operations are described. The results of research on the possibility of implanting a vegetal cover on highly acidic siliceous residues produced by uranium ore treatment plants at Ellito Lake, Ontario, are presented, demonstrating the success of a program of soil ph neutralization and the addition of nutritive elements.

title: Foreseeable Developments of Mining Techniques in Large Coal-Producing Countries.
authors: Ellie G.
abstract: The research to improve the productivity of coal mining operations basically tend toward finding techniques for reducing the personnel, either by doing away with certain tasks, or by mechanizing and automating certain operations or, yet again, by improving the reliability of the methods and equipment. For conventionally mined deposits such as, first of all, strikes in which the coal is extracted by known open-pit mining processes and also shallow mines having regular horizontal layers, the advances made in modernizing the methods and to which the major world producers are devoting their efforts are especially in the design of cutting, transport and pit propping equipment in order to arrive at ″the less″ workings. The question of exploiting the large coal reserves in difficult and deep deposits is considered. Problems of operational strategy, remote control and monitoring of underground installations are indicated.

title: OPEN-PIT MINING.
authors: Bunch J.
abstract: Problems of permit issuance and renewal and trends in machinery use are discussed. Open-pit miners will continue to take a critical look at equipment replacement and utilization during 1977. Traditional mining methods may be replaced by new procedures which require less fuel and energy. The major consideration in equipment manufacturing will be operating economy rather than expanded capacity. Improved efficiency and economy are the main criteria for competitive extraction and processing of declining ore grades in 1977.

title: Radiation exposures associated with surface mining for uranium
authors: Miller H.
abstract: Measurements of external gamma radiation, radon and radon progeny, and airborne uranium aerosols were made at an operating open-pit mining operation using readily available field survey techniques and instruments. Measurement techniques are discussed. Radiation exposure to various occupational categories, such as excavation equipment operators, truck drivers, equipment maintenance personnel, ore control personnel, and to the engineering staff, is estimated. These estimates are compared to the results of film badge dosimetry. While the average exposure rate was found to be in the order of 0.5 mR/hr±0.5 mR/hr, it was noted that higher exposures (up to lOmR/hr) were measured in the vicinity of ore bodies containing uranium in the per cent range. Some contamination of earth-moving equipment by uranium-bearing dusts was also noted. © 1977 Health Physics Society.

title: OPEN-PIT MINING IN POWDER RIVER.
authors: Jackson D.
abstract: This article deals with Carter Mining Co. 's Rawhide mine, one of the newest and largest (designed for 12 million tpy) coal complexes in the Powder River Basin, which will begin producing coal by the open-pit method, using a truck/shovel/scraper combination. Adoption of the open-pit method was done to gain greater flexibility of operation, easier land reclamation and a reduction in the area of disturbed land. The mine will produce coal from two seams totaling 100 ft in thickness.

title: UNIQUE APPLICATION OF SEISMIC METHODS IN AN OPEN-PIT MINING.
authors: Kim Y.S.; Bailey A.
abstract: A feasibility seismic refraction and reflection field survey was conducted at the U. S. Borax Company open-pit mine, Boron, California by the writers during the weekend of March 13 and 14, 1976. This field survey was carried out as a preliminary investigation primarily for the purpose of evaluating and establishing the ability of such geophysical techniques to locate and outline the subsurface openings of the old room-and-pillar mining under the present open-pit. The value of such knowledge about the old underground workings is directly related to the safe and economical operation of the open-pit mine for the company.

title: MINING ENGINEERING - REVIEW/'75 MINING EXPLORATION MINERAL PROCESSING.
authors: Anon
abstract: Summary reports with extensive bibliographics are presented on geology, geophysics, geochemistry, geological engineering, open-pit mining, underground mining, hydrology, solution mining, rock mechanics, operations research, mineral processing, crushing and grinding, concentration, hydrometallurgy, pyrolysis and agglomeration, materials handling, operating controls, and environmental control.

title: Computer Simulation of an Open-Pit Mining Process.
authors: Tarasiewicz S.
abstract: An approach to the way of forming a simulation model with the use of ″time slicing″ is presented. Before the simulation programmes are worked out the digital models of elementary units and technological structure configuration are formed. Then the model of technological process structure is represented in computer memory. As a result of this procedure a simulation programme for ODRA 1204 computer is worked out and tested. These programmes can be used to analyze mining technological processes of any open-pit mine.

title: Ore-Dressing Combine of the Future with Open-Pit Mining.
authors: Shafarenko I.; Davidyants G.
abstract: The project of a model ore-dressing combine of the future, envisaged for the Chernyanskoye iron ore deposit in the Kursk Magnetic Anomaly Basin is described. Lying under an overburden 160 m deep, its ore reserves down to the projected depth of the open-cast mine of 565 m amount to 1913 Mt, including 176 Mt of rich ore and 1737 Mt of ferrous quartzites. It is planned that the output of the first stage of the mine will be 60 Mt of quartzites and 8 Mt of rich ore. In the more distant future the output of quartzites will be 120 Mt p. a. The overburden rock will be dumped in ravines, covered with top soil, and handed over agricultural use. Slurry will be piped to distances of 10-15 km.

title: PIT SLOPE DISPLACEMENT MONITORING: AN AID TO OPEN-PIT MINE OPERATION.
authors: MacRae A.
abstract: Slope failures exact a large, unpredictable sum from the open-pit mining industry every year, and fatalities and large-scale equipment damage are not the only forms of loss. Direct cost for removal of slide material is considerable, and indirects associated with rescheduling and lost production are significant over the long term. This article describes existing slope displacement monitoring systems and some new developments, including information on system accuracy, range, applicability, and cost, based on the author's past projects. Advantages and disadvantages of the systems are discussed, and suggestions are made for future improvements in this field.

title: DEFORMATION OF A CONTACT-METAMORPHIC ROCK MASS AT LOST RIVER, ALASKA.
authors: Jeremic M.
abstract: The generally accepted principles of rock mechanics are used to explain the failure mechanism of a contact-metamorphic rock mass complex undergoing ellipse stress deformation. The investigation was based on structural data collected in the field and obtained from old mining and exploration reports and studies. The approach used analyzes the rock-mass mechanics resulting from a Cretaceous geological event. It follows a stress ellipse model based on the tectonic forces, the geometry of the rock structure and natural stress induced by the structural dilation. The role of geological structure and induced stress in determining the mechanism and nature of deformation bears on open-pit mining operations. Their influence on the stability of the possible open-pit mine deserves careful attention. 9 refs.

title: CAN ANTHRACITE MAKE A COMEBACK?
authors: Mutchler N.
abstract: Anthracite is overlooked or ignored by many, even as the U. S. turning once again to coal. The problem apparently occurs because it constitutes only 1 percent of U. S. coal resources. However, there are still some 17 billion tons of recoverable anthracite reserves, and this amount can be significant to a utility requiring, for instance, 1 million tons annually, or an industry requiring a fuel substitute of 200,000 tons of coal. The author takes a closer look at the anthracite potential in the U. S. , examines the anthracite's critical constraints and technology for producing methanol, and discusses massive open-pit mining.

title: Functional studies of the circulatory and respiratory apparatus during work in workers occupied in open-pit mining in the foothills
authors: Mambetaliev B.

title: NEW McDERMITT MINE JOINT VENTURE EMERGES AS DOMINANT FORCE IN US MERCURY PRODUCTION.
authors: Sisselman R.
abstract: The only major mercury mine in the US is newly on stream and tuning up to achieve a designed annual throughput of 20,000 flasks of prime virgin metal by the end of 1975. Production from the McDermitt mine in Humboldt County, Nev. , should be ample to supply just under 50% of primary metal requirements of the US, which in 1974 imported 45,000 flasks and produced only 1,200. Moreover, from open-pit mining through furnacing, production will comply with strict environmental and health guidelines established by state and federal agencies. The autogenous grinding mill circuit and the furnace plant are described, as well as several departures from the norm that are evident at the McDermitt mill.

title: DEVELOPMENTS IN MINING MACHINERY.
authors: Gosnell J.
abstract: The latest innovations in underground and open-pit mining in South Africa are reviewed. These developments include the use of hydraulic rock drills in underground gold mines, the use of large rotary drilling machines in open-pit copper and iron mines, boring experiments for recovering gold ore, tests with rock-cutting machines in gold and platinum rock, the use of the impact ripping technique in collieries to excavate without explosives, underground and open-pit blasting operatiions, underground mechanized loading and dumping facilities, draglines for open-pit or strip mining, and rail haulage systems for rock transportation.

title: Mineralogy and origin of the Coalinga asbestos deposit
authors: Mumpton F.A.; Thompson C.S.
abstract: Since 1960 asbestos production of the United States has more than tripled, a phenomenon due in large part to the development of the Coalinga asbestos deposit in western California. Although most asbestos ores contain 5-10 per cent chrysotile in the form of cross- or slip-fiber veins within massive serpentinite bodies, no such veins are to be found in the Coalinga deposit despite the fact that it contains more than 50 per cent recoverable chrysotile. The Coalinga ore consists of soft, powdery, pellet-like agglomerates of finely matted chrysotile surrounding blocks and fragments of serpentinite rock. The highly sheared and pulverized nature of the ore favors its exploitation by simple, open-pit mining, and high quality products can be prepared by either wet or dry milling processes. Four types of serpentine material are distinguishable: (1) hard, dense blocks of serpentinite rock, ranging from fractions of an inch to several tens of feet in diameter; (2) tough, leathery sheets, resembling mountain leather, up to several square feet in size; (3) brittle blades and plates of green serpentine, a few square inches in size; and (4) friable agglomerates of soft, powdery chrysotile containing appreciable amounts of the other three. Chrysotile is the principal component of all the above materials, with the exception of the serpentinite rock which consists mainly of lizardite and/or antigorite, with small amounts of brucite, magnetite, and very short fiber chrysotile. Although chrysotile fibers up to several microns in length are present in the leathery sheets, most Coalinga chrysotile is much shorter and arranged in a swirling mesh or disoriented, tangled fibers, much like cellulose fibers in paper. Fragments of serpentinite gangue are scattered throughout the ore and contain most of the lizardite, antigorite, and brucite. Chemical, electron probe, and X-ray analyses confirm the iron-rich nature of the brucite, a critical factor in the susceptibility of this phase to oxidation in the surface weathering zone. Here brucite either dissolves, leaving behind a residue of brown, amorphous iron oxides, or transforms in situ to pyroaurite or coalingite. Dissolved magnesium precipitates as hydromagnesite immediately above the water table throughout the deposit. The abnormally high chrysotile content of this deposit is probably a result of the intensive shearing that it underwent during or after emplacement. If the friable, chrysotile-rich ore was produced during this pulverization episode, (1) lizardite and/or antigorite in the serpentinite must have been transformed into chrysotile and (2) brucite must have been removed. It is likely that early-formed lizardite/antigorite dissolved in the ground waters which pervaded the highly sheared body and that chrysotile later precipitated from these waters, coating all available surfaces. © 1975.

title: Transport by Rubber Belt Conveyors at the Lignite Open-Pit Facilities in the Serbian Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (SFRJ).
authors: Kun J.
abstract: The author reviews the development of rubber belt conveying at the open-pit mining facilities in Serbia, which dates back to 1965. The total length of conveyor belts in lignite open-pit mining is doubling every five years, and is expected to reach about 180 km in ten years from now, which would represent a tripling over the present level. Length, speed and capacity of the conveyor belts currently in use are shown in tabular form and graphs, and the three basic transportation methods by rubber belt conveyors at the Serbian lignite open-pit mines are described.

title: New Directions of Chemical Processing of Kansk-Achinsk Basin Coal.
authors: Krichko A.; Semenov L.
abstract: Conditions for open-pit mining in Kansk-Achinsk Basin in East Siberia are very favorable. It is possible to mine about 1 billion t of coal per annum by this method. The seams are up to 50-70 m thick. At present 90% of coal mined here is used locally in Krasnoyarsk and Irkutsk regions. Its transportation is economically feasible only at distances well below 2000 km. The distances to the European part of the USSR where energy is required are 4,000-5,000 km, however.
