A strip mine for coal on the east slopes of the Alberta Rockies, occupied during its operations by Rocky Mountain bighorn sheep (Ovis canadensis canadensis, Shaw 1803), was reclaimed as bighorn habitat. By considering the behaviour and habitat requirements of bighorns in conjunction with an operating coal mine and reclamation process, a large coal mining company has been able to reconstruct the mine site restoration to benefit mountain sheep. Although bighorn habitat requirements are well known, it was not until the animal and its requirements were studied against the backdrop of an operating coal mine that obvious recommendations regarding the maintenance and placement of high steep excavated rock faces were made and accepted by the government regulatory agencies. An open pit mine is a devastated landscape; trees, soil and overburden are removed to retrieve coal that may be up to 215 m underground. Overburden and soil are returned, but the disturbance compares to the barren landscapes left behind by glaciers. Contouring of the land, grading of overburden and soil, seeding with grass and legume mixtures and extensive fertilization are designed to speed plant colonization and soil development. By examining the bighorn's biological needs with respect to specific mining operations, a unique opportunity arose to employ McHarg's "design with nature" concept. This approach incorporates environmental and societal values into every aspect of development, and promotes the evaluation of the constraints and opportunities arising. The sheep numbered about 200. Their seasonal movements were similar to those found on native ranges. They used the reclaimed areas as winter range and for the mineral licks exposed during mining; in summer, the sheep moved to nearby alpine areas. Two thirds of all sightings were confined to 1.3 km<sup>2</sup> of reclaimed grassland; its average productivity (4190 kg/ha) exceeded native ranges (1700 kg/ha). The body mass of female sheep in autumn equalled that of the largest in Alberta, but the skull dimensions were not larger than those of adjacent ranges. Infestation with lungworms was moderate. Lamb production and survival were high. Design criteria should be: feeding areas should be dry and lie within 300 m of escape terrain, which should have a slope of 40% and contain at least three benches. Rock piles should be placed on grazing areas. Mineral licks, a vital welfare factor, already existed within the high walls created by strip mining. © 1992 Kluwer Academic Publishers.

title: Hydrogeological Decision Analysis: 3. Application to Design of a Ground‐Water Control System at an Open Pit Mine
authors: Sperling T.; Freeze R.A.; Massmann J.; Smith L.; James B.
abstract: Control of ground water plays an important part in operations at many open pit mines. Selection of an efficient and cost‐effective ground‐water control program is frequently complicated by the complex and somewhat uncertain hydrogeo‐logic environment found at most mine sites. This paper documents a case study of dewatering operations at Highland Valley Copper that shows how risk‐cost‐benefit analysis can be used to identify the best ground‐water control strategy to improve stability of pit walls under such conditions. For each of a specified set of design alternatives, the analysis involves evaluation of an economic objective function, comprised of revenues, operating costs, and monetary risks associated with slope failure. The risk calculation requires an accurate estimate of the probability of slope failure on the pit wall. The calculation involves a coupled, steady‐state, saturated‐unsaturated, finite‐element ground‐water flow model and a limit equilibrium slope stability model. The coupled model is invoked in a conditional Monte Carlo simulation that is based on a geostatistical description of the level of uncertainty inherent in the available hydrogeological and geotechnical data. Although the emphasis in this paper is on identifying the optimum slope angle and ground‐water control strategy for open pit mines, the framework is equally well‐suited to the analysis of design issues for any engineering projects in which the hydrogeological environment plays an important role. Copyright © 1992, Wiley Blackwell. All rights reserved

title: Dragline loading analysis in marine sediment areas of the Syncrude open pit mine
authors: List B.; Czajewski K.
abstract: Draglines are use to excavate ore from atop an operating bench at the Syncrude Canada Ltd, the world's largest oil sand mine operator. Failure of the highwall slope along thin marine clay layers can cause danger and impede productivity of the draglines. Geotechnical investigations were made to better understand the failure mechanisms and thus reduce the negative impact on the dragline production. Optimization of productivity and safety assurance are given emphasis.

title: Single hole test blasting at an open pit mine in full scale: A case study
source: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
authors: Bilgin H.A.
abstract: A study by a series of single hole blasts, slab blasting, in full scale in a large open pit iron mine was conducted to assess the influence of burden on various blast parameters for safe and economical blasting. The paper has described how the full scale tests were performed and how the optimum and critical burden dimensions were determined. The determined optimum and critical burdens were also expressed in terms of bench height and blasthole diameter. Furthermore, the relations established between burden and angle of breakage, volume of broken material, throw and backbreak respectively were given and discussed. The results show that the maximal volume of broken ore was achieved when the burden is almost equal to half the bench height. © 1991, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

title: Practical aspects of availability and reliability management in a large open pit mine
source: Reliability Production and Control in Coal Mines Proc International Conference Wollongong 1991
authors: Golosinski T.
abstract: The large El Cerrejon coal open pit in north east Colombia has been developed over the last decade in a remote, entirely new mining area with hitherto unskilled inhabitants. Now over 200 pieces of heavy equipment operate with high reliability and availability due to successful theoretical training and skill improvement programs tuned to the specific reliability needs of the worksite and environment. The process of continuous improvement adopted promises further competitive advantages of the project. -Author

title: Dispatching system evolution at Chuquicamata Mine
source: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
authors: Lautaro Barros L.
abstract: Since 1976 the Chuquicamata's engineers have been worried about the way for improving the performance of fleets of trucks and shovels. In this paper, we analyse the evolution of the different systems applied in Chuquicamata; also, the ideas involved on each development for reaching the actual state. The purpose for this presentation is the fact that this system has been developed by Chilean engineers, directly, involved on the problems and experiences ocurring at Chuquicamata's Open Pit Mine. © 1991, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

title: Shallow translational failures along thin marine clay layers at the Syncrude Canada Limited open pit mine
authors: List B.; McKenna G.
abstract: Syncrude Canada Limited operates four 70 cu.m draglines which excavate oil sands from below an operating bench and cast the ore into windrows on the mining bench. Excessive differential settlement of the operating pad and failure of the highwall along thin Marine Clay layers within the Cretaceous Upper McMurray Formation can affect the safety and operation of the draglines. Geotechnical investigation of these Marine Sediments has included site investigations, laboratory testing, the monitoring and documentation of over 200 windrow induced translational failures, full scale field tests, and analysis of piezometric and deformation data from around operating drag-lines. The weak Marine Clay layers and the resultant poor trafficability of the Marine Sands have had a significant detrimental impact on dragline productivity including additional pad preparation time, subexcavations, and dragline downtime to read geotechnical instruments. Studies conducted to date have reduced the negative impact on production, and additional work is in progress to further optimize productivity while ensuring a safe and reliable dragline mining operation.

title: Les Mines Selbaie story: Open pit mine
authors: Pageau C.; Caron D.
abstract: The open pit as well as its related services were incorporated into a complex which includes an underground mine and a concentrator. The equipment was chosen with the objective of auto-sufficiency during each phase of mining. The paper outlines the organization and methods used in drilling, blasting, loading, transporting and crushing. The responsibilities of the Engineering Department are also outlined. A short resume of the results obtained as well as suggestions for improvement are provided.

title: Deformation of open pit mine slopes by deep seated toppling
source: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
authors: Martin D.
abstract: The relationships between engineering geology, structural geology, strength properties and failure mechanisms of several large slope failures in western North America are examined. The main failure mechanism identified at each site involves primarily deep seated toppling, Characteristics, diagnostic features and behaviour of each failure are reviewed, Back analyses of two failures using limit equilibrium techniques as well as numerical modelling confirms that the toppling mechanism is extremely sensitive to mining activity and groundwater pressure, Although deep seated toppling failures may involve more than several million tonnes, large deformations of the order of several tens of metres have been documented without catastrophic failure, These deformations are explained from the results of numerical modelling using a distinct element finite difference code. Ongoing research and documentation of such failures is providing a clearer understanding of the deformation behaviour of high rock slopes. © 1990, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

title: Aznalcollar
authors: Fox K.
abstract: Located at the eastern-most end of the Iberian pyrite belt, 40 km northwest of Seville, Spain, the Aznalcollar open pit mine has been in operation since 1979. It is currently producing 3.5 Mt/y of complex pyrite and pyroclastic ores from the open pit operation. Aznalcollar is one of the few complex sulphide orebodies being exploited on the pyrite belt to produce separate lead, zinc and copper concentrates. It also produces flotation pyrite as a byproduct and this is sold for sulphuric acid manufacture.

title: Geology of the fushun coalfield, Liaoning Province, People's Republic of China
authors: Johnson E.A.
abstract: The Fushun coalfield is located in Liaoning Province 45 km east of Shenyang in a relatively small east-west-trending exposure of Mesozoic and Cenozoic rocks surrounded by Precambrian terrane. The coal is included in a sequence of early Tertiary rocks consisting of Paleocene basalt and tuff, and Eocene coal, oil shale and mudstone. These units have been folded into a syncline that plunges gently to the east. The overturned north limb of this fold has been partly removed by a thrust fault. The principal coal beds are low-sulfur subbituminous and bituminous in rank, are of limnic origin, and are contained in the 55-m-thick Eocene Guchengzi Formation. The field, which has been active since the turn of the century, has both open pit and underground mines. The largest operation is the West Open Pit mine, which measures 2.0 km wide, 6.6 km long, and 300 m deep. Coal is mined by means of power shovels, trucks, and an electric rail system. Oil shale from the Eocene Jijuntun Formation is also mined. © 1990.

title: Characterization of overburden soils at Thompson Open Pit Mine
authors: Ramage R.; Slawinski A.; McRoberts E.
abstract: The Thompson Open Pit Mine is currently under development. The North Pit overburden removal program was completed in 1985 and the South Pit overburden removal has been started in 1989 and is currently underway utilizing a suction dredge. Geotechnical investigations were undertaken prior to each overburden removal program to identify the nature and engineering properties of the soils overlying the mineralized bedrock ore zones. Considerable data with respect to soil texture, thicknesses and shear strength was obtained during field investigations and augmented with laboratory testing. Hydrogeological evaluations were undertaken to determine the pore pressure distributions in the overburden soils and to be able to model the existing groundwater regime and the changes to that regime during operation of a dredge and maintenance of a dredge pool.

title: Rampura-Agucha design and development of major lead-zinc project in India. A case history
source: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
authors: Jain B.; Lahiri D.
abstract: A large lead-zinc deposit was discovered during the early 80s at Agucha in Rajasthan in a banded gneissic complex of the Bhilwara Supergroup of Archaean age. Hindustan Zinc Limited began exploration and ore reserves, tonnage and grade were estimated and evaluated. A 3000 tpd open pit mine and beneficiation plant along with other facilities are under development. The project is scheduled to be completed in 1991.

title: Use of the flotation reagent ketgol for flotation of coal from the Neryungrinsk Open Pit Mine
source: Coke Chemistry USSR English Translation of Koks I Khimiya
authors: Deberdeev I.K.; Krasnikova N.A.; Samoilova E.K.
abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate the flotation activity of the reagent KETGOL with respect to coal from the Neryungrinsk Open Pit Mine. This new heteropolar reagent is a byproduct from 2-ethylhexanol production by hydroxy synthesis and has found industrial use at a number of coal concentration plants. It is shown that the use of KETGOL offers the possibility of increasing the yield of concentrate by 2.5% with a slight increase in ash content. We should note that the ash content of the floated material at the concentration plant is 16%, and the ash content of the investigated sample was 16.75%. An additional advantage of the reagent is its lower consumption in comparison with diesel fuel and combined feed of reagents is eliminated.

title: Investigation of the feasibility of using coals from the Chernigov open pit mine for production of foundry coke
source: Coke Chemistry USSR English Translation of Koks I Khimiya
authors: Zaostrovskii A.; Balabanova N.; Dinel't V.; Zlatin L.; Shved V.
abstract: The coals of the Chernigov open pit mine (Volkovskii seam) are arbitrarily classified as grade SS, although according to their main indices they are actually coking coals of grade K2. they are characterized by higher caking properties in comparison with coals from the Sudzhensk Concentration Plant, a higher content of the sum of caking components according to petrographic analysis and reduced ash content (at a mean annual ash content of 8.7%). The yield of volatiles is somewhat higher. Introduction of as much as 40% coals from the Volkoskii seam to the charge of the Kemerovo Plant leads to an increase in yield of volatiles by 1-3.5% and a reduction in ash content by 0.5-1.5%. The caking properties of the charges, characterized by the thickness of the plastic layer Y, lie in the range 12-14 mm, remaining at the level of the similar charge on the average (variant 1). The strength of the lump coke according to index M<inf>40</inf> from charges with participation of coals from the Volkovskii seam of the Chernigov open pit mine increased by 0.03-1%, while the abradability according to index M<inf>10</inf> diminished by an average of 0.5%. The structural strength of the coke declined slightly, obviously because of the increase in porosity of the experimental cokes.

title: Curved conveyor system connecting an open pit mine with a power station
authors: Bruewer T.
abstract: In western Turkey a downhill long distance conveyor system with horizontal and vertical curves was designed and built by Krupp Industrietechnik and the Turkish company Gama Endustri Tesisleri. The exact planning of the route of this conveyor system was only possible with the aid of a CAD system and a simulation program for conveyors. The latest drive technology and controlled brake and pretensioning systems enable uncritical system behavior to be achieved in all load and operating conditions. The first year of operation confirmed the expectations the customer had of the system.

title: Truck dispatching in an open pit mine
source: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
authors: Soumis F.; Ethier J.; Elbrond J.
abstract: In an open pit mine operated by trucks and shovels, the trucks should be dispatched from the crusher to the shovels in such a way that the productivity of trucks and shovels in maximized while maintaining a rational production plan as well as obtaining target grades and other objectives with small variations at the entrance to the concentrator. To solve the dispatching problem we present a three step approach. First we select shovel locations with a man-machine interactive system. This step combines operator expertise and linear programming optimisation. In the second step, we establish an optimal strategy (production plan) for a certain period of time by solving a network problem with non-linear costs associated with estimates of trucks’ and shovels’ waiting times and the quality objectives. The solution gives, for each shovel, the best access paths, the trucks’ and shovels’ estimated waiting times and an estimate of the number of trucks loaded per unit of time. In the last step we dispatch each truck in real-time by solving an assigment problem, taking into account the next 15 trucks, which are becoming available for dispatching in order to get a series of dispatches which will realize the optimal strategy. © 1989, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

title: Fragmentation systems design in surface mines: An expert system application
source: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
authors: Paul J.; Gershon M.
abstract: Mining Engineers in charge of open pit mine planning very often face decision making situations dealing with the selection of the most economical method for the removal of overburden. Ripping versus conventional drilling and blasting are the options considered. The choice of a particular overburden removal method depends upon the physicomechanical properties of the overburden material as well as the various cost factors involved in the process. The analysis of technoeconomical factors, related to different methods of overburden removal in surface mines, needs detailed study and investigation by a technical expert. The expert system “FRAGMENTATION” has been developed to help and expedite the decision making process involving the selection of overburden removal method in surface mines. Furthermore, this expert system can be used for detailed design of overburden removal in open pit mines, specifically for determining charge geometry placement and cost analysis. © 1989, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

title: The influence of mining adjacent deposits on rock pressure dynamics in the Khibini Massif
authors: Kozyrev A.; Savtchenko S.
abstract: A finite element method is used to study the problem of the stressed state of a rock mass when deposits are developed, in two underground mines and an open pit mine. The stress state of the initial rock mass and at the following stages of mining are discussed. When large volumes of rock mass are mined out under high tectonic stresses, the reciprocal influence of mining of adjacent deposits on the stress state of the rock mass is shown to be substantial. As a result, technogenous earthquakes, rock bursts and rock mass movements along natural jointing planes take place. -from Authors

title: An application of discrete mathematics in the design of an open pit mine
authors: Caccetta L.; Giannini L.
abstract: The determination of the "optimum pit limit" of a mine is considered to be a fundamental problem in mine planning as it provides information which is essential in the evaluation of the economic potential of a mineral deposit, and in the formulation of long-, intermediate-, and short-range mine plans. A number of mathematical techniques have been proposed to solve this problem, some of the more elaborate ones posing considerable computational problems. In this paper we discuss the development and implementation of a graph-theoretic technique originally proposed by Lerchs and Grossman. Our implementation strategy involves the use of a dynamic programming technique to "bound" the optimum. © 1988.

title: WORLD'S LARGEST HYDRAULIC SHOVEL, O&K'S RH 300, NOW OPERATING AT CHUQUICAMATA, WORLD'S LARGEST COPPER MINE.
authors: O'Neil T.
abstract: The O&K RH 300 hydraulic excavator has been put into service to move overburden and mine ore at the Chuquicamata open pit mine of the Chilean state copper mining company, Corporacion Nacional de Cobre de Chile (Codelco). The hydraulic excavator is the second of these units to be put into use. The other unit operates at Northern Strip Mining's open pit coal operation in England.

title: Role of geotechnical engineering in the development and operation of Syncrude's open pit mine and tailings pond
authors: Fair A.
abstract: The Syncrude Canada Ltd. open pit mine and tailings pond, located near Fort McMurray in northern Alberta, represent two of the largest operations of their kind anywhere in the world. This paper is intended to provide an overview of the geotechnical role in the development and operation of the Syncrude project. The paper chronicles the geotechnical input into the project, beginning with the large scale test pits which were utilized to provide a basis for mine equipment selection and to evaluate highwall performance. Sophisticated instrumentation monitoring programs were developed to ensure the ongoing safety of major equipment operating along the highwall crest. The location and orientation of the pit have had a major impact on highwall performance. Considerable effort has also been devoted to understanding the unique material properties of the oil sand. Design of the tailings dyke has been based on the observational approach. Consequently, geotechnical parameters and monitoring programs continue to regulate the design and ensure the successful completion of the dykes. More recently, risk assessment studies, based on geotechnical considerations, are being utilized to help assess optimum operating strategies for both the tailings pond and highwall slopes. A comparison of the original geotechnical concerns with present day performance is also presented in the paper.

title: Case examples and developments in open pit mine stability
authors: Brawner C.
abstract: The reduced demand for coals and many minerals has led to substantial advances in geomechanics which are aimed at ensuring efficiency and reduce mining costs. These advances can provide major economic and safety benefits in various areas of surface mining in the near future. Stability on surface mining projects is primarily dependent on five factors. These include structural geology, groundwater, blasting and the existence of weak layers, particularly clayey gouge or clay infill. Case examples of stability on many surface mines including coal mines are presented in this paper.

title: COAL OF THE CHERNIGOVSKII OPEN PIT MINE - AN ADDITIONAL RESOURCE OF COAL FOR COKING.
source: Coke and Chemistry U S S R
authors: Zolotukhin Y.; Kukolev Y.; Eremin A.; Kachaev V.; Fon M.; Naimark M.; Stankevich A.
abstract: Screenings of coal from the Chernigovskii Open Pit Mine may be used in coking charges if coal from section no. 1, produced in a zone of partial oxidation, is excluded in the processing of the washery of the integrated plant. In order to improve the properties of the charge, particularly to increase its shrinkage properties, it is desirable to fully replace the type OS coal of the Sibirginskii Open Pit Mine with screenings of coal of the Chernigovskii Open Pit Mine in the quantity of 10% of the run-of-mine charge. The effect of the screenings on all the operating indices of the coking plant should be determined in greater detail. Coal of the Chernigovskii Open Pit Mine may be considered a good feedstock for production of low-phosphorus coke.

title: Testing the Possibility of Combusting Open Pit Mine Moscanica Coal - Zenica.
authors: Vuletic V.
abstract: The paper presents the results of full-scale testing of coal from openpit mine Moscanica, belonging to the brown coal mines Zenica in order to define the possibility of its industrial use, within the framework or activities related to opening and start-up of the openpit Moscanica deposit. Testing was carried out in the fireplace of a section boiler with a flat crawling grain in power generating plant at Zenica.

title: U. S. BORAX.
authors: Anon
abstract: Boron-containing compounds are used in the manufacture of heat-resistant glass, fibreglass, porcelain, enamel, ceramics, soaps and detergents, fire retardents and other products. Worldwide demand for borates is about 975,000 t/y B//2O//3, of which the U. S. A. supplies about 60%. Over half this is produced by the United States Borax & Chemical Corporation, a wholly-owned subsidiary of RTZ. U. S. Borax operates an open pit mine at Boron in the Mojave Desert.

title: Indicator kriging for unit vectors: Rock joint orientations
authors: Young D.S.
keywords: directional data | indicator kriging | rock joint orientation | spherical distribution | two-dimensional cutoff system
abstract: Indicator kriging (IK) is extended to analyze three-dimensional random unit vectors and evaluate the local probability distribution of rock joint orientations in geological formations. The pole vector representing joint orientations is regionalized and projected on a plane normal to the mean attitude of the joint family and centered at the mean. A two-dimensional cutoff system is developed to define the indicator variable, and corresponding indicator variograms and indicator kriging. The cutoff system defines probability regions similar to those of a bivariate distribution, concentric rings sliced into radial sectors. A case study made on an open pit mine proved positively the efficiency of IK and encourages its applications to localized probabilistic structural modeling for geotechnical or geohydrological analysis and oil and gas reservoir analysis. © 1987 International Association for Mathematical Geology.

title: OPTIMIZATION OF OPEN PIT SHORT- AND LONG-RANGE PRODUCTION SCHEDULING.
authors: Fytas K.; Pelley C.; Calder P.
abstract: A computer model has been developed which is capable of evaluating alternative production schedules (long- and short-range) of an open pit mine once the ultimate pit limits have been defined. The model user can choose the best alternative according to cash flow considerations and the particular mining conditions. The model involves a combination of simulation for long-range production scheduling and linear programming for short-range scheduling.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF A NEW AUSTRALIAN GOLD MINE.
authors: Anon
abstract: Late last year gold production began at Mount Leyshon open pit mine in Northern Queensland following the commissioning of heap leaching facilities on site. Once full scale operation is reached, the mine is expected to move some 1Mt/y mineralized material, producing 46,000 oz/y gold in its first three years of production. Mt. Leyshon represents an investment of A13. 5 million (A equals POUND 2. 3) for its owners, Pan Australian Mining Ltd, a young and developing Australian mining company. Current ore reserves are reported to be 6. 3 Mt grading 1. 8g/t gold and 4. 8g/t silver, and Pan Aust are confident that these will increase substantilly, with additions to both the oxide and primary ore reserve, 'significantly extending the mine life'.

title: Comparing Calculations with Measurement Results for Pulverized Lignite Flame.
authors: Modlinski Z.; Molatka A.; Karcz H.
abstract: Calculation results obtained with the aid of an electronic data processing facility regarding the combustion of pulverized lignite from the Brieske open pit mine (East Germany) in the swirling flame of an experimental burner are presented. The test results presented in earlier papers have been utilized in the flame model. Kinetic constants are derived. The calculation results obtained are compared with experimental results obtained from the flame. The results coincide qualitatively.

title: The use of dynamic programming for open pit mine design: Some practical implications
authors: Wright E.
abstract: Determining the optimum ultimate-pit limits can be justified when analysing low-grade and/or inhomogeneous surfacial deposits. Such deposits require investigations of a range of ultimate pits for correct economic judgement. A prerequisite for such economic analyses is a fast and accurate method for determining the multiple pit shells to be analysed. Dynamic Programming (DP) offers an advantageous alternative to both the Lerchs-Grossman algorithm and the moving-cone method, for the design of the multiple pits required for such economic sensitivity analyses. This paper examines some of the practical aspects involved in using dynamic programming for ultimate pit design (UPD). The basics are discussed and some DP proposals are reviewed. The question of the optimum ultimate pit versus the practical need for generating acceptable non-optimum pits, using minimum computing times and core storage, is examined. Results from tests with various refinements of the 3-dimensional dynamic programming approach for ultimate pit design proposed by Wilke and Wright are discussed. The indication is that ultimate-pit results, which, in terms of total economic values, are no worse than those designed by the moving-cone method, can be obtained with the modified approaches using only fractions of the computing times required by the moving-cone method. © 1987 Elsevier Science Publishers B.V.

title: Microseismic data processing associated with monitoring of mine slope instabilities
authors: Stuart N.; Vladut T.
abstract: Microseismic monitoring in open pit operations has been carried out at the Cardinal River Mine near Hinton, Alberta. The target region was an extremely extensive slope in highly tectonised, jurassic, coal bearing strata. The project was experimental in nature. The aim of this data flow analysis is to examine the possibility of using certain parameters as a prediction of failure, to examine where improvements seem possible in the system and how the results might be used in conjunction with other types of monitoring that are currently, or might potentially be used at Cardinal River or other open pit mine operations.

title: STUDY OF THE POSSIBILITY OF REPLACING COKE WITH LEAN COAL IN AGGLOMERATION OF PHOSPHORITES.
source: Coke Chemistry USSR English Translation of Koks I Khimiya
authors: Puzankov V.; Zoteeva A.; Trefilov V.; Gordeeva L.; Borisova M.; Nechaeva G.; Zhuravleva D.; Alybaev Z.; Kuz'min S.
abstract: The authors give the results of investigations to more correctly determine the agglomeration parameters of phosphorites, the indices of the process, and the quality of the product, when using coal from the Krasnogorsk Open Pit mine from the zone of thermal contact metamorphism, characterized by complete absence of tars. The results of the investigations provided support for the previously demonstrated possibility of full equivalent (by carbon) substitution of metallurgical coal in agglomeration of phosphorites with Krasnogorsk coal. It was shown that the parameters and indices of the process, as well as the product quality, are similar when this substitution is made.

title: STUDY OF THE BEHAVIOR OF NERYUNGRA COAL IN COKING CHARGES.
source: Coke Chemistry USSR English Translation of Koks I Khimiya
authors: Shreider E.M.; Mishin E.N.; Partina T.V.; Konovalova Y.V.; Kotov A.P.; Toletova V.A.
abstract: It is shown that use of 10% coal from the Neryungra Open Pit Mine in place of (type OS, SS, K) Kuznetsk coal decreased the yield of cleaned charge (by 1. 5%) with a simultaneous increase in its ash (by an average of 0. 64%). There was an increase in the losses of coal with the tailings and middlings. It is technologically infeasible to clean Neryungra coal together with coal from the Pechora and Kuznetsk Coalfields. The ash of the coke from the charge containing Neryungra coal rose by an average of 0. 7%. However, the total strength of the coke increased slightly. With the commissioning of a washery at the open pit mine using dense media (expected ash of the concentrate less than 9. 5%) it will be feasible to conduct additional studies on the possibility of use of the concentrate as an admixture to coal charges.

title: REVIEW AND SUGGESTION FOR SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH WORK ON MINE AUTOMATION IN CIMR.
source: Changsha Kuangshan Yanjiuyuan Jikan Quarterly of the Changsha Institute of Mining Research
authors: Zhang Y.
abstract: The author summarizes the major achievements on mine automation research work of CIMR in the past 30 years. Suggestions on the direction of research work and measures that should be required for developing underground and open pit mine automation of China in the future.

title: EMPIRICAL VALUATION OF A PROCESS TO HOMOGENIZE BROWN COAL PROPERTIES AT STORAGE YARDS OF THE BELCHATOW OPEN PIT MINE.
authors: Lazowski A.
abstract: The method of investigating the process of homogenizing brown coal properties at storage yards of the Belchatow open pit mine is described and the results discussed in detail. The estimated values of the degrees of inhomogeneity and homogeneity of the brown coal are given, the latter being the quality coefficient of the investigated process.

title: RECENT DEVELOPMENTS IN OPEN PIT MINE DESIGN AND PLANNING.
source: Journal of the Institution of Engineers India Mining Engineering Division
authors: Bose A.
abstract: Ultimate open pit mine designs originally required many months of effort. With the advent of computers, such manual efforts have greatly reduced. In all advanced countries, surface mine design is invariably computer assisted. The paper discusses a few concepts and techniques being adopted for open pit mine design.

title: Preliminary design of a deep open pit mine ( Bukit Asam): an exercise in the engineering method.
source: Geotechnical Stability in Surface Mining Proc Symposium Calgary 1986
authors: Shields D.
abstract: Initial planning for the development of an open pit coal mine in Sumatra, Indonesia, required detailed appraisal of the difficult geotechnical conditions at the site. One preliminary mine plan called for a pit 180 m deep; all plans involved pits at least 140 m deep. It was important that the pit slopes be as steep as possible to minimize costs; on the other hand, care had to be taken to ensure the slopes would not be so steep that they would be unsafe. -from Author

title: Escondida: evolution of a mine plan.
authors: Hickman R.N.
abstract: The various phases involved in the mine planning for the Escondida deposit in N Chile are described. Initial plans considered underground development as well as an open pit mine. A final decision was made to proceed with a 35 000 tonnes per day operation. The size of the operation was influenced by an analysis of the growth of copper consumption, by the need to obtain financing and by the availability of such financing. Much of the mine planning was done by hand and later refined by computer methods. Escondida is the best copper project in the world; its development programme and mine planning effort provide a classic example of the relationship between the various business and physical factors required for successful mine development.-J.M.H.

title: A method for evaluating the energy characteristics of the air in an open pit mine
authors: Baklanov A.A.

title: Determination of Criteria for Selection of Safety Factors for Coal Open Pit Mine Slopes.
authors: Obradovic R.; Ilic D.
abstract: The criteria for selection of safety factors of coal open pit mine slopes are differently treated and variably defined in preparation of investment technical documentation. The paper deals with additional factors such as the operating stage, flow sheet characteristics, proximity of important facilities and measures undertaken for artificial improvement of stability. A general safety factor corrected F //g//e//n//e//r//a//l, is defined on the basis of additional criteria. After opening of the deposit and the additional study of existing natural conditions, corrections of slope angles and other additional calculations should be made in the basis of investigations and monitoring of the slope state.

title: APPLICATION OF BUCKET WHEEL EXCAVATORS IN A PHILIPPINE CONTINUOUSLY OPERATED OPEN PIT MINE.
authors: Wimmer K.
abstract: The present paper describes the geological and hydrological conditions of the Unong deposit situated in the Southeast of the Semirara island, approx. 270 km south of Manila. Also, the planning of the open pit mine will be dealt with in detail and the technical data of the equipment will be given. All equipment has been installed during an erection period of twelve months. Production - in three-shift operation - was started in mid 1984.

title: Mass Rates of Combustion of Brown Coal Dust from the Brieske Open Pit Mine.
authors: Karcz H.; Malotka A.; Zembrzuski M.
abstract: The problem of determination of the coal grain burning rate has not yet been completely solved theoretically. It is therefore necessary to determine this value experimentally. One of the simplest and most reliable methods is the experiment which is based on the determination of the combustion times of grains of a certain size and a certain mass. The research material obtained is a basis for devising a calculation method that would permit determination of mass rates of individual coal combustion phases. The calculation formulas presented describe the fundamental physicochemical phenomena of the combustion process which it was possible to measure under the given experimental conditions and with the measuring equipment employed.

title: Locating Equidistant Elevations in the Open Pit Mines.
authors: Noaghi T.; Padure I.
abstract: The authors present an improved method for locating equidistant elevations on the bermes of an open pit mine, in order to evaluate the volumes for production monitoring. A mathematical model for specifying the elevation and determination of elevation intersections with a topographic polygonal contour, without prviously imposed conditions, is described.

title: AUTOMATION OF BUCKET WHEEL EXCAVATORS.
source: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
authors: Mason E.
abstract: The requirement to operate bucket wheel excavators closer to the limits of theoretical effective capacity without causing overloads as well as the requirement to generate a stable material flow at any defined level up to design capacity have increased the demand for automated bucket wheel excavators. A continuous 10-year period of development with automatic excavators in the open pit mine has yielded the current version of the automation system consisting of a basic automatic with diagnostic system and options for laser bed leveling and laser output volume. With the present automation system, operational stoppages have been reduced, and it is possible to define any stable material flow up to the design capacity of the excavator. In addition, the material flow has to a large degree become independent of negative weather influences such as rain and fog.

title: Designing Rows of Filter Wells with the Aid of the TAFEGA II Computer Program.
authors: Haenel U.; Hoentzsch J.
abstract: The article describes the EDV-Program TAFEGA II for open pit mine drainage. The program is based on the simulation of boundary conditions of the pipe flow method. The geohydraulic models are successfully developed by this program.

title: Open-pit mine planning and computerized evaluation of china clay reserves in Devon and Cornwall.
source: High Heat Production Hhp Granites Hydrothermal Circulation and Ore Genesis
authors: Howe J.H.; Smith L.J.; Varcoe C.
abstract: A continuous programme of drilling has been conducted since the mid 1950's, resulting in a vast data base, constantly expanding and becoming increasingly difficult to handle. A computerized reserve evaluation system was considered essential to enable a quick response and a detailed and continual update of the Company's reserves. Because of the increasing requirement for sophisticated open-pit mine planning, a multi-disciplinary team was formed to handle all aspects of open pit mine planning; including geology, reserves, mining engineering, slope stability, design draughting and economics. -J.M.H.

title: INDIA'S FIRST LONG-DISTANCE PHOSPHATE SLURRY PIPELINE SYSTEM.
authors: Paliwal H.; Sharma R.
abstract: The 10. 5 km long pipeline located south-east of Udaipur in the State of Rajasthan, India, connects the mine site of Maton and the Phosphoric Acid Plant at the Debari Zinc Smelter. The entire project includes an open pit mine, a beneficiation plant, a pipeline with pump station at Maton and terminal facilities at the phosphoric acid plant located at Debari for feeding slurry directly to the phosphoric acid plant.

title: Experience in internal overburden disposal at Pyatikhatki open pit mine
authors: Makeev G.; Guglya V.; Bur'yan I.

title: Open Pit Landslides Calculations.
authors: Fenk J.
abstract: The article presents solutions to empirical equations for calculation of the landslide probabilities and volumes of a coal open pit mine with high water table.

title: RECENT DEVELOPMENTS AT THE SCHEELITE MINE IN MITTERSILL.
authors: Spross M.
abstract: Since the discovery of the scheelite deposit at Mittersill in 1967, this mining operation has become one of the largest in the western world. The open pit mine will be closed in 1985 so that the total production of 450,000-500,000 tons is expected to be mined underground. Indications on the ore reserves as of December, 1983, are made. In 1981/1982, a conveyor tunnel between mill and mine was built. The whole crushing plant will be transferred underground so that in the future a material no larger than 15 mm is delivered to the preparation plant on a belt conveyor. A new tailings pond was built near Stuhlfelden, 10 km from the ore preparation plant. Operating data for the slurry pipeline which has been in operation since 1983 are given.

title: Geometry of the Pinoasa Open Pit Mine, Bucketwheel Excavator Mining Technology Applied in an Area of an Exploited Mine.
authors: Staicus I.
abstract: The author reviews various aspects of mining a raw field via the open pit method and the problems involved in working a previously exploited mine.

title: Role of Rock Mechanics in the Development of Optimal Open Pit Technology and for the Development of New Open Pit Mine Equipment.
authors: Gehrisch M.; Klahn H.
abstract: The article discusses the effects of local rock mechanics on the development and optimization of new open pit coal mining methods and mine equipment.

title: Noise Control Planning of Open Pit Mine Equipment.
source: Gluckauf Die Fachzeitschrift Fur Rohstoff Bergbau Und Energie
authors: Reiser P.; Baerendorf B.
abstract: The environmental protection laws in Federal Republic of Germany requiring noise control in coal mining operations. Open pit operations with frequent blastings, excavating operations and haulage are abundant noise sources, and constant subject of neighborhood complaints.

title: Energy and water savings in the handling of mine tailing slurries.
authors: Sellgren A.
abstract: The study shows how mineral tailings slurries when transported at a low water content can save large amounts of energy and water. A Swedish underground mine extracting talc, lead, copper and zinc and an open pit mine are taken as examples. (P.J.B.)

title: Crustal structure of southwestern Montana and east‐central Idaho: Results of a reversed seismic refraction line
authors: Sheriff S.D.; Stickney M.C.
abstract: On October 20, 1982, we collected seismic refraction data on a 250 km line segment between Butte, Montana and Challis, Idaho. These data are from two open pit mine blasts; one at Anaconda Minerals Companys' southeast Berkely pit and the other at Cyprus Mines Corporations' Thompson creek mine. Eight of our ten recorders wrote clear records of both blasts with measured travel times accurate to +/−0.2 seconds. We supplemented these data with data from permanent stations in the Butte area. The Pg (crustal) velocity is 5.8 km/s to the southwest and 6.0 km/s to the northeast. The Pn (mantle) velocity is 7.9 km/s to the northeast and 8.1 km/s to the southwest; total travel‐times are equal. The S‐wave velocity in the crust is about 3.5 km/s. The symmetry of the travel‐time results, with their intersection within one kilometer of the midpoint between the pit blasts, strongly suggests the refraction line overlies a horizontal Moho or parallels the strike line of a dipping Moho surface. These data indicate the crust in southwestern Montana and east‐central Idaho is approximately 33 km thick. Contrasting tectonic processes, compression and thickening during the Laramide orogeny with extension and thinning since the Paleocene, resulted in a crust with slightly less than normal thickness. Copyright 1984 by the American Geophysical Union.

title: SAFETY IS A BARGAIN AT KIDD CREEK MINE.
authors: Turnbull A.
abstract: Kidd Creek began operations as an open pit mine, but now runs two shafts in a blast-stope operation, with about 2800 employees in the mine and a 4800 tpd mill and smelter. Its safety record is considerably lower than the Ontario Mines Average Injury Frequency.

title: NYCO STRENGTHENS OPERATION WITH NEW MINE, CRUSHING PLANT.
authors: Herod S.
abstract: To maintain its position as a leading world processor and supplier of wollastonite, NYCO, a division of Processed Minerals, Inc. , headquartered at Willsboro in northern New York, recently carried out the development of an open pit mine at Lewis to replace an underground mine nearing final depletion.

title: Power supply for open-pit operations in magnezit' combine
authors: Pleshkov V.; Kolesnik I.
abstract: The elements and electrical equipment of open pit mine distribution networks produced by domestic industry require further improvement for the purpose of increasing their reliability, simplicity, and safety in servicing under open pit mine conditions. It is necessary to constantly increase the quality of design of power supply equipment of open pit mines. © 1984 Plenum Publishing Corporation.

title: On the computation of resection results by least squares
authors: Corbyn J.A.
abstract: Position fixing by resection within a surveyed area requires a minimum of instrument work and a considerable amount of calculation. A computer/desktop calculator method is described which involves a least square solution and reconciliation between the various sources of error. This is intended to overcome the principal drawback to the use of resection; the practical difficulty with the calculations when more than three points are observed and when the observed points are at widely differing distances. Applications are given in open pit mine surveying and determination of ground movements for slope stability work. © 1983 Maney Publishing.

title: HARDWARE, SOFTWARE, AND SYSTEM CONSIDERATIONS IN COMPUTER-BASED OPEN PIT MINE TRUCK DISPATCHING.
authors: Baker M.R.; Coburn J.W.; White J.W.
abstract: Modular hardware and software subsystems can be integrated to obtain a functioning, field-supportable computer-based system for optimal dispatching of haulage vehicles in an open pit mine. However, the task is much more complicated than it appears. Here are considered key aspects of the problem using an example the DISPATCH system installed at the Tyrone mine of the Phelps Dodge Corporation.

title: Pulsation Torques of an Induction Slip Ring Motor with a Pulse Controlled Resistance in the Rotor Circuit.
authors: Chura V.
abstract: The article presents the theory needed for the design of a computer program for an exact computation of pulsation torques. A simple formula is also derived for the approximate determination of the amplitude of the pulsation torque at the slip s equals 1/6 when the pulsation torque attains large values. An example of the calculation of pulsation torques is presented for a 6 kv, 200 kw motor considered for the drive of transport belts in an open pit mine. Although there exists possibilities for an effective limitation of pulsation torques, they increase the costs of the drive as well as the electrical and machine complexity of the drive.

title: NEW BUCKET WHEEL RECLAIMER FOR EUROPE'S BIGGEST ELECTRIC POWER CENTRE.
authors: Dette A.
abstract: The bucket wheel reclaimer will be operating the coal stockpile situated between the open pit mine and the power station, and as of September 1983 will continuously reclaim the coal from the stockpile at a daily output of 120,000 t. The bucket wheel reclaimer has been designed on the basis that the machine will normally be operating by the side block digging method and will load a conveyor system taking the coal away. However, full block operation will also be possible.

title: Utilization of Burden Rock of Coal Deposits.
authors: Ratynskii V.
abstract: About 1. 5 billion t of burden rock were dumped in the USSR in 1979. Using the example of the Angrenskiy open pit mine the possibilities of utilizing the burden rock are considered. In particular, utilization of kaolin, clays, limestone and gypsum as well as other minerals is discussed.

title: Seismicity of large explosions in karagai open pit mine of magnesite combine
authors: Davydenko A.I.; Kokorev N.A.; Ivanov A.D.; Lesnikov V.V.; Chistyakov Y.N.; Shkuropatov V.N.

title: A feasibility study for controlling groundwater around an open pit mine with slurry trench cutoff.
authors: Haug M.D.; Gerwick B.C.
abstract: The technical feasibility of controlling groundwater around an existing open pit uranium mine in Northern Saskatchewan by means of a slurry trench cutoff around the excavation is evaluated. (from authors' abstract)

title: Genecological investigations on zinc plants. V. Barriers to gene flow limiting the introgression of Viola arvensis (Murr.) into Viola calaminaria Lej. ssp. westfalica (Lej.) Ernst ( Blankenrode, West Germany).
authors: Kakes P.
abstract: Hybrids of V. arvensis (annual) and V. calaminaria (perennial) are found on an open pit mine near Blankenrode (W. Germany). Morphological as well as karyological studies show that these hybrids represent different generations of selfing and/or backcrossing to V. calaminaria. The hybrids show a low Zn tolerance. F<inf>1</inf> and F<inf>2</inf> hybrids have a higher fitness than V. calaminaria if both are grown in normal soil. This is caused by hybrid vigour and by a combination of the reproductive strategies of the parent species. When the progenies of hybrid plants are cultivated together with V. calaminaria in soil with Zn added to it, no difference in reproductive capacity is shown. -from Author

title: COMPUTERS IN MINING: PROGRESS AND PITFALLS.
authors: Stokes W.
abstract: This article reviews the progress made in the last twenty years in the application of computers to ore reserve estimation and open pit mine planning. It explains why it is still difficult to find appropriate software for a problem. The answer lies partly in the difficulty of fitting technical computing into a data processing department and partly in the rapid change in hardware. Much of the existing software is too rigid in structure and cannot be easily adapted to particular needs. The general characteristics of a new generation of mining software, already under development should solve a number of current problems according to the author.

title: ERDENET - WORLD'S NEWEST PORPHYRY COPPER-MOLY MINE.
authors: ARGALL G.
abstract: A NEW OPEN PIT MINE AND 44,000 TON-PER-DAY PORPHYRY COPPER-MOLYBDENUM MILL IS NOW IN OPERATION IN MONGOLIA BY A COOPERATIVE SOVIET-MONGOLIAN PROGRAM. THE PORPHYRY DEPOSIT AVERAGES0. 85 PERCENT COPPER AND 0. 016 PERCENT MOLYBDENUM.

title: Prospects of Development of the Ekibastuz Deposit.
authors: Tomakov P.; Variichuk M.
abstract: Based on a multivariant analysis, a succession of steps of transition from multiple coal pits to a single large open pit mine in the Ekibastuz basin is determined. The open pit mine will be 600 in deep and will produce 150 Mt of coal per annum. The transportation coal will be carried out by 9 railroad branch lines, each successively going deeper into the mine and linked to different railroad stations.

title: PINSON MINE: A CARLIN TYPE GOLD DEPOSIT.
authors: Antoniuk T.; Crombie D.
abstract: The Pinson property is located in Humboldt County in Nevada. The open pit mine and 1000 tpd mill were brought into production in January 1981. The article describes mineralization and reserves.

title: NEW DEVELOPMENTS IN CONTINUOUS MINING AND MATERIALS HANDLING.
authors: Rixen W.
abstract: Bulk mining and handling technologies have been affected in two ways by the soaring cost of oil and oil products in recent years. The substitution of oil by coal, oil sands and oil shale demands the development of high-capacity mining and handling equipment, and the rising fuel costs favor a trend away from cost-intensive heavy truck transport. To cope with the growing volumes of material in mining and handling, larger equipment units have to be designed. This tendency becomes apparent from the examples of the Hambach open pit mine in Germany. A combination of the flexibility of heavy truck transport and the cost advantages of belt conveyors is achieved by the system of semi-mobile crushing installations described in this paper.

title: On the mechanism and process of slope deformation in an open pit mine
source: Rock Mechanics Felsmechanik Mecanique Des Roches
authors: Wang S.
abstract: On the Mechanism and Process of Slope Deformation in an Open Pit Mine: This paper presents an example of slide-toppling deformation in the slope of Jinchuan open pit mine. The composite mechanism and deformation process are controlled by the tabular-blocky structure of a faulted rock mass. The rheologic behaviour is found to be consistent with a three stage creep law and can be expressed by an exponential function. The results of field investigations and long-term observations demonstrate that the time-dependent deformation of rock masses is essentially related to creep along faults and other weak surfaces. © 1981 Springer-Verlag.

title: THREE Cu ORE TYPES MINED AT BAIYIN OPEN PIT MINE.
authors: Argall G.
abstract: 2. 0 percent copper on average is mined from two open pits at this Chinese operation. Shafts are being sunk to access underground mineralization.

title: AUTOMATIC TRUCK DISPATCH COMES OF AGE.
authors: Anon
abstract: The Automatic Truck Identification and Dispatching (ATID) system increases the productivity of open pit mine assets (trucks, shovels, crushers). The system described is being used at the Mount Wright iron ore mine of Quebec Cartier Mining Company in Labrador.

title: GOLDEN OPPORTUNITIES FOR MODULAR CONSTRUCTION.
authors: Zambon D.
abstract: This paper describes how using modular construction a chemical plant has been built for the production of crude oil from Canadian oil sands. The construction project included: an open pit mine, hot water extraction plant, and hydration/demineralization and bitumen upgrading facilities. The main objective of the facilities was to mine the tar sands, separating out the bitumen and upgrading it to a marketable, mineral-free, lighter synthetic crude oil at the production rate of 125,000 bbl (20,000 m**3)/d. Some of the project data are given. By using the modular techniques described, the construction schedule has been cut down by at least two months, thus bringing significant savings.

title: Surface and Underground Drainage in an Open Pit Mine of Gaspe Mines, Murdochville, Quebec.
authors: Liard A.; Sauriol G.; Sommelet H.
abstract: Hydrogeologic and hydrology studies were undertaken in order to design a mine drainage system.

title: SUCCESSFUL METHOD OF SAMPLING AND TESTING HIGHLY FRACTURED MATERIAL, USING LARGE DIAMETER CORE.
authors: Lockhart C.W.; Lumsden A.M.
abstract: A rock strength evaluation study was initiated to help establish slope-design criteria for the projected expansion of a large operating open pit mine in Arizona. A major fault intersected the pit wall in the area of the proposed expansion. This paper presents the methodologies and techniques employed to recover, handle and test samples of highly fractured or poorly consolidated materials.

title: Engineering geological mapping for an open pit mine
source: Bulletin of the International Association of Engineering Geology Bulletin De L Association Internationale De Geologie De L Ingenieur
authors: Bing X.; Yurui L.
abstract: L'objectif de la cartographie géotechnique est de présenter les conditions géologiques pour pouvoir résoudre quelques problèmes de construction. La théorie et la méthode de cartographie doivent tenir compte très étroitement du projet et de l'ouvrage. Il existe différentes cartes géotechniques, leur diversité étant due au degré d'expérience du géotechnicien, à la sélection et à la représentation des facteurs géologiques naturels. Une carte géotechnique devrait pouvoir représenter clairement et précisement les conditions naturelles et devrait convenir à la réalisation d'un projet et d'un ouvrage. Le massif rocheux est considéré être un produit complexe de formations et déformations géologiques, sa principale nature étant d'avoir une structure définie. Sous une charge, celle-ci commande principalement sa déformation et sa rupture. Selon l'opinion ci-dessus mentionnée, en cartographie géotechnique une attention particulière est portée aux problèmes de stabilité. Dans cet article, on discute de la cartographie géotechnique de la mine à ciel ouvert de Jin Chuan et de ses applications.

title: DEEPENING CONSIDERED FOR PIPE OPEN PIT.
authors: Pabst M.
abstract: Inco's Pipe open pit mine, Thompson, Man. began production in 1970. The pit was designed for a maximum depth of 720 ft, a depth which will be reached by 1983. Plans are underway to increase the maximum depth to 800 ft and extend the life of the mine. The ore grade ranges from an average of 0. 5 percent to 1. 0 percent nickel.

title: Investigation of Irsha-Borodino Coal Supplied to Steam Power Plants.
authors: Bruer G.; Protsailo M.; Malyutina A.; Goreva G.; Matvienko V.
abstract: Statistical processing of data on the quality of coal from the Irsha-Borodino open pit mine shows that the qualitative characteristics according to the data given by the supplier and the consumer are close to one another. The average annual ash content of coal amounted to 9. 1-9. 2, while the ash content of commercial samples fluctuated from 6. 5 to 25. 5%.

title: BRAZIL'S VALEP PROJECT - PHOSPHATE SLURRY LINE COMPLETES FIRST YEAR WITH EXCELLENT RECORD.
authors: Fister L.; Finerty B.; Hill R.
abstract: The authors describe the precedent-setting project, which includes an open pit mine, concentrator, 75-mile, 9-inch pipe line with pump station and orifice station, and terminal facilities at the complex. The line was designed on the basis of bench scale tests used in conjunction with computer models.

title: The greening of open pit mine surfaces
authors: Boecker C.

title: Developing and Putting into Service Computerized Systems of Design of Coal Enterprises.
authors: Kuznetsov K.
abstract: The main organization in the coal industry of the USSR engaged in the development and introduction into experimental operation of a system of computer aided design (CAD) of enterprises is Tsentrogiproshakht (Central State Planning & Design Instute of Coal Mine Construction). The main structural units of the CAD system are plant subsystems identified by their functional characteristics: the type of enterprise (coal mine, open pit mine, coal dressing factory, coal machinery plant, building industry enterprises), the design stage, the element (object) of the projected enterprise. Plant subsystems consist of a functional and a special software part. The coal CAD system consists of 60 plant subsystems that include over 1000 project assignments whose computer-aided solution requires revision and creation of about 630 computer methods and design standards. The software is developed as packets of applied programs.

title: VALEP - the world's first long distance phosphate concentrate slurry pipeline.
authors: Fister L.; Hill R.; Finerty B.
abstract: The VALEP pipeline, which started operation in March 1979, is the world's first long distance slurry ppeline to transport phosphate concentrate. The 120 kilometer line is northwest of Rio de Janeiro, in the state of MinasGeras, Brazil; it connects the mine and concentrator near Tapira with a fertilizer complex near Uberaba. The 9 inch line is designed to transport 2.0 million dry metric tonnes of phosphate per year (dmtpy) at 61% solids by weight. As initial capacity of the concentrator is 900,000 dmptpy, batchimg of slurry alternately with water will be required until the concentrator is expanded. The particle size distribution of the slurry is minus 65 Tyler mesh, with approximately 35 percent of the solids minus 325 Tyler mesh. The entire project includes an open pit mine, a concentrator, a pipeline with pump station and orifice station, and terminal facilities at the fertilizer complex. (A)

title: Dust Control in Open Pit Mines.
authors: Pchelkin Y.; Tokmakov M.; Kupin A.
abstract: Dust conditions in open pit coal mines are considered in relation to different technological processes of mining. Results of laboratory investigations and industrial experiments regarding dust control when mining coal by rotary excavators and when transporting the mass of rock by trucks are presented. The investigaitons were carried out, inter alia, at the ″Korkinski″ open pit mine, 420 m deep, in South Yakutia, and other places. As a result, new dust-binding substances, ″Universin-A″ and ″Universin-B″ , satisfying all physico-chemical and production requirements have been developed. They belong to liquid compounded bitumens.

title: In-situ induced-polarization and magnetic susceptibility measurements-Yerington mine
authors: Hunter Ware G.
abstract: The Yerington Mine is an open pit mine of 'porphyry-copper' type. Primary mineralization (quartz veins, Cu-Fe sulfides, magnetite, and silicate alteration) is closely associated with a complex sequence of quartz monzonite porphyry intrusives. This primary mineralization is disrupted by subsequent alteration and faulting. The fault block containing the deposit has been rotated almost 90 degrees to the west; plan maps represent pretilt vertical sections. Almost one mile of pretilt vertical extent is exposed in the pit. Geologic observations may be taken only upon mining advances at discrete intervals. Detailed in-situ induced-polarization response and magnetic susceptibility surveys, both taken upon the pit floor, have been used to supplement geologic mapping. These in-situ measurements reveal the distribution patterns of sulfides and magnetite and are useful in interpolation or correlation of contacts, faults, and mineralization patterns between mapped advances. In-situ induced-polarization (IP) response was measured using a Scintrex IPR-7 receiver. Observations were made on a 10 × 10-ft grid using a Wenner electrode array with 3 1/3-ft a-spacing. Susceptibility measurements were taken with a Bison model 3101-A bridge and an in-situ coil arrangement 5 ft in diameter. A composite area approximately 3000 by 500 ft, representing 15,000 data points, has been surveyed. Contoured maps of in-situ IP response and magnetic susceptibility reveal the mineralization pattern in detail. These maps correlate well with the geologically mapped distribution of porphyry intrusives and also indicate zones of sulfide remobilization and/or magnetite destruction, including fault zones. IP response and magnetic susceptibility correlate well with elemental assays, mineral abundances, ratios, and textures determined from bench mapping and pit floor samples. The spatial distribution of physical properties is extremely complex, which demonstrates the need for caution in the use of simple interpretative models. The abundance of magnetite locally present in this particular porphyry-copper environment is noteworthy.

title: WOODLAWN BASE METAL OPEN PIT MINE REACHES CAPACITY.
authors: Anon
abstract: 50 Woodlawn, near Canberra reached full milling capacity this year. The complex ore assays 1. 7 percent copper, 5. 5 percent lead, 14. 4 percent zinc, and 2. 9 ounces of silver per ton. The copper ore assays 1. 9 percent copper, 0. 1 percent lead, 0. 5 percent zinc, and 0. 25 ounce of silver per ton. The differential flotation mill has a designed throughput of 3,300 tons of ore per day and is operated in separate campaigns to treat the complex ore and copper ores.

title: Determination of the seepage characteristics of thick layers of heterogeneous soil mounds.
authors: Lavrinenko I.; Saratov I.; Tseitlin A.
abstract: For the first time in the U.S.S.R. , a tailings storage dump is being built on the surface of interior mounds of overburden of an operational open pit mine - at present the first stage of the mining operation, of 100 ha. surface area has been brought into operation. The spoil heaps comprise 40m. thick embankments of a heterogeneous mixture of sandy, loamy and clayey soils. To assess the amount of water percolation to be anticipated through the foundations of the embankments and drainage systems, it was essential to obtain the seepage characteristics of the soil mix. However, it was found that traditional methods did not give sufficiently reliable and consistent answers. Some in situ tests were therefore carried out using sections of the embankment each 100m. x 100m. in plan of different ages, i.e. 6 years, 4 years and 2 years. The tests were of several months duration and were confirmed by laboratory experiments. A formula was developed for assessing change in seepage coefficient with time in accordance with data obtained on site. (A.L.)

title: CERRO VERDE.
authors: Anon
abstract: This article describes mining, mineral processing and metallurgical operations at this Peruvian opencast copper complex, the first stage of which was placed onstream last year. The first stage involved the mining and treatment of the oxide ore in the Cerro Verde deposit for an eventual output of 33,000 tonnes/yr of electrolytic copper in the form of 99. 98% pure cathodes. The first section to come onstream in Stage 1 was the heap-leaching unit, in which acid solutions are sprayed over heaps of oxide ore. Other operations described include the open pit mine, processing plant, as well as solvent extraction and electrowinning facilities.

title: SURFACE TRIALS OF THE HYDROMINER.
source: Pap Presented at the Int Symp on Jet Cutting Technol
authors: Summers D.A.; Barker C.R.
abstract: A longwall water jet mining machine called the Hydrominer has been developed at the University of Missouri-Rolla under a Bureau of Mines contract. The first design, referred to as Hydrominer One, has been extensively tested in an open pit mine and has clearly demonstrated that the working principle is viable. The second and greatly improved version, Hydrominer Two, has been built but has not as yet been tested extensively. This paper describes the test series and some of the changes which were required to better achieve the full productive potential of the Hydrominer concept.

title: BEAR CREEK FINDS WYOMING U3O8 ORE; THEN GETS MANY PERMITS FOR NEW MINE.
authors: Anon
abstract: Bear Creek Uranium is a joint venture between the Mono Power Company and the Rocky Mountain Energy Company with the latter as operator. The new mine and mill are 70 miles northeast of Casper, Wyoming. Bear Creek is one of the first companies to obtain all the necesary operating permits to develop a new open pit mine and operate a uranium processing mill. The mine and mill operations are described.

title: Gusino-Ozero Fuel and Energy Complex.
authors: Shchadov M.
abstract: The Gusino-Ozero district electric power station is the main link in the identically named fuel and energy complex presently being developed in the Buryat ASSR in East Siberia. The Kholboldzhino open pit mine now under completion is to produce 3 Mt of brown coal per annum. The deposit consists of seven gently sloping seams from 2 to 34. 7 m thick. The depth of the open pit is 285-325 m. The capacity of the Gusino-Ozero power plant, when completed in 1979, will be 1260 MW (comprising 6 power units of 210 MW each). So far three units have been put into operation.

title: RHEINBRAUN PRESERVES ENVIRONMENT.
authors: Anon
abstract: In the fall of 1978 stripping will start at what will become the largest open pit mine in the world. The Hambach pit of Rheinische Braunkohlenwerke AG will reach its full production rate by 1995 when 50,000,000 annual metric tons of brown coal will be mined. This mine is in the heart of the Rhineland. The approval of the decision to develop the Hambach pit was only granted after intensive investigations and studies. A much larger number of original forest areas is now to remain undisturbed. These will act as nuclei for natural regeneration and also as screens and buffers shielding the mining areas.

title: CONTINUOUS EXCAVATOR FOR SURFACE COAL MINING.
authors: Kay F.J.; Gordon J.; Crow L.
abstract: A forward-rotating bucket wheel excavator designed to continuously fragment and load unshot coal has been tested in an open pit mine. In principle, the excavating wheels rotate faster than required for rolling contact with the surface so the buckets excavate, carry away material, and provide a tractive effort to aid in pulling the vehicle forward. Production rates of over 1,080 tons per hour (1,000 cubic yards per hour) have been achieved utilizing 510 hp, verifying projected fragmenting and loading cost savings of 80 percent over conventional methods. Furthermore, due to the uniformly small size of the coal excavated, additional savings in preparation plant costs are possible.

title: EXPANSION AT BRUNSWICK.
authors: Anon
abstract: The current expansion of Brunswick Mining & Smelting Corp. Ltd. at its base metal property in New Brunswick, Canada, is highlighted. The Canadian lead/zinc producer is expanding output from its underground mining operations and phasing out its open pit mine. The expansion program involves the sinking of a new shaft and underground development by novel methods.

title: ITERATIVE APPROXIMATION TECHNIQUES FOR MICROSEISMIC SOURCE LOCATION.
authors: Dechman G.
abstract: This report presents a method that was developed to adapt microseismic techniques for rock structure analysis to investigations of surface problems, such as slope failure in an open pit mine. The source location method and two derivative location algorithms are described in detail, and the speed and accuracy of the two algorithms are compared.

title: Optimal Control Algorithm for the Automated Operational Control System of an Open Pit Mine.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Chernin E.; Legostaev V.; Tupitsyn A.
abstract: The problem of synthesis of an optimal control algorithm, maximizing the profit, for the extremal automated operatioal control system (AOCS) for the transporation complex at an open pit mine is considered. A target function equation is obtained establishing the dependence of the profit variation on the main components. It is shown that the open pit mine AOCS may be considered as a control system, extremal as regards the profit value, with random drifting of the extremum. An algorithm ensuring the search for the optimal transport route according to the magnitude of the profit.

title: Project Solutions for Construction of the ″Vostochnyi″ Open Pit Mine.
authors: Vinnitskii L.
abstract: In addition to the two existing open pit mines in the Ekibastuz coal basin, a third one is to be constructed in the southern part of the basin. The open pit mine is to be 2. 8 km long and 0. 9 km deep. Coal reserves up to the depth of 350 m amount to 750 million t. Coal is to be mined by four ERP-2500 rotary excavators with the capacity of 2500 m**3/hr each. The annual output is to reach 20 million t. The total length of conveyor lines will amount to 11 km.

title: MAINTENANCE: AN ESSENTIAL SERVICE TO OPERATIONS.
authors: Webster L.
abstract: Located in the Highland Valley of B. C. 's interior the Lornex copper mine is a subsidiary of Rio Algom Mines Ltd. The open pit mine and concentration plant process a low-grade prophyry-type ore containing copper and molybdenum, as well as minor amounts of precious metals. A comprehensive program of preventive maintenance is carried out on all vehicles and equipment. Working round the clock, seven days a week, the crews service all items according to a predetermined schedule based on a 200-hour interval. Shovels and drills, however, get more frequent attention.

title: Comparison of Physical Methods of Control of Stability of Open Pit Mine Slopes.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Turintsev Y.; Zobnin V.
abstract: Results of investigations of the microseismic, pulse, and seismic methods to control open pit mine edge stability are set forth. Calculation formulas are presented and criteria of evaluation of the state of stress of slopes at a stage close to an equilibrium are derived. This permits timely development and application of antideformation measures.

title: GEOTECHNICAL FACTORS IN OPEN PIT MINE DESIGN.
authors: Pentz D.; Hodges P.
abstract: This paper discusses those aspects of open pit mine design which are affected by geotechnical factors. Open pit mines in the context of this paper also includes open cast mines, where the ″ore″ is extracted and the waste material is immediately replaced or backfilled in the mined portion of the pit. Open pit mine design is a significant portion of project management and an attempt is made here to demonstrate where geotechnical engineering can be useful in improving mine design.

title: BLASTING VIBRATION LEVELS TRANSMITTED ACROSS FRACTURE PLANES.
authors: Berzal J.L.
abstract: This article presents experimental results obtained by means of field tests measuring vibration levels transmitted across a presplit fracture plane, across a natural fracture plane or joint in the rock mass, and across two artificial fracture planes with a distance between them of one metre. The vibration levels were compared with those assuming a solid rock mass. The tests were carried out in a Spanish open pit mine.

title: PROSPERITY RETURNS TO OLD GOLD CAMP WITH UMEX THIERRY MINE DEVELOPMENT.
authors: Fish R.
abstract: The main orebody at the Thierry mine is 15 million tons grading 1. 63 per cent copper. There is another 70 to 100 million tons of material grading 0. 4 per cent copper and 0. 2 per cent nickel which could become an open pit mine. The Thierry deposit ore minerals are chalcopyrite and pyrrhotite disseminated in a chlorite biotite schist and an ultrabasic intrusive. In addition to the copper values it also contains nickel, gold, silver, palladium and platinum.

title: The use of equivalent models in slope stability investigation
source: International Journal of Rock Mechanics and Mining Sciences and
authors: Reik G.; Teutsch C.
abstract: The example of model tests carried out within the framework of a rock mechanics program investigating the stability of an open pit mine, is used to demonstrate the possible application of such experiments in the assessment of slope stability. If rock properties, rock structure and boundary conditions (in-situ stresses, water pressure etc.) are sufficiently well known, model tests can yield information on slope deformation and possible failure mechanisms that cannot be at present obtained by other methods. Tests carried out on two slope models simulating structural conditions at Cala mine, Huelva, Spain, have demonstrated the decisive influence of joint fabric on the mode of failure. © 1976.

title: Deformations of a Slope Excavated in the Valdarno Overconsolidated Clay.
authors: D'elia B.; Ottaviani M.
abstract: The authors describe a study which used inclinometer measurements to determine the displacements of a clay slope during and after its excavation at the S. Barbara open pit mine. The influence of the structures present in the Valdarno overconsolidated clay on the time-dependent deformation process of the excavated slope is discussed. The finite element method was used in an analysis of the slope deformation immediately upon excavation, assuming a linear and nonlinear behavior of the clay. The analyses show the importance of a correct evaluation of the geotechnical properties of the soil.

title: Prospects of Development of the Krivoy Rog Iron Ore Basin.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Nivalov N.N.; Lubenets V.A.; Dzyubenko M.G.; Astaf'ev Y.P.; Chirkov Y.I.
abstract: Krivoy Rog basin is the largest iron ore basin in the world. In 1974, its output of commercial ore amounted to 107 M t. Rich ore deposits are estimated at 1. 5 G t; with 57. 9% iron content, 1. 3 G t of them of industrial categories. In 1975, over 45 M t of commercial rich ores were mined. The resources of ferruginous quartzites down to the depth of 500 m are estimated at 14. 9 G t. Five ore-dressing combines produced 61. 6 M t of ore concentrates with 65. 04% iron content in 1975. Future prospects of the basin are described. It is proposed to divert the river Ingulets and to build a super open pit mine with the design depth of up to 1000 m and annual output capacity of 150-180 M t of raw ore.

title: Prospects of Development of the Iron Ore Base and Ensuring Supply of Iron Ore Raw Material for Metallurgical Plants of the urals Economic Region.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Gorshkolepov M.
abstract: Since 1960, the iron ore industry of the Urals has been forced to rely on increasing output of poor ore grades with unchanged output of commercial ore. There are 88 iron ore deposits in the Urals, amounting to 15% of the overall USSR resources. They are represented mainly by titanium-magnetite ores poor in iron. Large metallurgical plants in the Urals constitute 28% of the pig iron industry of the USSR. They consume 52-53 Mt of ore per annum while the output of commercial ore in the Urals and Kazakhstan amounts to 45 Mt, i. e. 86-88% of the required amount. Even by 1980 the deficit in local and Kazakhstan ore will amount to 5-6 Mt. The plans to increase the output of the Kachkanas open pit mine and to build another mine there with an annual output of 45 Mt of raw ore, as well as to develop smaller deposits by 1980, are outlined.
