title: Protection of thermal springs in a region of brown-coal opencast mining
authors: Skorepova J.
abstract: The experimental modelling method is dealt with, which is used for prediction of deformations and possibilities of outflows occurring at the bottom of an open-pit mine during the excavation of brown coal. Thermal gas-bearing artesian water exerts an uplift pressure on the impervious subsoil of the coal seam and threatens the stability of the mine bottom. The breakthrough of the mine bottom would seriously affect the groundwater regime within the wide neighbourhood. Due to the fact that the mining is carried out within the protection zone of spa springs, these might be endangered by mining activities. (Author)

title: The isotopic composition of groundwaters related to native sulphur deposits
authors: Szaran J.; Niezgoda H.; Jasinska B.; Halas S.
abstract: The major components of hydrosulphuric waters (H<inf>2</inf>O, HCO<sup>-</sup><inf>3</inf>, SO<sup>2-</sup><inf>4</inf>, and H<inf>2</inf>S) have been analysed for stable isotope ratios in samples from Machow open-pit mine as well as from selected wells of the area adjacent to native sulphur ores collected in May 1993. The oxygen and hydrogen of recent water from the uppermost layer are isotopically very close to the recent infiltration waters. This means that these waters nearly completely replaced the original isotopically heavier waters. Nevertheless, a very high rate of bacterial reduction of sulphate to hydrogen sulphide is indicated by the high concentration of H<inf>2</inf>S (292 mg/l) and δ<sup>34</sup>S of SO<sup>2-</sup><inf>4</inf> (26.3‰) and H<inf>2</inf>S (-7.9‰). This is further confirmed by high δ<sup>18</sup>O of SO<sup>2-</sup><inf>4</inf>. -from Authors

title: Risk assessment in reserve estimation and open-pit planning
source: Transactions Institution of Mining Metallurgy Section A
authors: Dowd P.
abstract: The effects of the uncertainty of the ore reserve on feasibility studies and open-pit mine design for a small gold-mining venture are explored. Geostatistical simulation is employed as a method of quantifying the risk associated with the use of grades and tonnages that have been estimated from sparse data. -Author

title: Mitigation of adverse effects at the Lezama-Leguizamon abandoned open-pit mine (Bilbao, northern Spain)
authors: Saiz de Omeñaca J.; Ereño I.; Atxabal K.; Azurmendi I.
keywords: Limestone sealing | Mine reclamation | This abandoned open-pit mine
abstract: Solid fills arranged in 1-m-thick layers were prepared with stone blocks and pebbles of a drainage bed every 8 m. Runoff gathering in a well and the use of silts and mud lands for bordering and sealing the limestones are the main techniques employed for minimizing unfavorable effects at the Lezama-Leguizamon abandoned open-pit mine. Since there were waste disposal problems in the area, the rate of disposal has made the activity profitable. No significant faults have been detected by control studies, and the objectives are being achieved without problems. © 1993 Springer-Verlag.

title: Evaluation of geological and geotechnical data by using GIS for the diggability classification of an open-pit mine
source: Exploration Environment and Engineering Proc Ninth Thematic Conference on Geologic Remote Sensing Pasadena 1993 2 Vols
authors: Ayday C.; Goktan R.M.
abstract: In many excavation projects careful consideration should be given to numerous factors including geological and topographic information, proximity of the excavation operation to waste disposal areas and environmental restrictions together with equipment characteristics. For the rapid achievement of this aim, adequate techniques of evaluating such complicated data is of prime importance. In an attempt to demonstrate such an application, this paper gives the use of Geographic Information Systems in conjunction with two selected diggability classification systems for the rippability assessment of a particular site. The approach described will be actually applicable to the selection of excavating equipment for a wide range of other mining and civil engineering projects. -Authors

title: Quick deals and raw deals: A perspective on abuses of public ADR principles in Texas resource conflicts
authors: Kartez J.; Bowman P.
abstract: Comparing the recent Texas Copper Company smelter controversy with the celebrated Homestake open-pit mine case a decade ago illustrates that opportunities exist for resolving difficult siting and resource development conflicts, but that such opportunities can be misused, and sound dispute resolution principles abused. The route to failed siting efforts is to ignore the established evidence of the need for processes that acknowledge all stakeholders and the need for treating environmental analysis as a joint effort among parties instead of as a battle over facts. Unfortunately, cases continue to exist where a narrow focus on the settlement, however creative it may be, is leading to failure because of contempt for or ignorance of the importance of pre-negotiation and in-negotiation process requirements. In short, the "quick deal" may be no bettern than "no deal" in environmental conflicts. © 1993.

title: A critical appraisal of the Whittle 3-D open-pit mine optimization software package
authors: Costelloe D.
abstract: In 1965 Lerch & Grossman produced a paper describing a 3-D algorithm based on graph theory which could be specifically applied to the optimization of open-pit mine designs. At the time, most computers were incapable of performing the large quantities of iterative calculations required by the method. A 2-D algorithm was also described which, though effective on sections, lost its optimized quality when sections were combined. The 3-D algorithm therefore remained the preferred option. In 1986 the Whittle 3-D open-pit optimization package was launched by Whittle Programming Ltd. This package utilized the Lerch-Grossman algorithm for the first time in a commercial software application. Since then the package has undergone a number of changes and improvements. The purpose of an optimization package is to produce the most cost effective and most profitable open-pit design from a block model of an orebody. It must be capable of rapidly analysing alternatives accurately; it must be able to carry out sensitivity analyses of different components to assess financial risk; it must allow frequent updates to take into account changes in costs etc. and it must allow the production of interim designs. In today's mining world, a hastily produced or non-rigorous design is financially unacceptable as the design determines the potential for profit or loss. To develop this further it is essential not just to make a profit but to maximize the return on investment. This paper appraises the ability of the Whittle 3-D package to satisfy this objective. © The Geological Society 1992.

title: GPR measurements for locating underground mine workings at an active open-pit mine
source: Special Paper Geological Survey of Finland
authors: Daniels J.J.; Harris D.; Roberts R.; Schilling B.
abstract: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) measurements have been used recently at the Zortman Gold Mine (located in Zortman, Montana, USA) to locate underground mine workings beneath the current working level of the Zortman Open Pit Gold Mine. The igneous host rock is generally uniform, and GPR is routinely used to detect drifts, stopes, winzes and rooms located at depths of over 30 feet below the surface of the pit floor. The usefulness of GPR for detecting underground hazards is confirmed by blast hole drilling, with additional confirmation from historical underground maps of the old workings. -from Authors

title: Albitites and oligoclasite from Szklary (Lower Silesia)
source: Bulletin Polish Academy of Sciences Earth Sciences
authors: Muszynski M.; Natkaniec-Nowak L.
abstract: Fine-crystalline leucocratic rocks, found within the serpentinite massif of Szklary (Lower Silesia) in the abandoned nickel open-pit mine, were studied by microscopic, X-ray, infrared adsorption spectroscopic and chemical methods. It has been concluded that they represent almost monomineral feldspathic rocks - albitites and oligoclasite. Results obtained, particularly REE contents indicate a genetic link between these rocks and lower-Silesian gabbros. -Authors

title: Hydrothermal and supergene uranium mineralization at the Osamu Utsumi mine, Poços de Caldas, Minas Gerais, Brazil
authors: Waber N.; Schorscher H.D.; Peters T.
abstract: The Osamu Utsumi uranium deposit in the Mesozoic alkaline complex of Poços de Caldas (MG, Brazil) is a product of subsequent hydrothermal and supergene processes. The lithology of the open-pit mine is composed of a sequence of volcanic and subvolcanic phonolites and nepheline syenite intrusions similar to those of the alkaline complex; volcanic breccia pipes of about 80 m in diameter also occur, characterized by UThZr-REE mineralization concentrated in the matrix. A strong hydrothermalism, related to the formation of the breccias, has resulted in the potassic alteration and pyritization of the phonolites and syenites, with a low-grade mineralization of disseminated pitch-blende. The potassic alteration has transformed all feldspars into pure potash feldspars, nepheline into illite and kaolinite, and clinopyroxenes, which are the primary REE-bearers, into mixtures of TiO<inf>2</inf>-rich minerals, clay minerals and pyrite. The enrichment of K, S, U, Th, Pb, Rb, Ba and Mo was accompanied by a strong depletion in Ca, Na, Mg and Sr. The fluid inclusion data indicate temperatures around 250°C and a KClH<inf>2</inf>O mixture with approximately 7 wt.% KCl for the hydrothermal fluids. For fluids in the breccia pipes that transported additional Zr, Hf, F and minor REEs, the inclusions indicate boiling and give temperatures of 210°C with 40-45 wt.% KCl for a KClNaClH<inf>2</inf>O brine containing FeSO<inf>4</inf> and KF. Uraninite, pitchblende and brannerite are the main U-carriers, and monazite the major REE-bearing mineral in the high-grade mineralization of the breccias. Ultramafic dykes (dated to 76 Ma) with carbonatitic affiliation put a younger age limit to the hydrothermal event. As a result of supergene weathering below a lateritic soil cover 20 to 40 m thick and a saprolite zone 15 to 60 m thick, the pyrites in the rocks have been oxidized to varying depths of 80 to 140 m below surface, resulting in a redox front marked by a contrasting color change from oxidized (reddish-brown) to reduced (bluish-grey). In the vicinity of water-bearing fissures these redox fronts have penetrated to greater depth. Due to mobilization in the oxidized zone and precipitation immediately below the redox front, a secondary mineralization of pitchblende, partly occurring as nodules associated with secondary pyrite, has been developed. This secondary pyrite is sometimes related with CdS, and has a δS of -13% compared to δS values of -3.63 to +1.24% for hydrothermal pyrites: the low δS values of the former are attributed to bacterial action. In the immediate vicinity of the redox front, dissolution of the potash feldspar becomes apparent and the kaolinite content begins to increase. The marked color change at the redox front is caused by the presence of hydrous ferric oxides that, with time, evolve from amorphous Fe-hydroxides to goethite and hematite. On the oxidized side alunite-jarosite minerals are frequent. The porosity increases by 5 to 8% (almost doubled) at the redox front. Gibbsite is present when potash feldspar has been removed at the saprolite-laterite contact. Uranium is partly retained in the oxidized zone by adsorption onto poorly crystalline phases and due to incorporation into hydrothermal refractory minerals. Many of the REEs are associated with clay-sized phosphates (including crandallite group minerals) and seem to be hardly mobilized by the oxidizing weathering fluids. Only a slight general loss of REEs was observed between oxidized and reduced rock, with the degree of loss being greater for the light REEs. Certain indications for a fractionation of Ce and Eu from the other REEs are present. © 1992.

title: An evaluation of the toxic gas pollution in an open-pit mine
authors: Panev T.; Dzharova V.; Bobev G.
abstract: The present work aims at giving a complete characteristic of the toxic chemical factor in the working environment of a pit "Kremikovtsi", for evaluating the occupational risk for the engaged workers. The basic pollution sources of the pit are the eliminating toxic gases during work from different types of machines and heavy-freight vans. The already measured concentrations of carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, nitric oxides, hydrocarbons, aldehydes and lead, manganese, ferrous and mercury aerosols in all working places of the pit are under MAC. The calculated total index of toxicity for all working places surpasses up to 3 times the unit and is rated. 1st degree--unfavourable conditions of work concerning the toxic chemical factor.

title: Grasberg open-pit. Ertsberg's big brother comes onstream in Indonesia
authors: Hickson R.
abstract: The Grasberg copper-gold deposit was discovered in the spring of 1988, one year before the planned closure of Freeport Indonesia's original Ertsberg open-pit copper mine. In spite of Grasberg's remote location, 600 m (1968 ft) above the Ertsberg, atop a hitherto inaccessible mountain, Freeport-McMoRan brought its latest open-pit mine into production in the last week of 1989, less than two years after discovery. Freeport Indonesia's (FI) copper-gold mining operations are located in Irian Jaya, the easternmost province of Indonesia on the western side of the island of New Guinea.

title: Labour conditions and morbidity with temporary disability in the excavator operators engaged in the Karaganda open coal mines
authors: Lutsenko L.; Gvozdeva L.; Shabolina T.; Bobulov S.
abstract: Studies performed at an open-pit mine in the Karaganda Region showed that excavator operators were exposed to the complex action of vibration, noise, unfavourable microclimate and dust in the parameters axceeding the existing norms. A comparative analysis of the levels of morbidity with temporary disability and the actual occupational conditions proved the latters' influence on the morbidity rate, particularly in case with diseases caused by respiratory infections, spinal disorders (radiculitis, lumbago), blood circulation disfunctions, all of which should be attributed to occupationally conditioned ailments. Hygienic and preventive measures, with due account of specific groups of diseases, can considerably improve the workers' health status and decrease morbidity with temporary disability rates.

title: Thermal decomposition and formation of properties of fine-grained coke from brown coals
source: Coke Chemistry USSR English Translation of Koks I Khimiya
authors: Unterberger O.; Nefedov P.; Ryvkin I.; Popov V.; Barskii V.
abstract: Studies were conducted on a laboratory unit that stimulates heating of coal in a fluidized bed by heating the boosting bed of coal through the wall of a rotating retort. The installation permits running of the process over a wide range of rates of temperature rise right up to heat shock, as well as isothermal holding of the coal at the final coking temperature. Brown coal from the Irsha-Borodino open-pit mine of the Kansk-Achinsk Basin ground to a size of 83.4% content of <3 mm class was used for the study. Investigation of the possible rates of coking showed that the maximum rate of heating of the boosting coal particles is achieved during heat shock and amounts to 100-120°C/min. The conditions of heat shock most fully correspond to the conditions of heating of coal with a solid heat transfer agent during thermocontact coking, for which reason the rate of coking of 100-120°C/min was chosen to investigate the principles of pyrolysis of brown coal.

title: Performance monitoring of electric mining shovels
source: Transactions of the Institution of Mining and Metallurgy Section A Mining Technology
authors: Hendricks C.; Scoble M.; Peck J.
abstract: A review is presented of studies undertaken in a large open-pit mine with the aim of defining the relationship between shovel performance and muckpile characteristics, as governed by bench geology and ground preparation. The studies included the development and application of microprocessor-based instrumentation to monitor the performance of rotary blasthole drills and electric shovels. Particular attention is given to the methodology for the evaluation of shovel digging performance. Sample shovel performance data and their interpretation are presented to illustrate how this has been related to muckpile diggability in a range of digging conditions. A diggability index, based on hoist motor response, has been determined. Elements of dipper trajectory have also been considered in the interpretation of monitored motor responses.

title: On the problem of fuzzy searching for hard workability rocks in open-pit mine exploitation
authors: Kacewicz M.
keywords: fuzzy sets | strength parameters | uncertainty | workability coefficient
abstract: The problem of fuzzy searching for hard workability rock areas is divided into two steps. The first is description of uncertainty of compressive strength, internal friction angle, and cohesion. The second is description of workability coefficient via fuzzy sets. The method presented is used in a computer program, which is an element of data base utility library. © 1989 International Association for Mathematical Geology.

title: Short term mine planning at Syncrude
source: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
authors: Malhotra Y.P.; List S.J.
abstract: The synthetic crude oil from the oil sands with a consistently upward trend in production each year. The open-pit mine currently delivers an average of 300,000 tonnes of oil sands per day to the Extraction Plant. For the mining of oil sands, the mine is equipped with four draglines, four bucketwheel reclaimer/ conveyor systems and an auxiliary production system to supplement major equipment production. Overburden is stripped by a large fleet of shovels and trucks. All these systems combined will handle approximately 325 million tonnes of material in 1988. The effective technical support is crucial to the achievement of high production objectives. The short term mine planning functions to achieve these objectives, are performed by two groups; Overburden Engineering and Short Range Planning. The short term plans range from day to day operating plans to one year mine plans. This paper will discuss the short term planning process, the complexities and some of the challenges faced by the mine planning engineers. © 1989, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

title: Electrical equipment for heavy duty conveyors in open-pit mines
source: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
authors: Hartlief F.; Einenkel O.
abstract: The area to the west of Cologne as far as the borders with Belgium and the Netherlands contains the largest coherent deposit of lignite in the Federal Republic of Germany, covering approximately 2500 km<sup>2</sup>. 110×10<sup>6</sup> tonnes of lignite are produced annually in 4 open-pit mines using bucket-wheel excavators, conveyors, stockpile machines and spreaders; this requires transporting 450×10<sup>6</sup> m<sup>3</sup> of overburden each year. Consequently, the mass transport of coal and overburden, as 40% of the cost of an open-pit mine, is a major consideration within the context of engineering, economics and organization. The article describes the conveyors and their electrical systems.

title: Computer simulation of a semi-continuous open-pit mine haulage system
source: International Journal of Mining and Geological Engineering
authors: Peng S.; Zhang D.; Xi Y.
keywords: computer simulation | in-pit crusher | Iron ore mine | open-pit mine haulage

title: Relationship between soil organic carbon and microbial biomass on chronosequences of reclamation sites
authors: Insam H.; Domsch K.H.
abstract: The interrelationship between soil microorganisms and soil organic carbon was studied on an agricultural and on a forest chronosequence of open-pit mine reclamation soils. Thirty years after reclamation, soil carbon levels of 0.8% on the agricultural sites and 1.7% on the forest sites (A-horizon) were reached. Microbial biomass rose very fast to levels characteristic of undisturbed soils. Microbial carbon (C<inf>mier</inf>) was 57 mg·100 g<sup>-1</sup> soil after 15 years on the agricultural sites and 43 mg·100 g<sup>-1</sup> on the forest sites. The contribution of C<inf>mier</inf> to the total organic carbon (C<inf>org</inf>) decreased with time, more rapidly on the forest sites than on the agricultural ones. From the C<inf>mier</inf>r/C<inf>org</inf> ratio it became evident that both chronosequences had not yet reached a steady state within the 50 years of reclamation. A significant decrease of the metabolic quotient qCO<inf>2</inf> (microbial respiration per unit biomass) with time was observed on the agricultural sites but not on the forest sites. The C<inf>mier</inf>/C<inf>org</inf> ratio proved to be a reliable soil microbial parameter for describing changes in man-made ecosystems. For evaluating reclamation efforts, the C<inf>mier</inf>/C<inf>org</inf> ratio can be considered superior to its single components (C<inf>mier</inf> or C<inf>org</inf>) and to other parameters. © 1988 Springer-Verlag New York Inc.

title: Overview of hydraulic construction techniques utilized at the syncrude Canada Limited tailings pond.
source: In Hydraulic Fill Structures Speciality Conf Fort Collins U S A Aug 15 18 1988 D J A Van Zykl S G Vick Eds
authors: Yano L.; Fair A.
abstract: The use of tailings sand from a tar-sand and open-pit mine in Alberta, Canada, to construct the containment dyke for the tailings pond is described by the foundation geology and the in-situ density of the compacted tailings sand. Construction techniques and the history of the tailings pond are outlined.

title: Phytogeochemical surveys within kimberlite bodies
authors: Komogorova L.; Stadnik Y.; Fedorov V.
abstract: Based on certain theoretical assumptions, the authors conducted surveys within the Daldyn kimberlite field, Daldyn-Alakit district, Yakutia, in the Udachnaya, the Dal'nyaya and the Zarnitsa pipes. A survey was conducted along the south side of an open-pit mine and along separate profiles, where the authors sampled needles and small twigs of larches (Larix daurica) of roughly the same age. Elements characteristic of the kimberlite-dispersion halo (Ti, Ni, Cr and Fe) were detected in relatively high concentrations in the halo zone around the open-pit mine. The results of phytogeochemical sampling in the vicinity of the Zarnitsa pipe also confirm the possibility of using the phytogeochemical method to outline kimberlite pipes.

title: Quaternary stratigraphy and geochemistry at the Owl Creek Gold Mine, Timmins, Ontario, Canada
authors: Bird D.; Coker W.
abstract: The Owl Creek Gold Mine is located in Hoyle Township, approximately 18 km northeast of Timmins, Ontario, Canada. The open-pit mine exposes a sequence of altered and mineralized mafic tholeiitic volcanics bounded to the north and south by greywacke and argillite. Gold occurs in the free state in quartz veins, often with graphite, and as fine gold on surfaces of, and within fractures in, pyrite. The study was designed to determine the distribution and distance of transport of Au in overburden down-ice from subcropping Au mineralization. This required an understanding of the glacial history of the area. The Quaternary stratigraphy at Owl Creek was studied and sampled by means of 17 sonic and 15 reverse-circulation overburden drill holes near the open pit, and several overburden exposures in the open-pit walls. Nonmagnetic heavy-mineral concentrates (specific gravity >3.3) were made from the <2000 μm (-10 mesh) fraction of all overburden samples from the drill hole and section sampling. The heavy-mineral concentrates were analyzed for Au by neutron activation. A till pebble lithology study was done on the >2000 μm (-10 mesh) fraction of the sonic drill core. Our stratigraphic studies indicate that there were three major Wisconsinan (Weichselian) ice advances and one minor, late readvance in the Timmins area. The transport and deposition of sediments comprising the "Oldest", "Older", Matheson and Cochrane stratigraphic "packages" (oldest to youngest) are related to three ice advances and one readvance which moved towards 240° ± 10°, 150° ± 5°, 170° ± 5° and 130° ± 5°, respectively. Geochemically anomalous levels of Au in the overburden define two dispersal trains down-ice of the Owl Creek Gold Mine. One, in the "Older" lodgement till, is 400-500 m long. The other in Matheson ablation and waterlain tills, is approximately 700 m long. The till pebble lithology study showed that pebble counting can be used to approximate bedrock contacts, but may not necessarily identify the source rock type of the matrix. © 1987.

title: RE-USE OF TAILINGS DAM WATER AT A LARGE MINE IN THE NAMIB DESERT IN NAMIBIA.
authors: Hamman P.
abstract: Roessing is a high tonnage open-pit mine situated in the Namib Desert and is one of the largest producers of uranium in the world. The waste from the plant is pumped as an acidic slurry to the tailings dam, and as the solids settle, the water in the impoundment clears. The three causes of water loss from this tailings dam are entrainment into the settled solids, evaporation and seepage. Water treatment and desalination methods were investigated and rejected in favor of direct recycling. The advantages of recycling water from the tailings dam are the recovery of uranium and two of the process reagents, acid and ferric iron. This results in a saving equivalent of 3/4 million US dollars each year, but recycling is constrained by the corrosivity of the water and its detrimental effects on the process. To date Roessing has spent about 2,75 million on water recycling and has recouped this sum in a little over three years.

title: RECENT LESSONS THAT HAVE BEEN LEARNED IN OPEN-PIT MINE STABILITY.
source: Transactions of the American Institute of Mining Metallurgical and Petroleum Engineers Society
authors: Brawner C.
abstract: As a result of the typical problems that have been described, a number of developments were made in the 1970s and early 1980s that have improved the ability to evaluate structural geology, ground water conditions, blasting, shear strength parameters, stability analysis, etc. However, further improvements are still required to design rock slopes with a high degree of accuracy. As a result of this, it is necessary to measure and monitor the behavior of the pit slopes during the entire mining process to match technical and theoretical ability with practical experience in the field.

title: SMALL THICKENERS YIELD BIG GAINS AT BOUGAINVILLE.
authors: Deans B.; Glatthaar J.
abstract: At Bougainville Copper Limited (BCL), a new thickener installation recovers 60% of plant water needs from tailings. This relieved periodic water shortages, trimmed high pumping costs, cut consumption of flotation reagents, and created a more effective flotation environment with better mineral recovery. BCL operates a large open-pit mine and concentrator at Panguna on the island of Bougainville in the North Solomons Province of Papua New Guinea.

title: IN-PIT CRUSHING AND CONVEYING REDUCES HAULAGE COSTS.
authors: Althoff H.; Clark R.
abstract: The advantages and disadvantages of a mobile crushing plant with a belt conveyor system compared to a stationary crushing plant with haulage by heavy trucks are described. The capital expenditure and operational expenses are compared and the individual cost factors are explained. Every open-pit mine or quarry, however, is different and has to be assessed and analyzed individually in order to find the optimum and most economical solution. Due to the high truck haulage costs, many open-pit mines tend to the more economical solution with mobile crushing plants and continuous belt conveyor operation.

title: TIRES, THEIR IMPORTANCE AND COST IN THE MINE.
authors: McColman D.
abstract: Haulage truck tire life and costs in a hard rock open-pit mine are governed and controlled by four important factors: field control; operating within manufacturer's guidelines; different tire purchasing methods; and scrap piles. These factors are discussed briefly.

title: Geodynamic phenomena induced by the opencast mining activity at Belchatow.
source: Proc 5th International Association of Engineering Geology Congress Buenos Aires 1986 Vol 1 Balkema
authors: Wysokinski L.
abstract: The seismic activity phenomenon induced by the mining works at the Belchatow open-pit mine of depth down to 200 m is described. The phenomenon mechanism was discussed and the forecasted values of tremors calculated on the basis of the simplified seismic hazard method are presented. -from Author

title: Preventing and Fighting the Deformations of the Constructive Elements in Open-pit Mines and Waste Dumps.
authors: Fodor D.
abstract: The deformations of the constructive elements in open-pit mine and waste dumps are presented together with actions to be taken in order to prevent and fight them in relation to the development degree and the rock nature.

title: SOLID WASTE DISPOSAL SITE SELECTION FOR THE MCLAUGHLIN GOLD PROJECT IN NORTHERN CALIFORNIA.
source: Transactions of the American Institute of Mining Metallurgical and Petroleum Engineers Society
authors: Crouch D.; Poulter D.
abstract: The engineering and metallurgical assessment of the McLaughlin Project are body concluded that an open-pit mine and cyanide leach mill process would be feasible, producing both waste rock and residual mill tailings. As a part of the planning and permitting process, site selection studies were conducted for the tailings and waste rock disposal. The site selection process began with a regional identification of potential disposal sites and proceeded through 1) regional screening, 2) elimination of sites with obvious fatal flaws, 3) qualitative ranking of site evaluation criteria, 4) quantitative ranking of sites, 5) field investigation, 6) evaluations of field data, and 7) selection of preferred sites. Based on this approach of site rankings and field evaluations, tailings and waste rock disposal sites were selected and recommended for the preliminary design phase of the permitting and project development process.

title: GEOCHEMICAL AND GEOLOGIC RELATIONS OF GOLD AND OTHER ELEMENTS AT THE GOLD ACRES OPEN-PIT MINE, LANDER COUNTY, NEVADA.
source: Discoveries of Epitherm Precious Met Deposits
authors: Wrucke C.; Armbrustmacher T.
abstract: A study of the relation of gold and other elements of the Gold Acres mine was undertaken as part of an investigation of the geochemistry and geology of the mineral deposits on the east flank of the northern Shoshone Range. The investigations have established background and threshold concentrations for 31 elements resulting in definitions of anomalies at the open-pit mine. This paper presents evidence that three suites of elements occur and that deposition of gold began late in the history of mineralization. The case history was originally published in 1975.

title: CUT-OFF GRADE CALCULATIONS FOR AN OPEN-PIT MINE.
authors: John H.
abstract: The paper demonstrates how the optimum cut-off grade can be calculated for typical large tonnage open-pit mines. In the examples, it is assumed that the concentrator tonnage is fixed and that there are no market restrictions. The mining rate is assumed to be variable.

title: COST REDUCTION BY IN-PIT CRUSHING AND CONVEYING.
authors: Althoff H.
abstract: The advantages and disadvantages of a mobile crushing plant with a belt conveyor system compared to a stationary crushing plant with haulage by heavy trucks are described. The capital expenditure and operational expenses are compared, and the individual cost factors are explained. Every open-pit mine, however, is different and has to be assessed and analyzed individually in order to find the optimum and most economical solution. Due to high truck haulage costs, many open-pit mines tend to the more economical solution with mobile crushing plants and continuous belt conveyor operation.

title: SOCIEDAD MINERA PUDAHUEL PRODUCES LOW-COST COPPER AT LO AGUIRRE.
authors: Burger J.
abstract: Sociedad Minera Pudahuel (SMP) is producing some of the lowest cost copper in Chile from a near ideal site on the suburban fringe of Santiago. The Lo Aguirre mine is about 30 km west of the business center and just off the main highway linking Santiago with Valparaiso on the coast. The current operation consists of an open-pit mine, modified 'thin layer' (TL) leaching of ore placed on sloped pads, solvent extraction (SX), and electrowinning (EW) of cathode copper having remarkable purity. A secondary leach of the residue reclaimed from the TL leach cycle also recovers additional copper from the mixed oxide-sulphide ores mined at Lo Aguirre. Fine copper recovery is currently 14,000 mt/yr. As now drilled, the orebody is estimated to consist of 8. 5 million mt grading 1. 9% copper, for an estimated mine life of eight years.

title: MATERIAL HANDLING IN MINE AND PLANT AT THE MALANJKHAND COPPER PROJECT.
authors: Puranik S.; Kamra S.
abstract: The Malanjkhand copper mine is located 90 km north-east of Balaghat, a district town of Madhya Pradesh in India. The ore body is fairly continuous, exhibiting an arcuate shape. The average thickness is about 70 m. There are three distinct ore zones, viz. , the oxidation zone, the primary, and the secondary sulphidization zone. The primary sulphidization zone is represented by chalcopyrite. The mine is designed for 5 Mm**3/a excavation to produce 2 Mt/a ore. The ore from the open-pit mine is fed to a primary gyratory crusher, where its size is reduced from 1,200 to 150 mm. The ore is then stocked inthe coarse-ore stock pile with 18,000 t live capacity.

title: USE OF A REORIENTATION STRATEGY FOR GEOSTATISTICAL ORE RESERVE ESTIMATION OF A COMPLEX DIPPING TABULAR OREBODY AS AN AID TO OPEN-PIT MINE PLANNING.
authors: Mol O.; Gillies A.
abstract: An evaluation method for a complex dipping tabular orebody is introduced using an iron deposit, the Main Orebody on Koolan Island in north-west Western Australia, as the case study. The method involves use of a reorientation strategy to convert the deposit to a simple flat lying orebody, geostatistical analysis for estimation of sub-blocks, and estimation of bench block values. A mineral inventory file which contains bench block location coordinates, ore tonnage and block grades, is produced. This information is then used to determine grade-tonnage curves.

title: ACCURATE PREDICTION FOR GREAT SLOPESLIDE.
source: Changsha Kuangshan Yanjiuyuan Jikan Quarterly of the Changsha Institute of Mining Research
authors: Cheng G.
abstract: There had occurred more than once, slopeslides or earth-slipping accidents in a stope of a copper open-pit mine which has been mined for years by Baiyin Non-ferrous Metals Co. Two great land-slides with a total volume of 1 million m**3 of rocks falling down the slope broke out on July 9th and 10th 1983. These were predicted with accuracy. The causes leading to sliding and the type of slides are herein analyzed. An advanced prediction of the slope-stability in the vicinity of the slided rock mass is also made.

title: Open-pit mine design in seismic areas.
source: Transactions Institution of Mining Metallurgy Section A
authors: Gonzalez De Vallejo L.; Eldred P.J.L.; Oteo C.S.
abstract: Two methods used in seismic hazard analysis are referred to as 'probabilistic' and 'deterministic'. The first gives results, in terms of the annual probability of occurrence or the return period, for a range of intensities, magnitudes or ground accelerations. Deterministic method give only the largest possible intensity, magnitude or ground acceleration. An increase in the volume of excavation that can result from a reduction in the slope angle to allow for seismic aspects leads to higher production costs and other similar economic consequences. The final decision on what is considered to be an acceptable level of risk should, therefore, be based on a cost-benefit analysis. The proposed Arenas del Rey open-pit mine in S Spain is presented as a case study in which these considerations and procedures have been applied and developed. Detailed seismic, geological and geotechnical investigations were carried out for the mine.-from Authors

title: GOLDEN SUNLIGHT - A NEW GOLD MINING OPERATION.
authors: Smolik T.; Ziesing G.; Loros E.
abstract: The Golden Sunlight mine began operations in 1983 with a conventional open-pit mine supplying 4536 t/d (5000 stpd) of milling ore. After crushing and grinding, the ore is leached with cyanide solution in agitation tanks. Soluble values are removed from the sand portion of the leached ore with five stages of countercurrent washing cyclones. After thickening of the cyclone-wash overflow slurry, the gold is recovered in activated carbon with a six-stage carbon-in-pulp circuit and a five-stage upflow carbon column circuit. Pressure stripping, carbon reactivation, electrowinning, and refining complete the recovery process.

title: OPEN-PIT MINE MAINTENANCE CONSIDERATIONS.
authors: Anon
abstract: The type of maintenance a mine company wants to practice is preventive maintenance (PM), which is when a unit is out of service in accordance with a predetermined schedule. During this period the unit is cleaned, lubricated, undergoes routine servicing, inspection, and minor repairs.

title: COMINCO ON THE HUNT WITH RED DOG AND BUCKHORN.
authors: Anon
abstract: Cominco American Inc is developing Cominco's largest and richest zinc-lead mine. The Red Dog deposit is located 55 miles from the Chukchi Sea. Although the orebody has not been completely defined, current mining plans indicate a life of 50 years. The company's first precious metal operation is 88 km southwest of Carlin, Nevada, in the Cortez Mountains. The Buckhorn open-pit mine, scheduled to come on stream in 1984, is expected to produce gold and silver for seven years.

title: EVALUATION OF FLORIDA PHOSPHATE MATRIX TRANSPORTATION FROM MINE TO PLANT.
authors: Raulerson J.; Williams J.
abstract: This paper presents a comparative evaluation of several systems currently being used or proposed for the transport of matrix from an open-pit mine to a large fixed plant. The matrix is a sticky, wet clay to be carried from 8-16 km (5-10 miles) at 910 t/h to 1. 8 kt/h (1,000-2,000 stph). The system is complicated by frequent moves of the open-pit mine site and other factors such as use of the clay component in land reclamation.

title: Torony Lignite Deposit - A Model for Development.
authors: Simon K.
abstract: The exploration of Pliocene lignite deposits in western Hungary began in the Koszeg-Szombathely-Szentgotthard area in 1962. Prospecting work ending in 1977 indicated the presence of considerable reserves. Extensive exploration work carried out after the initial development phase confirmed the presence of about 500 million tons of lignite reserves west of Szombathely up to the Austrian border. The coal seams continue westward into south Burgenland, but in the opinion of the author this part of the deposit is not large enough for the opening of a separate open-pit mine.

title: PRELIMINARY ANALYSIS OF THE MINOR STRUCTURES IN THE BAIYIN OPEN-PIT MINE, GANSU.
source: Zhongnan Kuangye Xueyuan Xuebao Journal of Central South Institute of Mining and Metallurgy
authors: Duan J.
abstract: There are various types of minor structures occurring in the Baiyin Open-pit Mine, Gansu. On the basis of the deformation succession of the structures, it may be subdivided into two main phases and three subordinate stages, and all of them belong to the Caledonian Cycle. For all the stages, the styles of structure, dynamic characteristics, heat-flow values, strain-facies and metamorphism that have been found in the minor structures reveal certain regularities.

title: COSTS OF IN-PIT CRUSHING.
authors: Iles C.D.
abstract: Duval Corp. has historically been sensitive to mining costs, in part because of relatively low grade copper-molybdenum ore bodies. These concerns have resulted in three haulage system generations at the 218 kt/d (240,000 stpd) Sierrita-Esperanza open-pit mine, Tucson, Ariz. Studies indicate an average haulage cost savings of 32 cents/t(29 cents/st) of rock processed through the portable system. With three portable crushing systems handling 55% of the material mined, the total annual non-capital cash flow (before taxes) will increase more than 12 million. In addition, average truck requirements will be reduced by 37%, eliminating all truck capital expenditures over the next 10-year period.

title: NEW INDUSTRIAL TRACTION SETS.
authors: Dubina I.
abstract: Basic technical data are reported and structural features indicated for the new type OPE1B alternating-current and PEZT direct-current traction sets; they permit a 20-25% increase in the productivity of open-pit mine transportation in movement of material, with a substantial reduction in electric-power consumed for traction and expanded sphere of effective utilization of rail transport in deep open-pit mines.

title: OPEN-PIT MINE PLANNING - THE EXPANDED ROLE OF COMPUTERS.
source: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
authors: Weiss A.
abstract: Applications of computer assisted mine planning are described in mineral exploration, development and operations. The strength of this tool lies in the improved ability to plan and execute mining projects. Such benefit is illustrated by three cases representing feasibility studies, long- to short-range mine planning, and operations monitoring and control. Quantitative benefit and cost data are presented.

title: EFFECT OF SHEARING ON THE QUALITY OF SOME COALS IN THE SOUTHEASTERN CANADIAN CORDILLERA.
authors: Bustin R.
abstract: Extensive deposits of tectonically sheared coal of the Mist Mountain Formation occur in the southeastern Canadian Cordillera. In order to determine the effect of shearing and comminution on washability, samples of sheared and unsheared coal of two seams were collected from an open-pit mine at Eagle Mountain. The results of investigation indicate that the sheared, finely comminuted coal has a disproportionately large amount of dash, lower yields on washing and is more extensively oxidized than the unsheared coal.

title: Development and recultivation of the Altenburg 4 lignite open-pit mine of the Preussische Elektrizitats-AG, Borken section
authors: Schroder H.

title: Numerical Simulation of Potentiometric Surface Changes Caused by a Proposed Open‐Pit Anthracite Mine
authors: Bair E.; Parizek R.
abstract: The Trescott, Pinder, Larson (Trescott and others, 1976) finite‐difference flow model was modified and used to simulate potentiometric surface changes caused by the development of a proposed open‐pit anthracite mine. The modifications to the program code were made to account for site‐specific hydrogeologic conditions and to simulate the mining operation. In order to account for vertical changes in hydraulic conductivity caused by underground mine voids, the coefficient subroutine (COEF) was modified to permit the value of hydraulic conductivity to vary with depth. The lateral growth and deepening of the mine were simulated by changing the data input subroutine (DATAI) to allow the number, location, and hydraulic head of constant‐head nodes to vary with the time period. The mass balance subroutine (CHECKI) was modified to print out the flux into each constant‐head node at the end of each time period, thereby permitting calculation of changes in the rate of ground‐water flow into the mine. Site‐specific values of hydraulic conductivity, specific yield, aquifer recharge, streambed permeability, and hydraulic head initially were used in the modeling studies. Input parameter values were adjusted within the range of established field values during steady‐state model calibration. It was not possible to calibrate the transient model because the mining operation was in the planning stage and, therefore, no historical data existed. Nonetheless, transient simulations using the adjusted input parameter values and the simulated hydraulic head values were made to show that it is possible to model potentiometric surface changes caused by ground‐water flow into an open‐pit mine. These simulations predicted that, after eight years of mining, a cone of depression approximately 20,000‐feet long, 8000‐feet wide, and 1000‐feet deep would form around the proposed mine. The results of the transient simulations were used in a preliminary manner to assess the potential hydrogeologic impact of the proposed mining operation. Copyright © 1981, Wiley Blackwell. All rights reserved

title: ESTIMATING DRILLING AND BLASTING COSTS - AN ANALYSIS AND PREDICTION MODEL.
authors: Borquez G.
abstract: Drilling and blasting cost estimates that closely approximate eventual operating costs are important to mining companies and their contractors. Mining companies need accurate estimates to evaluate financially ongoing projects and assess bids from contractors. The key to accurate cost estimates lies in identifying and accounting for all of the factors that affect the financing of a particular operation. In this paper, an analysis of the drilling, blasting, operating, and economic parameters that should be accounted for in a drilling and blasting program are identified and treated quantitatively. The parameters are then used to help design a cost estimate for driling and blasting in the preproduction program of a large open-pit mine.

title: SHORT-DELAY BLASTING AT ANACONDA'S BERKELEY OPEN-PIT MINE, MONTANA.
authors: Oriard L.L.; Emmert M.W.
abstract: The authors outline the development and application of blasting methods put into use 11 years ago. The blast design uses a very short delay (5 milliseconds) between detonation of explosives charges. Concern is expressed over categorical rejection of very short delay blasting which can make the difference between success and failure of major mining operations.

title: KAISER JOINS THE BIG COAL PRODUCERS.
authors: Jackson D.
abstract: Kaiser Resources Ltd. is preparing to install a new generation of equipment at its Sparwood mine in British Columbia. KRL has broken ground for the Green Hills open-pit mine.

title: Pneumatic piezometers: multiple and single installations in vertical and inclined boreholes.
authors: Deardorff G.; Lumsden A.; Hefferon W.
abstract: A large-scale slope optimization program was undertaken in the Twin Buttes open-pit mine in Arizona, USA. A key element of this program was the depressurization of a fault zone, which intersects the pit wall. In order to monitor the effectiveness of the depressurization program and to establish water pressure gradients within the fault zone affected by surface and underground mining and drilling, multiple installations of up to three sealed pneumatic piezometers in one borehole were installed to depths in excess of 274m. -from Authors

title: CYPRUS BAGDAD.
authors: Niemi L.
abstract: Details are given of Cyprus Bagdad Copper Co. 's major expansion in northwestern Arizona, which was designed to increase the company's annual copper production from approximately 35 million lbs to more than 140 million lbs. The open-pit mine and 40,000-stpd concentrator, located 120 miles northwest of Phoenix in the Santa Maria Mtns. at Bagdad, now accounts for over 7% of Arizona's copper output and 4. 5% of US production. The ″new″ Cyprus Bagdad is an excellent example of a safe, clean, and highly efficient operation which reflects the successful application of ″state-of-the-art″ mining and processing techniques.

title: 7 DAYS TO MINE EIGHT SEAMS.
authors: Jackson D.
abstract: This article describes how the financial advantages of a seven-day, three-shift operation were used by Carbon Coal Co. to maximize the mining of eight thin, elusive coal seams at the company's New Mexico open-pit mine. Mining the multiple seams at the Mentmore, N. M. , mine required elaborate and crucial scheduling at times. The flow chart of the mine's coal preparation plant is included.

title: Opening of the Hambach Open-Pit Brown Coal Mine and the Mine Infrastructure.
authors: Berkenbusch J.
abstract: The coal field has extractable coal deposits of 2400 million tons. With an annual output of 45 to 50 million tons, the Hambach open-pit mine will provide about 40% of the total output of the Rhine Brown Coal Company until far beyond the year 2000. After the definition of responsibilities had been announced in May 1977, it was essential to equip the new open-pit mine with the required construction plant for the infrastructure. In this respect three aspects can be distinguished - namely, 1. the conveyor plant for the transport of water, waste and coal away from the coalfield; 2. the plant for opening up the area to traffic; and the 3. plant for surface construction work at the extraction base and dumping base.

title: MINIMIZING FAILURES OF TRUCK HOIST CYLINDERS AND FRAMES.
authors: Blaylock J.
abstract: Normally, the hydraulic system and structures are considered to be unrelated items. In reality, the two cannot be separated because one affects and depends on the other to function properly. This paper explores the potential failure areas of hydraulic cylinders, such as used on open-pit mine trucks, and suggests possible methods to prevent failures from occurring. The use of high-strength low-alloy steel in frames is reviewed and the benefits discussed.

title: COMPUTER APPLICATIONS IN OPEN-PIT MINE PLANNING.
authors: Garg O.; Piche A.
abstract: This paper summarizes the computer applications in open-pit mine planning at the Iron Ore Company of Canada (IOC). A brief history of the use of computers at IOC is given, and a description of the existing facilities is outlined. The following systems are discussed: storage and retrieval of geological data; geotechnical data analysis; long-term grade and tonnage forecasting; ore grading; and open-pit mine design. Justification for using computers in open-pit mine planning is given, and possible future areas of application are considered.

title: AMERICAN NUCLEAR IS BROADENING ITS HORIZONS.
authors: White L.
abstract: A brief outline is given of the expanding activities of American Nuclear Corp. in uranium drilling mining and milling. Currently one of the smaller companies participating in U. S. uranium development, American Nuclear is mapping out plans to quadruple feed capacity at its Gas Hill mill, from 1,000 stpd to 4,000 stpd, and is also developing its new Cotter Ferguson open-pit mine in the Gas Hills. In the northern Powder River Basin, the company is conducting detailed drilling on properties held jointly with TVA to define reserves that may become the basis of a mine-mill complex, with startup possible in 1984. Further, seismic techniques are being used to identify channels of possible uranium deposition under the Sweetwater Plateau south of the Gas Hills.

title: TREND TOWARDS MECHANICAL DRIVES FOR OPEN-PIT MINE HAULAGE TRUCKS.
authors: Williams R.
abstract: There has been a trend to the mechanical drive concept in the 85-ton class truck during the past few years. It appears that this trend is continuing throughout the range of mid-size end dump trucks, up to and including 120-ton units.

title: Impressions of the Chinese Mining Industry.
authors: Fettweis G.
abstract: The author gives his impressions, obtained during a visit to the Chinese People's Republic from Oct. 21 to Nov. 4, 1977, of mining operations in the northern, northeastern, and southern parts of China, with particular attention paid to coal mining. After briefly noting the estimated coal reserves in China, the organization of the mining industry, the degree of modernization, and estimated output, the author discusses the damage caused by the earthquakes of 1976 and reviews the mining techniques currently used, most of the coal mines being undergound mines worked by longwall retreating. Finally, the author describes his visits to two underground coal mines and one open-pit mine.

title: Development of Scheelite Mining at Mittersill.
source: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
authors: Spross W.
abstract: A short historical review of the discovery, exploration and development of the scheelite deposit in the Felbertal near Mittersill, Austria, is presented. Details are given of the open-pit mine planning, ore extraction, and stripping operations. The development of the deposit's western part for underground mining is also covered, and some aspects of the ore dressing operations are outlined.

title: GEOLOGY OF THE CARGILL PHOSPHATE DEPOSIT IN NORTHERN ONTARIO.
authors: Sandvik P.; Erdosh G.
abstract: The Cargill phosphate deposit, located 32km. southwest of Kapuskasing, was discovered in 1975 and has been evaluated through an extensive program of 190 drill holes, numerous chemical analyses, metallurgical tests, and engineering and economic studies. The alkalic complex, comprising principally carbonatite and pyroxenite-amphibolite rocks, has been interpreted to have been intruded into the rift system of the Kapuskasing High during late Precambrian near the intersection of northeast- and northwest-trending faults. The complex is one of at least ten known alkalic complexes in or close to the magnetic-gravity-high system and is expressed by an elongated, northeast-oriented, three-part magnetic anomaly 7. 2km. long by 2. 3km. wide. Vermiculite, columbium-bearing minerals, clay minerals and quartz sand are present in quantities that suggest the possibility of commercial development. Uranium is absent or occurs only in very minor amounts. A tentative open-pit mine, designed for preliminary feasibility studies, is estimated to contain a probable phosphate-bearing deposit of 62. 5 million metric tons at an average grade of 19. 6 per cent P//2O//5.

title: Mechanism of Deformation of Rocky and Semirocky Banks.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Turintsev Y.; Golubko B.
abstract: Based on natural and laboratory investigations, a hypothesis is worked out about the mechanism of deformation of rocky and semirocky open-pit mine slopes in pre-limit and limit equilibrium stages. The proposed hypothesis permits prediction of the character of development of the deformation of banks. This is necessary for timely and correct elaboration of measures to prevent such deformations.

title: CANADA TUNGSTEN - CHANGE TO UNDERGROUND MINING & DESCRIPTION OF MINE-MILL PROCEDURES.
authors: Cummings W.; Bruce D.
abstract: Canada's only current tungsten producer started up in 1962 with a small open-pit mine on the Flat River, 130 air miles north of Watson Lake, Yukon Territory. The orebody was in a contact-metamorphic skarn zone and contained about 1. 5 million tons of ore grading an estimated 2. 47% WO//3 and 0. 5% copper. Near the end of the open pit, a new zone was discovered on the lower limb of the same structure, and the decision to go underground was made in 1972. A continuing program of change and up-grading is necessary in the conversion from a seasonal open-pit mine with limited life to an underground operation with twenty years of reserves. Changes are necessary in plant and services as well as the mine. This paper sums up the changes in the operation since 1971 and outlines the changes yet to come.

title: Use of Explosives at the Kiruna Mine.
authors: Sundholm R.
abstract: The LKAB Company exploits two underground iron mines and one open-pit mine in the Swedish Lapland. Total output of these three mines is 60 million tons/yr of ore and gangue. Consumption of explosives at the three mines is significant and has spurred LKAB to produce its own explosives: output in 1975 consisted of 9,705 tons of ANFO explosive, 5,229 tons of explosive slurries and 9,936 tons of Kimit (a water-gel explosive called Tremite in the U. S. ). The use of Kermit was introduced by LKAB to solve the problem of fumes from blasting in the underground mines. The Kirma mine is briefly described, and the reasons that prompted LKAB to manufacture and use Kermit are explained.

title: DESIGNING OF OPEN-PIT MINES - THE OPEN-PIT MINE AT THE UDOKAN COPPER DEPOSIT.
authors: Sedlow M.G.
abstract: The Udokan copper deposit is one of the biggest deposits in the world with the copper grade of 1. 5%. The mining conditions are favorable for open-cast operations. Production of 35 million tons per year of ore or 90 million m**3 of ore and waste is due to be attained in two stages with the help of heavy-duty shovels and dumpers. With the deepening of the open-pit and greater distances, possible use of continuous-type transport facilities will have to be considered. All equipment, buildings and constructions must meet arctic conditions.

title: Industrial Tests of Different Types of the Top Structure of Permanent Rail Tracks.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Volkov G.; Kutkin A.; Popov Y.
abstract: An experimental open-pit mine rail track sector with different construction of its top structure has been built at the Sarbay open-pit mine of the Sokolovsko-Sarbayskiy Ore Dressing Combine in Kazakhstan. It is designed for tracks with inclinations of up to 60 per 1000 and axial loads on the rolling stock of up to 35 t. Industrial tests of timber and - both serially produced and experimental strengthened - concrete sleepers laid on ballasts of different thickness have been staged. Results of experimental measurements of stresses in rails and sleepers, and of pressures on the basic area of the bed arising when the PE-2M traction unit moves over it are presented.

title: ASBESTOS HILL-NORDENHAM STORY: THE OPEN-PIT MINE AT ASBESTOS HILL.
authors: Roussin R.
abstract: Annual production from the Asbestos Hill pit is 1,550,000 tons of asbestos ore, with a yield varying between 18 and 20%. The orebody was exposed at the top of a hill, and initial production started without having to remove any overburden. The final pit will be 2300 feet long by 1000 feet at the longest and widest points. The final depth will be 680 ft. A pit slope stability study was carried out and an average wall angle of 60-70 degrees must be maintained. Preshearing of final pit limits will produce good wall stability. Permanent access ramps will be 60 ft wide, with an 8% maximum grade. Geological conditions and the low rock temperature are the major causes of the operation's drilling and blasting problems.

title: DIRECT REDUCTION HEATS UP IN STEELMAKING.
authors: Miller J.
abstract: A mini-hydraulic slurry mining program that is scheduled to strip 265,000 cu yd of redeposited silt from the Caland open-pit iron mine near Aitkon, Ont. , is described. The program is a microcosm of an earlier project at the site - one of the largest preproduction dredging and water diversion projects in mining and construction history - but it will help Caland, an Inland Steel Co. subsidiary, obtain a new lease on mining life. For Marconflo, the Caland effort marks the first use of its slurry repulp and reclaim system at an open-pit mine - a new addition to a growing list of actual and conceptual slurry handling applications. A tandem set of Marconflo units, Dynajet 1000 capsule and a caisson 1000 jet, are briefly described.

title: Plotting Open-Pit Mine Plans by Means of a Device for Graphic Data Output from Computers.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Bogachev A.; Omelin V.
abstract: A system of graphic man-computer interaction is proposed for utilization in solving problems of plotting open-pit mines by the method of selection. The article describes the experience of using such a system developed at the All-Union Institute of Mineral Prospecting Geophysics in application to geological and mining problems. The system of graphic interaction consists of a computer set, including a CRT display and a graphic data input device.

title: LASER SURVEY CONTROL OF DIVERSION TUNNEL DRIVE SAVES TIME AND MONEY AT KENNECOTT'S RAY MINE.
authors: Goff J.S.; Bills R.F.
abstract: Laser guidance systems for survey control of tunneling are quickly gaining wide acceptance in the mining industry. One method for control of curves, recently employed at the Ray open-pit mine of Kennecott Copper Corp. in Arizona, has apparently broken some new ground. The laser control system was put into action in driving a diversion tunnel for Mineral Creek, which flowed across the proposed northeast boundary of the Ray pit. Fluor Utah Inc. began the tunnel construction using conventional drill and blast methods in November 1970. Tunnel cross-section and length necessitated the use of rail-mounted equipment. Details of laser beam application in construction of the tunnel are described.

title: Simplified Method of Determination of the Slipping Surface and the Safety Margin Coefficient in an Isotropic Medium.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Okatov R.; Popov I.; Shaburnikov A.; Fedorov V.
abstract: A simplified analytical method is worked out for the determination of the safety margin coefficient when investigating the stability of spoil slopes and open-pit mine edges. A circular, cylindrical form of the slipping surface is accepted. This method is simpler than the generally accepted graphic solution.

title: ISUA, GREENLAND: CALCULATIONS OF GLACIER FLOW FOR AN OPEN-PIT MINE.
source: U S Army Cold Reg Res Eng Lab Res Rep
authors: Colbeck S.
abstract: Investigation of the possibility of developing an open-pit mine along the edge of the Greenland Ice Cap. The response of the glacier to a sudden change in surface slope and thickness is calculated. The existing flow is diverted away from the mineral deposit but will increase when the excavation begins. It is calculated that 66 million cubic meters of ice must be removed to establish a stable profile beyond the pit.

title: The age of sulfide mineralization at Rossland, British Columbia
authors: Fyles J.; Harakal J.; White W.
abstract: Mines near the city of Rossland in the West Kootenay district of southeastern British Columbia were important producers of copper and gold from 1894 to 1928 and of molybdenum since 1966 from an open-pit mine near the copper-gold camp. Eighteen new K-Ar dates of plutonic, dike, and volcanic rocks indicate that the age of the oldest pluton (the Rossland monzonite) is more than 90 m.y. and that all the other rocks are between 46 and 52 m.y. Geological relationships show that the molybdenite is older than the copper-gold mineralization. The molybdenite is about 48 m.y. because it is cut by 48.1 m.y. dikes and occurs in fractures which cut quartz diorite with an apparent age of 48.7 m.y. The copper-gold mineralization is younger than lamprophyre dikes with an average age of 48.2 m.y. and is thought to be about this age. Mineralization in the Rossland camp, therefore, is Tertiary and appears to be genetically associated with two bodies of quartz diorite and granodiorite formerly regarded as part of the Nelson plutonic suite. © 1973 Society of Economic Geologists, Inc.

title: Statistical Evaluation of the Interrelation Between Rock and Ore Volumes When Mining Deposits of Different Types.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Arsent'ev A.; Gritsai A.; Ovodenko B.
abstract: A method is presented for quick evaluation of the possible boundaries of open-pit mines and the productivity of the mines as regards the volume of rock and mineral. The method consists in finding the coefficient of nonuniformity of overburden removal over a period and the ratio of useless rock extracted during the period of construction of an open-pit mine. Deposits with different bedding of ore bodies are classified and represented schematically and the influence of the thickness of the overburden on the coefficient of overburden removal is investigated by the method of modeling. For the initial period of operation the coefficient of nonuniformity of overburden removal is 1. 25 (until the extraction of about 40% of ore reserves).

title: Evaluation of the Stability of Open-Pit Mine Edges by the Dynamic Programming Method.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Popov S.; Reznikov M.
abstract: The way of constructing the weakest possible slope or edge surface of an open-pit mine is considered. It is based on the use of the method of dynamic programming. The slope is divided into N vertical prisms, and each of the boundaries of an elementary prism into m sections. The problem is formulated as follows: it is necessary to find in the region of the possible location of the weakest surface such a line, beginning at the base points and ending at the right-hand boundary of the prism N, along which the difference between the restraining and the shifting forces is minimal. The formulated optimality principle makes it possible to solve this problem. A program is compiles and tested in the BESM-4 computer codes for the realization of an algorithm. Variation of the rock properties during transition from one elementary prism to another is allowed.

title: Kinematic Features of Scooping Blown-up Rock by Single-Bucket Open-Pit Mine Excavators.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Kubachek V.; Desov I.; Devyatkin Y.
abstract: Results are presented of investigations of the operation of the excavators with nominal bucket capacity from 3 to 8 cubic meters, designed by the Uralmash Plant, carried out at various open pit mines in the USSR. It is found that when working blown-up rock by open-put mine excavators, scooping takes place mostly thanks to crumbling falling of the debris down the slope of a heap. This determines essentially the parameters of the trajectories of scooping, displacement and relations of the speeds of the drives of the lifting and thrust mechanisms. Lack of correspondence of the presently accepted relations between lifting and thrust speeds and the conditions of scooping of blown-up rock is made evident. Recommendations are given for limiting the speed of lifting to 0. 6-0. 65 m/s during scooping and for its increase during the performance of auxiliary operations. This will make an increase in the productivity and efficiency of the excavators possible.

title: A three-dimensional consideration of the stresses surrounding open-pit mine slopes
source: International Journal of Rock Mechanics and Mining Sciences and
authors: Stacey T.
abstract: Models of open pits of circular and non-circular shape are analysed using the three-dimensional finite element method of stress analysis. The effects of different lateral latent stress fields and different plan radii of curvature of the slopes on the stress distributions are studied. Particular attention is paid to the circumferential stresses in the slope. It is found that the orientation of a non-circular pit with respect to the lateral stress field is very important when considering slope stability; the magnitude of tensile zones in the slope, and the presence of tensile zones in the pit floor both depend on this orientation. © 1973.

title: On the Type of Open-Pit Mine Loading Machines for Hard Rock.
authors: Spivakovskii A.
abstract: Designing of a face loading machine of continuous action for loading and conveying large-size rock pieces, resulting from blasting hard rock deposits in order to speed up and automate transportation, is considered. Two types of such machines are discussed: with scooping and raking working organs. It is recommended that one of the designs proposed, namely, a continuous-action machine with a blade rotor and paired raking paws, be adopted for development and manufacture. This machine would weigh about 200 t and its capacity would be 1500-1800 t/h.

title: MINE EVALUATION AND PRODUCTION SCHEDULING (MEPS).
authors: Bosman H.
abstract: Over the past five years, contributions from geologists and mining engineers were instrumental in the successful development of MEPS. It is a system of FORTRAN programs specifically designed to be used by mining personnel to solve geological and mining problems. MEPS is a flexible keyword-driven system. Extensive error editing procedures significantly reduce the time required to proceed from problem recognition to solution. Possibly the most attractive feature of MEPS is that computer solutions may be guided or selectively modified to obtain desired solutions. Some highlights of MEPS are: vocabulary that is familiar to mining people; geological data storage and retrieval; statistical analysis and variograms; contour maps of assays and geological horizons; trend surface analysis with residual evaluation; ore reserve calculations; open-pit mine design; marginal profitability calculations on pit walls; production scheduling; and vertical cross-section plots indicating pit outlines, ore grade contours and selected geological horizons.

title: On the Method of Calculation of the Upper Structure of Permanent Open-Pit Mine Tracks.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Volkov G.; Kutkin A.
abstract: Recently, the traction units of the PE-2, PE-2M and Ye-10 type with motor dump-cars, with 31 t load per axle, have been put into operation at open-pit mines in the USSR. In this connection it became necessary to investigate the conditions of operation of the existing upper structure of permanent tracks under high axial loads. The article describes an experiment designed to measure the stress in the upper structure of the track in the access trench to the Sarbay open pit ore mine in Kazakhstan. As a result, the method of calculating the strength of the track, built on wooden and on reinforced concrete ties, has been corrected. Possible designs of reinforced concrete slabs are shown.

title: Driving an Inclined Trench for the Skip Hoist at the Sibay Open-Pit Mine.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Khokhryakov V.; Sorokin L.; Moor A.; Galkin A.
abstract: The experience of driving an inclined trench for a skip hoist of Sibay open-put copper ore mine is generalized. The lifting capacity of the skip is 40 t, maximum depth of the hoist - 380m, the gradient - 39 degree , maximum hoist speed - 8. 2 m/s. The length of the trench (first stage) to the depth of 180m is 286m, its bottom width - 14. 5m, top width - 28 to 65m. It is to be equipped with two rail tracks 3. 07m wide each. The drilling and blasting work and the technology of stoping of the steep skip trench are described in detail. Recommendations are given for improving the technology of driving an inclined trench.

title: Solving the Static Problem of Determination of the Boundaries of Open-Pit Mines.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Atamas P.
abstract: The existing principles of static determination of open-pit mine limits are considered and a new principle is proposed, based on comparing the mean weighted boundary coefficient and the mean exploitation coefficient of overburden stripping. It is shown that application of the principle permits fuller utilization of possibilities and an expansion of the field of application of the open-pit method of mining.

title: Determination of Rational Direction of the Sinking of an Open-Pit Mine by the Method of Proportioning of the Working Zone.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Evsin V.; Maulyanbaev T.; Alenichev V.
abstract: A new method is described concerning the shaping of the open-pit area in accordance with generally accepted criteria by means of proportional correlation of the parameters of the working zone. The direction of the sinking of thepit is determined by the equation of minimal relations of projections of the open pit working zones as to the rock volume and ore at different pit edges. The dependences obtained are valid for ore and several ore bodies separated by rock layers. The use of this method does not involve the measuring of the areas by a planimeter on geological sections and approximation of the contours of the deposit and of the pit, it sharply reduces the volume of calculations. The method can be easily realized on a computer. It has been practically tested at Sarbay open-pit mine in Kazakhstan.

title: Artificial Ventilation of Deep Open-Pit Mines.
source: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
authors: Veselov A.; Faddeev B.
abstract: The existing and proposed mobile installations for the ventilation of deep open-pit mines by means of free turbulent streams show considerable drawbacks and are unsuitable for this task. Only the lower part of the open-pit mine, and not its entire volume, should be ventilated. For this purpose, suction ventilating installations with modern centrifugal ventilation mounted on the surface of the open-pit mine, should be used. They should be equipped with strongly-built suction air ducts laid on the edge of the open-pit mine and extending to its bottom.

title: TWIN BUTTES. A DEEP LOW-GRADE COPPER PRODUCER
authors: CALDWELL AB
abstract: At Twin Buttes near Tucson, Ariz, the Anaconda Co has recently completed the largest earth-moving task so far undertaken in the mining industry, removing 235 million tons of rock and overburden to uncover a complex deposit of ore grading slightly over 0. 5% copper and lying between 600 and 800 ft beneath the surface. How and why this was done, and what the results have been so far are set forth in detail in this survey of the complete operation at Anaconda's huge new open-pit mine. Article describes the equipment used, maintenance program by which down time is minimized and the methods by which mining and milling are accomplished. It also gives background detail in this survey of the complete operation atAnaconda's huge new openpit mine. Article describes the equipment used, maintenance program by which down time is minimized and the methods by which mining and milling are accomplished. It also gives background details on the geology and discovery of the orebody.

title: OPEN-PIT PLANNING USING A COMPUTER
authors: BOYCE WP
abstract: A system is described which uses a computer to determine the annual extraction sequence and final excavation extent of an existing, or a proposed open-pit mine. This system uses estimates of capital and operating costs for a range of annual outputs of ore and waste materials, and the physical properties of the potential pit area, to calculate ranges of unit costs and associated pit extents. It determines the scale of operations and final pit extent which would give maximum net monetary return, and then assesses the profitability of this return.

title: The porphyry copper deposit exposed in the liberty open-pit mine near Ely, Nevada. Part II. the formation of hydro-thermal alteration zones
authors: Fournier R.
abstract: In the southwest part of the Liberty pit a large porphyry body exhibits a zonal alteration pattern related to fissures and pyrite-bearing veins. The outermost zone contains unaltered K-feldspar, kaolinite after plagioclase, and black biotite after hornblende. An intermediate zone contains reconstituted K-feldspar, phlogopitic biotite, and muscovite or muscovite plus K-feldspar replacing only plagioclase. In the innermost zone the only silicates are quartz and muscovite. In some places an alteration band of K-feldspar after plagioclase separates kaolinite and muscovite. The widespread association of kaolinite and K-feldspar in hydro-thermal alteration zones suggests that these two minerals were stable together at the time of formation. Experimental data show that, where quartz controls the activity of silica in solution, kaolinite and K-feldspar should react to form muscovite. However, calculations predict that, at 15,000 psi, solutions with silica activities compatible with amorphous or gelatinous silica could stabilize K-feldspar and kaolinite relative to muscovite at temperatures below about 250° C. The rapid decomposition either of plagioclase feldspar or montmorillonite is considered a prime cause for the attainment of such high activities of silica in pore solutions of rock. The supersaturation of pore solutions with silica is a transient condition; quartz precipitates where kaolinite and K-feldspar react to give muscovite. Thus, the zonally distributed alteration at Ely is considered to have taken place after the rock had cooled to below 250° C. In contrast, the diffusely distributed muscovite and montmorillonite found in another portion of the pit probably commenced at 600° to 700° C with only minor formation of alteration products below 250° C. © 1967 Society of Economic Geologists, Inc.

title: The porphyry copper deposit exposed in the liberty open-pit mine near Ely, Nevada. Part I. Syngenetic formation
authors: Fournier R.
abstract: Detailed mapping- of the Liberty open-pit copper mine indicates that a monzonite porphyry complex was emplaced into a folded sedimentary sequence during active faulting in Cretaceous time. The upper portion of the intruded igneous material was the first to solidify and at times mobile mushes of plagioclase, hornblende, and biotite crystals in a viscous groundmass were injected along lines of rupture into already solid and altered upper portions of the same igneous body. Alteration of the upper part of the porphyry complex took place simultaneously with the continued injection and crystallization of magma from deeper in the system. First, K-feldspar partly replaced plagioclase and later, muscovite replaced most of the remaining plagioclase. Phlogopitic biotite containing rutile replaced hornblende and iron-rich biotite. This alteration preceded the final emplacement of a second, comagmatic portion of the rock which in turn exhibits an alteration suite mainly composed of iron-rich biotite, montmorillonite, and the zeolites, chabazite and stilbite. The distribution of sulfides in igneous rocks and immediately adjacent sediments suggests that the sulfides originated in the porphyries and locally escaped into the surrounding rock as the porphyries crystallized. Most chalcopyrite, the main primary copper-bearing mineral, is distributed as grains in the groundmass with no trace of alignment along earlier cracks. The groundmass which contains the chalcopyrite is composed mainly of aplitic-textured K-feldspar and quartz, and it formed at the time of the original crystallization of the rock and not as a result of later alteration processes. In some rocks the groundmass K-feldspar contains a greater proportion of potassium than does coexisting phenocryst K-feldspar. If a dense aqueous pore fluid had been present during the cooling history of the rock these feldspars should have equilibrated by base exchange of Na+ and K+. It is postulated that the formation of hydrous alteration products after feldspar and hornblende may effectively have kept the fugacity of water low in the porphyry as it cooled so that only an attenuated gas phase existed in the pores of the rock. © 1967 Society of Economic Geologists, Inc.
