keywords: Automatic total station | Banský model | Geologický model | MONITORING | Probabilistic models | Simulation surfaces
abstract: The application of computer technology by simulating opencast mining and deposits of raw materials. The mathematic principles of three-dimensional probabilistic models of raw materials deposits and a familiarization with the user interface software GEOLOGICKY MODEL. The principles of the simulation of opencast mines, generation intersections with models of raw materials deposits, computation of mining materials with the quality scaling,and the design of advanced mining with the software BANSKY MODEL. The monitoring the potential of dynamic movements' of unstable slopes with the automatic total station and a following interpretation in general time intervals by means of the software MONITORING.

title: Soil quality standards (SQS) for bio-reclamation of coal overburden dumps: ISO-14000 requirements
authors: Nikhil K.
keywords: 14000 | Bio-reclamation of coal overburden dumps | Soil quality standard (SQS)
abstract: In India 18,289 hectares of land is under various type of land degradation due to coal mining in which 1100 ha is by overburden dump. With the increase demand of coal and its opencast mining degrade 1400 ha of fertile land every year. This deterioration in the fertility is due to loss of soil through water erosion, contamination through leaching of heavy metals and siltation with runoff. The essential nutrients with micro-flora and fauna from the soil disappear from the mining affected areas. In environmental management plan and under the ISO certification for environment ISO: 14000 must include soil as important input and output character in the reclamation process and their must be defined standards in the successful mine closure. In this paper a brief discussion is made to define the soil quality standard for the reclamation of affected mining land to meet the ISO: 14000 norms in the mine closure. © Enviromedia Printed in India. All rights reserved.

title: Impact of opencast coal mining on soil environment and its management
source: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
authors: Gupta I.; Gorai A.C.
abstract: Opencast mining causes land degradation, land fragmentation, soil disruption, soil contamination, erosion and soil quality degradation. The contribution of opencast mining to total coal production around 350 million tonnes in India during 2003-04 was more than 75%. Mine spoils created due to opencast mining not fit for plant growth due to their high concentration of heavy metals and destruction of flora and fauna. The paper describes the procedures to improve the damage to the soil and improve the ability to support plant growth in long term. It also includes the practices of mine rehabilitation with emphasis on revegetation. The same can also be adapted in rejuvenation of mined out areas.

title: Plant communities on ironstone outcrops: A diverse and endangered Brazilian ecosystem
authors: Jacobi C.M.; Do Carmo F.F.; Vincent R.C.; Stehmann J.R.
keywords: Biodiversity | Canga | Ferruginous rocky field | Iron Quadrangle | Opencast mining | Quadrilátero Ferrífero
abstract: Mountain areas are recognized centres of endemism and diversity on account of their isolation and altitudinal diversity. In tropical regions, mountain tops usually stand as islands of xeric vegetation among mesophytic assemblages. Unlike the vegetation growing on other rock outcrops lithologies, such as inselbergs (granite/gneiss) or campos rupestres (quartz/arenite), ironstone outcrop plant communities still lack systematic studies in Brazil. These outcrops (locally known as canga) share most of the characteristics of other rock outcrops, such as isolation and edapho-climatic harshness, but differ in that they are the object of opencast mining, and thus subjected to irrecoverable degradation. In addition, they are expected to harbour metal-tolerant and hyperaccumulator plant species. A botanical survey of two ironstone outcrop locations in the most important mining region of southeastern Brazil, the Iron Quadrangle, revealed a high within-site (138 and 160 species per site), and between-site diversity (only 27% of common species), totaling 64 families and 234 species among basal families and eudicots (154 species), monocots (68 species), and ferns (12 species). Canga crusts are rich in dicots, several of which play an important role in community structuring, together with the more usual monocot aggregations. Distinct plant communities are found associated to different microhabitats within the iron crust, depending primarily on the amount of soil and moisture retention in the different microtopographies. The environmental uniqueness, high diversity, lack of studies and rapid destruction of these ecosystems pose an immediate challenge for their conservation. © 2007 Springer Science+Business Media, Inc.

title: Development of mining system at Neyveli
source: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
authors: Ansari A.; Paramasivam R.
abstract: Neyveli Lignite Corporation (NLC), Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu, India, is developing mining technologies and systems. The company is developing mining systems, to extract lignite ore for power generation. It continues to develop new mining technologies and systems, such as bucket wheel excavators, belt conveyors, and spreaders, to excavate large quantities of overburden and lignite. The company used underground and opencast mining methods, to extract lignite ore from mining operations. It selected discontinuous mining equipment, such as draglines, power shovel, along with continuous equipment, such as excavators, wagons, and conveyors for transporting excavated lignite. The advantages and disadvantages of the two types of equipment were evaluated, while selecting them for mining operations. The company also modified the continuous type machines according to the requirements of hard soil conditions existing in the area.

title: Environmental performance
source: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
authors: Ansari A.; Ravindranath M.
abstract: Neyveli Lignite Corporation, Tamil Nadu, India, is focusing on better ecology development and pollution control. The company has adopted monitoring strategies, to control liquid, or gaseous effluents that are being released into the environment from its mining and power generating units. It has adopted afforestation programs, and reclamation of waste land development, to control pollution and improve environmental conditions. It has realized the environmental impact of opencast mining operations. It is adopting certain environmental friendly measures, to protect the environment from the impact of opencast mining operations. It has installed 13 ambient air quality monitoring stations, to monitor the level of air pollution. It also sprays the haul roads inside the mines, to suppress dust and pollution.

title: Productivity analysis of extraction methods applied in coal mining at Tuncbilek Region
authors: Uygun M.; Kasap Y.; Konuk A.
keywords: Coal | Energy | Total factor productivity
abstract: In this study, total factor productivity method is used to compare productivity of different extraction methods applied in coal mining. Firstly, total factor productivity ratios are calculated by using the production factor data for in underground and opencast mining at GLI, a subsidiary of TKI. Then statistical analysis of total factor ratios productivity revealed that opencast mining is generally more productive in GLI. However, concerning that the 80 per cent of coal reserves in the license area of GLI is suitable to only underground mining, some regulations must be made over the production factors to increase the total factor productivity.

title: Bioreclamation of coalmine overburden dumps - With special empasis on micronutrients and heavy metals accumulation in tree species
authors: Maiti S.K.
keywords: Bioaccumulation | Bioreclamation | Coalmine overburden dumps | Metals | Tree
abstract: Major environmental impacts of opencast mining are degradation of landscape and aesthetics of the area by creating huge overburden dumps and deep voids at the mining sites. These overburden dumps are characterised by high rock fragment contents, low moisture retention capacity, higher bulk density, low nutrients, lower pH and elevated metal concentrations. Overburden dumps are reclaimed by tree species for stabilising as well as pollution control and overall improvement of the visual aesthetics. A field study was carried out in the old reclaimed coal mine overburden dumps at KD Heslong project, Central Coalfields, India to study the physico-chemical changes in the reclaimed overburden dumps and determines the magnitude of trace elements accumulation in the planted tree species. Total, bioavailable and acid extractable trace metals concentration in minesoils of overburden dump and topsoil in the mining areas was compared with undisturbed soil. The study showed that tree plantation improves the moisture contents, bulk density, pH and overall nutrient contents of minesoils. The study revealed that lower pH in the minesoils increases the bioavailabity of metals but concentration were found within toxic limits. However, ratio between total and bioavailable metals was found lower in overburden dumps than topsoil due to low pH and lack of organic matter. Out of six tree species studied, Bambusa shows highest accumulation of Fe and Cr. Bioaccumulation coefficient for Cr and Zn was found 74 times in Bambusa and 83 times in Dalbergia sissoo. The results of the study underscore the need for close monitoring of trace elements in reclaimed overburden dumps. Tree species like Dalbergia sissoo, Eucalyptus, Cassia seamea, Acaccia mangium and Peltaphorum were found to be the best species for bioreclamation of overburden dumps. © Springer Science+Business Media, Inc. 2006.

title: Water quality impact assessment and management for opencast coal mining projects
authors: Maiti S.K.; Maiti P.
keywords: Impact assessment | Opencast coal mining | Wastewater treatment | Water pollution
abstract: Major pollution sources in opencast coal mining are pumping of mine effluents; run-off from coal stock yards, overburden dumps and haul roads; effluents from workshop and washing of heavy earth moving machinery (HEMM) and Coal Handling Plant (CHP); disposal sites of sludge from oil and grease trap; domestic effluents from colony In this paper a six-step-six activity model is suggested for planning and conduction of water quality impact studies for opencast mining project. At the end best practicable control measures being adopted at various opencast mining projects are also included. © 2007 - Kalpana Corporation.

title: Partial automation of large-sized items of lignite opencast mining machinery
source: World of Mining Surface and Underground
authors: Ballmann S.
abstract: Partial automation of large-sized items of lignite opencast mining machinery between various finished products, made by different manufacturers has been discussed. The strategies which are followed for the development are partial automation of loading cars and the radio remote control systems, automation of the spreader-tripper car delivery units, and automation of the excavator process. The automation of RWE Power's large-sized items of machinery is achieved by the fully automation of the tripper cars, partially-automated loading cars, automated of the excavator process and fully-automated dumping process. The systems used at the opencast mining end must be able to cope with the boundary conditions that are specific to the mining industry.

title: A study on application of Markovian decision process in drilling and blasting operation of opencast mines
source: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
authors: Brahma K.C.; Pal B.K.; Das C.
abstract: Indian mining industry today stands at a critical juncture looking for new directions of growth and improved competitiveness. Technological change continues to trigger change in industry as it grapples with problems of technology diffusion. There is a quantum jump in opencast mining production due to tremendous change in mining machine design. Drilling and blasting plays a vital role in opencast mining. It not only affects the cost of production directly but also influences the overall operational cost significantly. Lots of emphasis is being given on the optimum blast design to get uniform blast fragmentation with designed level floor so that the loading operations are swift and simple and less breakdown of the handling equipment. Thus, the success or failure of drill and blast methods cast a long shadow over the balance of the operations. In the present paper, the authors have attempted to develop models on drilling and blasting operation based on the Markov chain techniques. This technique has been found to be very effective in modelling other operational sub-tasks like charging and loading in opencast mining operation.

title: Embedded system for intelligent control of opencast machines
source: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
authors: Banerjee S.; Sil J.; Bhattacharyya P.
abstract: Sensor integration and ease of fault management are long addresses issues for opencast mining machines. With the advent of electronic BJT (bipolar junction transistors) to high speed micro-controllers/processors are available for advances automation. The present paper deals with on-board integration of all electronic device viz, from source to control processors; the issue of fault tolerance is also taken into account. High level abstraction using VHDL is used for experimental integration of the above scheme.

title: The use of hydrotransportation systems in the mining environment
source: Journal of the Southern African Institute of Mining and Metallurgy
authors: Brock S.
abstract: Increasing Importance is now rightly being placed on the 'side effects' of mining operations with regards health, safety and the environment, with the environmental aspect being considered more than at any other time in history. Operators must, however, deliver an economically sound system in order for their processes to continue being viable. With regards new environmental concerns, as well as the primary function of extraction, the 'incidentals' such as dust and noise must be considered when designing and implementing either shaft or opencast mining projects. Coupled with this, more attention is also being given to the life cycle implications of works, including their eventual decommissioning. This paper describes technology that has been designed to produce safe, environmentally acceptable results without compromising the efficient operation of primary mining function. In fact, it is likely that the system discussed can be used to enhance productivity along with the secondary benefits delivered. Over the past number of years, systems have been developed, tested and proven to hydraulically transport solid material over long distances without passing that material through any significant moving parts (e.g. pumps). This technology has recently been further developed in order to transport this material under atmospheric conditions while minimizing the volume of carrier fluid required. This paper will discuss the development, operating methodology and efficiency of the technology, while demonstrating the health, safety and environmental benefits that such a system can bring. © The Southern African Institute of Mining and Metallurgy, 2006.

title: Chemical and morphological indication of the state of lodgepole pine and scots pine in restored oil shale opencast mining areas in Estonia
authors: Kuznetsova T.; Mandre M.
abstract: Experimental comparative investigations of lodgepole pine (Pinus conforta) and Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris) plantations were carried out on exhausted oil shale opencast sites in Estonia, with the aim to assess the perspectives to avoid monocultures and to broaden the species list in the recultivation of areas destroyed by mining. The levelled detritus of the Narva opencast (59°15' N, 27°48' E) is characterized by rather extreme growth conditions for conifers: very alkaline (pH > 8.0) and stony substrate, lack of N in soil, destroyed water regime etc. The concentrations of nutrients vary in the growth substrate between plots and under different species. The needles of Scots pine contain more P, K, Ca than the needles of lodgepole pine. Comparison of the nutrient composition of two conifer species in 21-23-year-old plantations showed the deficiency of N, P and K and optimal concentrations of Ca an Mg in needles. Research indicated that lodgepole pine and Scots pine differ in their needle and shoot biomass as lodgepole pine formed longer and heavier needles and shorter and thicker shoots than Scots pine. Regardless of unfavourable soil conditions a good growth of stands have developed on levelled opencasts. From a practical point of view and taking into account the aim of the present study, besides the native Scots pine lodgepole pine from the list of introduced tree species for recultivation of oil shale opencast mining areas may be promising. © 2006 Estonian Academy Publishers.

title: Lean maintenance - Concept, procedure and usefulness
source: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
authors: Pal B.; Maiti J.
abstract: In the era of mechanization and automation, machines are just as much as employees as the humans. Each is paid per hour wage based on their value to the company's products and services. Usually the machines wages are much higher than human beings. When they make a break, make a mistake, or take a day off, the company loses profit. This is more so for highly capital intensive machines employed in industries such as opencast mining operations. Therefore, a near 100 per cent equipment uptime and reliability is demanded for such highly capital intensive machines. To prevent downtime (hence increasing uptime) from happening before it occurs, one must eliminate the basic stresses that cause the downtime. Lean maintenance can help by providing methods that allow reduced maintenance support and reduced maintenance overhead while achieving maximum permanent reduction of unscheduled downtime. This is done by systematically surveying and analyzing each machine and control system to determine which basic stresses are affecting each machine over time and laying out a scheme to protect each machine or control system from these stresses. Lean is a set of principles, concepts, and techniques designed to help find and eliminate waste., Lean maintenance starts with three categories of downtime: (i) downtime from operator or programmed error, (ii) downtime from inadequate preventive maintenance procedure or performance, and (iii) downtime from chronic wear and stress to circuit boards, hydraulic components and other system components. However, its main focus is on the third. The stresses are heat, vibration, oxidation and corrosion, dirt build-up, electrical voltage transients and current surges, hydraulic contaminations of dirt, water, acids and others. Major tools and processes to achieve lean maintenance improvements are:(i) assessing the situation through value stream mapping (VSM) and (ii) implementing changes through accelerated improvement workshops (AIW's) and 5-S (Sort, Simplify, Sweep, Standardize, Self Discipline) workshops for workplace organization and other tools. In this paper an attempt has been made to discuss the concept, procedure, and usefulness of lean maintenance for improving machine uptime and profit.

title: Soil mesofaunal responses to post-mining restoration treatments
authors: Andrés P.; Mateos E.
keywords: Bioindicators | Mining | Restoration | Soil mesofauna | Soil quality
abstract: As soil destruction is one of the most conspicuous environmental impacts of opencast mining, mining companies are compelled to restore the exploited areas and to develop monitoring programs to test the effectiveness of the restoration treatments. Soil physical and chemical parameters are usually used as soil quality indicators, but bioindicators are more promising as they evaluate the global soil capability to support its ecological functions. In this work, we used soil mesofaunal bioindicators to evaluate four post-mining restoration treatments (soil spreading, soil spreading + grass and herb sowing, soil spreading + tree planting and soil spreading + sowing + planting). Twelve years after restoration none of the treatments had achieved the restoration of the preoperational forest soil conditions. Soil spreading was the least effective treatment. Soil spreading + sowing and soil spreading + sowing + planting generated grassland soil conditions. Soil spreading + planting induced an incipient forest soil structure. Number of taxa, collembolan and oribatid species diversity and communites structure were the most sensitive mesofaunal parameters to evaluate the soil restoration treatments. © 2005 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved.

title: A techno-economic model for optimum regeneration of surface mined land
authors: Mukhopadhyay M.K.; Sinha I.N.
keywords: Coal | Disposal optimization | Economic vectors | India | Mining remediation | Overburden disposal | Sensitivity analysis | Surface land generation
abstract: The recent global scenario in the mineral sector may be characterized by rising competitiveness, increasing production costs and a slump in market price. This has pushed the mineral sector in general and that in the developing countries in particular to a situation where the industry has a limited capacity to sustain unproductive costs. This, more often than not, results in a situation where the industry fails to ensure environmental safeguards during and after mineral extraction. The situation is conspicuous in the Indian coal mining industry where more than 73% production comes from surface operations. India has an ambitious power augmentation projection for the coming 10 years. A phenomenal increase in coal production is proposed from the power grade coalfields in India. One of the most likely fall-outs of land degradation due to mining in these areas would be significant reduction of agricultural and other important land-uses. Currently, backfilling costs are perceived as prohibitive and abandonment of land is the easy way out. This study attempts to provide mine planners with a mathematical model that distributes generated overburden at defined disposal options while ensuring maximization of backfilled land area at minimum direct and economic costs. Optimization has been accomplished by linear programming (LP) for optimum distribution of each year's generated overburden. Previous year's disposal quantity outputs are processed as one set of the inputs to the LP model for generation of current year's disposal output. From various geo-mining inputs, site constants of the LP constraints are calculated. Arrived value of economic vectors, which guide the programming statement, decides the optimal overburden distribution in defined options. The case example (with model test run) indicates that overburden distribution is significantly sensitive to coal seam gradient. The model has universal applicability to cyclic system (shovel-dumper combination) of opencast mining of stratified deposits. © Springer-Verlag 2006.

title: Dump design for opencast mine based on land-conserving
source: Nongye Gongcheng Xuebao Transactions of the Chinese Society of Agricultural Engineering
authors: Wei B.; Fu M.; Bai Z.; Fu W.
keywords: Dump | Land-conserving | Reclamation area | Rock-earth volume | Stabilization
abstract: Land-conserving plays an important role in the building of resource-conserving society. The relationship among dump formation and rock-earth volume in opencast mine were discussed by geometry analysis. Then the correlation model was constructed and proved by the example of Shangyao Dump of Anjialing opencast mining in Pingshuo. As a result, it will get the aim of land-conserving and insure the stabilization of dump if the relationship between the length of slope and the width of step is taken into account logically when the Dump is designed.

title: Properties of mine soil and its affects on bioaccumulation of metals in tree species: Case study from a large opencast coalmining project
source: International Journal of Mining Reclamation and Environment
authors: Maiti S.K.
keywords: Bioaccumulation | Heavy metals | Mine soil | Reclamation | Tree species
abstract: Opencast mining results in severe destruction of the landscape due to the formation of overburden dumps and voids at mining sites, increased erosion, altered aesthetics and an increased pollution load onto the surroundings. Reclamation of these mine dumps forms an integral part of environmental management plan for any mining project. An advance understanding of the properties of mine soil (e.g. rock geochemistry, rock depth profiling) is important in the preparation of reclamation and closure plans. The studies undertaken in the Central Coalfield Limited (CCL) KD Heslong opencast project, revealed that the bioavailability of toxic metals depends on the physico-chemical characteristics of mine soil, and that bioaccumulation of toxic metals varies among tree species. In the nutritionally poor mine soil, the plant species Dalbergia sissoo, Cassia seamea, Acacia mangium and Acacia auriculiformis were found growing satisfactorily. Addition of topsoil and liming in the plantation pits was found to be essential and, if possible, incorporation of acid neutralizing materials such as fly ash should be undertaken. © 2006 Taylor & Francis.

title: Factal analysis of the dispersion of air pollutants
authors: Ghose M.K.
keywords: Coking coal | Dispersion | Dominant wind | Impact | Monitoring | Opencast
abstract: Factal analysis is a technique that can be utilized to assess the actual contribution of air pollutants to air quality and also to evaluate their effects following dispersion to surrounding locations. A large opencast coal project was chosen as the study area. This paper examines the sources of air pollution in the study area and focuses on the superimposition of air pollutants emitted by the project in question and by other surrounding activities The selection of air monitoring stations and methods adopted for air quality survey is described. Data were generated over the four seasons and they were critically analyzed on the basis of dominant wind directions at different seasons to establish the factal analysis concept. This paper concludes that the actual contribution of pollutants from opencast mining and their dispersion to the surrounding locations can be successfully evaluated by facial analysis technique The outcome of this study will enable mine officials to take appropriate steps to achieve the right kind of balance between sustainable development and environmental management. © 2006 Taylor & Francis.

title: Melioration of tilting clay/tone by means of flue-gas desulphurization plant-gypsum on an attempt surface in the opencast mining Nochten
authors: Haubold W.; Klingbeil J.; Preußner K.
abstract: The brown coal opencast mining Nochten in the northeast of Saxonia reached the offshoot of the Trebendorf high surface in the year 2003 with its carvings. The self-changing geological conditions, especially the substantial growth of the bottle clay/tone portion in the Deckgebirge, led to inevitable changes in the composition of the tilting substrates and higher requirement for melioration and recultivation.

title: Strength from within - Continuous improvements in opencast mining operations (KVT)
source: World of Mining Surface and Underground
authors: Gärtner D.; Sauthoff M.
abstract: A continuous improvement process in the various operations of the opencast-mines division (KVT) is launched to increase productivity from the bottom up along with in depth involvement of staff. The aim of KVT is a steady, sustainable increase in efficiency in all areas. The responsibility for the implementation and success of KVT lies with the executives in the line organization. The various operations in KVT process make use of a jointly defined toolbox. This contains methods like the KVT team (quality circle), hothouse (field trial), 7-A method, and benchmarking. The toolbox is compiled, updated and redeveloped by the coaches of all operating units, so that all staff can make use of it, as the involvement of all employees is the key to success.

title: Segregation calcinations of oxidized nickel ores in laboratorial and enlarged laboratorial scale
authors: Reznik I.; Shamin A.; Kharlakova T.; Kartamyshev N.
abstract: The reserves of oxidized nickel ores are large. Their opencast mining is cheap and safe. Ural enterprises has operating mines and metallurgical works, developed infrastructure; they are located in average climatic area and are provided with regular skilled personnel. Putting into practice the new concentrating plant will help 'Yuzhuralnickel' company to manufacture up to 25,000 f of nickel and 1,0001 of cobalt, using the existing equipment with high profitability. High efficiency of concentration of poor oxidized ores is clearly brought up by three calculation schemes undertaken on different dates and for different prices.

title: Seismic experiment on the North East edge of the Messel Pit using the environmental Inklinometer IN28
authors: Buness H.
keywords: Messel formation | Messel Pit | Reflection seismics
abstract: The Eocene deposit Grube Messel was not exploited by opencast mining at its northwestern edge. This area is presently affected by landslides. A hole 94 m deep was drilled in its center to measure changes of inclinations. The Leibniz Institute for Applied Geosciences (GGA-Institute) shot 3 short reflection seismic profiles in this area and reprocessed an older one. The eastern border of the deposit is documented with an E-W directed profile; the northern border can be recognized indirectly by dipping reflections. Both borders show a very steep dip. In the western section, the reflections reach a depth of only 120 m, compared to 240 m in the eastern section. The reflections are often bounded by faults. The reflections on the N-S trending profiles show dips towards the border of the deposit.

title: Seismic reconnaisance of an eozanen Maars (grube Messel)
authors: Buness H.; Harms F.J.; Nix T.
keywords: Diatrem | Maar | Messel formation | Messel pit | Reflection seismics
abstract: The Leibniz Institute for Applied Geosciences (GGA) conducted four reflection seismic profiles to clarify the structure of the Eocene deposit Grube Messel in preparation for the research bore hole at Messel in 2001. The profiles could be realized mainly using the vibroseis technique, despite a difficult terrain as the result of opencast mining. Sediments can be clearly recognized inside the former maar to a depth o f 240 m below the floor of Grube Messel. The Middle Messel Formation, which is the oil-shale deposit, appears seismically almost transparent and reaches a residual thickness of about 100 m. The Lower Messel Formation is characterized by strong reflections, which are partly continuous across the whole central area of the deposit. Below the sedimentary fill of the former maar, horizontal as well as steeply dipping reflections hint at a layering in the diatreme structure to a depth of about 600 m below the original surface.

title: Shaping the future - Opportunities attaching to real property, resettlement, mining damage and recultivation
source: World of Mining Surface and Underground
authors: Herbst A.
abstract: All activities flanking opencast mining operations are handled at RWE power by a central division, PFB, within the Mining portfolio. RWE Power is supporting the process of structural change with the surrender of real property no longer required for its operation. RWE power contribution also includes the assumption of all costs associated with land development, and also bears the cost of external land development or provides funds for kindergarten places. It also receives planning documents for individual building projects, all the way to comprehensive project planning records for scrutiny as regards mining damage. The mining damage prevention is an important module in minimizing the interference with the existing landscape.

title: Management of rock raw material resources in the Polish Carpathians on sustainable development conditioning
authors: Radwanek-Bak B.
keywords: Carpathians | Environmental impact | Resource protection | Resource valorisation | Rock mineral deposits | Sustainable development
abstract: A comprehensive approach to problems and conditions of management of mineral resources in the frames of sustainable development has been presented in an area of the Polish part of the Flysh Carpathians. This area, characterized by outstanding nature values includes scarce, although mined for the long time, rock mineral resources, as road and building stone (mainly sandstone), clay, natural aggregate and diatomite, which have been mined on the opencast technology. Some schemes of typical geological setting of the deposits as well as recent status of threir recognition and management have been discussed, and also the trends in the future application in the light of market conditions and ecological delimitations have been pointed out. Conflicts of mining/processing activity with natural environment has been assessed in details and possibilities of decreasing of the negative effects during all the stages of the deposit management has been analyzed. Landscape transformation manifesting itself in the surface exposition and changes in morphology is an important effect of the opencast mining in the Carpathians. The obtained regularities allowed to construct some conceptual models displaying synthetically typical kinds of anthropopression, and also environmental standards and indicators suitable for assessment of its level and ways to decrease it. In an effect of this analysis, the change of the common formula of geoenvironmental analysis from the form: impact→status→reaction to the form: impact→status→standard→reaction. The term "standard" refers to mining activity performed according to required environmental standards and to realize of final concept of abandoned mining areas. Such concept ought be prepared just during the stage of feasibility study and it should be included into spatial planning documents. Also the method of comprehensive multi-criterial valorization of mineral deposits and perspective areas has been elaborated for the purposes of resource protection. These concepts, together, form a concise system of evaluation of mineral resources allowing to make gradation of their protection level. The implemented valorization procedure makes possible to compare different rock raw materials on a base of the same uniform criteria, representative for three separated domaines of assessment: (1) geological-resource value (natural one), (2) recognition certainty (level of geological information), and (3) ecological conditions for land-use planning. A few of mineral resources in the Carpathian area have been qualified into a group of the highest protection after the implemented valorization method, what denotes mining of those mineral resources as an absolute priority. Also teen of the deposits have been qualified into a group of high protection, being natural reserves of regional scale. Moreover, a group of the deposits requiring detail recognition and revalorization before any decision on land-use planning has been defined here. In contrary to mineral deposits, treated as point objects, perspective areas have been considered as surficial objects and preliminary principles of their valorization using the GIS tools have been presented. Application of the differentiated levels of protection of mineral deposits and perspective areas should contribute to their real protection and to easier compromises on the field of sustain utilization of land and natural environment potential.

title: Risk analysis of liquefaction at an embankment of tailing sand
authors: Friedrich S.; Schreyer A.; Blumenberg E.; Ebersbach F.
abstract: In the gravel opencast mining Lüttow-Valluhn (Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania) an embankment consisting of tailing sand (0 to 2 mm) is under construction, dividing the later dredging pond into two parts and influencing the hydraulic conditions. In the length direction two safety pillars, each 50 m wide and consisting of natural grown material, should be preserved. The western safety pillar was partially mined on a length of 250 m. At the same time a screening plant for gravel and sand has been built on the tailing sand of the embankment. The size distribution of the tailing sand and the structural and hydraulic situation of the embankment gave rise to the assumption that the material is susceptible to liquefaction. Additional tests (e.g. cone penetration tests, radiometric measurements, triaxial tests on disturbed and undisturbed samples) demanded by the Mining Department Stralsund showed that the material is susceptible to liquefaction under the given on-site conditions. Because the liquefaction has to be initiated by an actual event, in an additional step on-site dynamic load tests combined with measurements of pore water pressure were conducted. The results showed that the dynamic impacts caused by the operation of the purification plant are not strong enough to cause liquefaction. Due to the results of the risk analysis, safety zones were defined and instructions for operation were given.

title: Ecological restoration of acidic coalmine overburden dumps - An Indian case study
authors: Maiti S.K.; Ghose M.K.
keywords: Coal-mine overburden dumps | Ecorestoration | Nutrients
abstract: Opencast mining results in the formation of large overburden (OB) dumps and voids at mining sites. The OB dumps can be acidic, due to local geochemistry. Reclamation of these dumps is an integral part of environmental management in any mining project. Overburden dumps of various ages were selected to monitor change in physico-chemical and nutrient properties. Increased stone content and reduced field moisture, together with higher bulk density, were found to be major constraints on the ecorestoration of OB dumps. Correlation studies showed that organic matter is the major source of available nitrogen and potassium in the overburden dumps. Bioavailable Mn, Fe, Zn and Cu were found both in acidic and neutral pH conditions. Bioavailable Zn was found at concentrations ten to 30 times greater than in natural soils. Higher bioavailability of metals in OB dumps may be due to relatively low concentrations of organic matter For the sustainable ecorestoration of acidic dumps, it is essential to increase the pH and organic matter content. During investigation, it was found that Dalbergia sissoo grows very well in these acidic dumps, and improves dump characteristics. © 2005 EPP Publications Ltd.

title: Assessment and prediction of contaminant migration in ground water from chromite waste dump
authors: Tiwary R.; Dhakate R.; Ananda Rao V.; Singh V.
keywords: Chromite mine waste | Contaminant migration | Groundwater modeling | Hexavalent chromium | Leachate
abstract: Sukinda chromite valley is one of the largest chromite deposits of the country and produces nearly 8% of chromite ore. It greatly contributes towards the economic development but at the same time deteriorates the natural environment. It is generally excavated by opencast mining method. In the Sukinda mining area, around 7.6 million tons of solid waste have been generated in the form of rejected minerals, overburden material/waste rock and sub-grade ore that may be resulting in environmental degradation, mainly causing lowering in the water table vis-à-vis deterioration in surface and ground water quality. The study conducted in and around one of the chromite mine of the valley reveals that the concentration of hexavalent chromium is found in the water samples of ground and surface water, mine effluents and seepage water. Hexavalent Chromium (Cr<sup>+6</sup>) have been found varying between 0.02 mg/l and 0.12 mg/l in mine effluents and 0.03-0.8 mg/l in shallow hand pumps and 0.05 and 1.22 mg/l in quarry seepage. The concentration of Cr<sup>+6</sup> in Damsal nalah, the main surface water source in the area, is found varying between 0.03 mg/l and 0.14 mg/l and a increasing trend, which is in the downstream of mining activities, has been observed. Leachate study clearly shows that the soil lying in the vicinity of mine waste dump shows highest concentration of Cr<sup>+6</sup>. Contaminant migration in ground water depends upon various geohydrological conditions of the area. The study shows that aquifer resistivity varies between 15 Ωm to 150 Ωm and aquifer depth varies from 4 m to 26 m below ground level. The ground water flow and mass transport models were constructed with the help of geo-hydrological and geophysical informations using Visual Modflow software. Contaminant migration and path lines for 20 years have been predicted in two layers model of ground water. The study provided an insight into the likely migration of contaminant in ground water due to leaching from overburden dump of chromite ore and will be helpful in making strategic planning for limiting the contaminant migration in the ground water regime in and around the mining areas. © Springer-Verlag 2005.

title: Liebherr, demonstrating new features
abstract: Leibherr will be exhibiting at Hillhead its R 954C Litronic excavator, PR 724 hydrostatic bulldozer and its modular, high technology concrete batching plants. The R 954c Litronic is a 50 t-class machine with a heavy-duty undercarriage is specifically designed and constructed for arduous applications in quarrying and opencast mining, and has a digging force of 244 kN and a breakout force of 307 kN. The PR 724 Bulldozer is fully hydrostatic with electronic drive control and is powered by a Liebherr-made. title: Soil conservation for rehabilitation and revegetation of mine-degraded land
source: TIDEE Teri Information Digest on Energy and Environment
authors: Ghose M.K.
abstract: The benefits of soil conservation for rehabilitation and revegetation of mine-degraded land are discussed. The impact of the deterioration of soil properties due to mining and stockpiling is also discussed. It is observed that the opencast mining severely disturbs land in and around the mining areas. It is stated that the gypsum can be used to improve the structure of poorly structured sodic soils.

title: Long-term final void salinity prediction for a post-mining landscape in the Hunter Valley, New South Wales, Australia
authors: Hancock G.R.; Wright A.; De Silva H.
keywords: Final void | Limnology | Mine lake | Salinity | Water quality | Water quality modelling
abstract: Opencast mining alters surface and subsurface hydrology of a landscape both during and post-mining. At mine closure, following opencast mining in mines with low overburden to coal ratios, a void is left in the final landform. This final void is the location of the active mine pit at closure. Voids are generally not infilled within the mines' lifetime, because of the prohibitive cost of earthwork operations, and they become post-mining water bodies or pit lakes. Water quality is a significant issue for pit lakes. Groundwater within coal seams and associated rocks can be saline, depending on the nature of the strata and groundwater circulation patterns. This groundwater may be preferentially drawn to and collected in the final void. Surface runoff to the void will not only collect salts from rainfall and atmospheric fallout, but also from the ground surface and the weathering of fresh rock. As the void water level rises, its evaporative surface area increases, concentrating salts that are held in solution. This paper presents a study of the long term, water quality trends in a post-mining final void in the Hunter Valley, New South Wales, Australia. This process is complex and occurs long term, and modelling offers the only method of evaluating water quality. Using available geochemical, climate and hydrogeological data as inputs into a mass-balance model, water quality in the final void was found to increase rapidly in salinity through time (2452 to 8909 mg 1 <sup>-1</sup> over 500 years) as evaporation concentrates the salt in the void and regional groundwater containing high loads of salt continues to flow into the void. Copyright © 2004 John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.

title: Evaluation of SRTM3 and GTOPO30 terrain data in Germany
authors: Denker H.
keywords: DEM | DEM evaluation | Digital elevation model | GTOPO30 | SRTM3 | Terrain data
abstract: High-resolution terrain data are crucial for gravity field modelling in mountainous regions. In areas without national digital elevation models (DEMs) available, fill-ins from global models have to be used. For this purpose, the global models GTOPO30 (30 resolution) and SRTM3 (3 resolution) are considered. The SRTM3 model has been released recently from the analysis of the Shuttle Radar Topography Mission and covers the latitudes between 60°N and 54°S, while the GTOPO30 model is a global public domain data set completed already in 1996. Li this contribution, 1 × 1 national DEMs for Germany are used to evaluate the global models. The differences between the best national models and the SRTM3 data show a standard deviation of 7.9 m with maximum differences up to about 300 m. The largest differences are located in opencast mining areas and result from the different epochs of the DEMs. Histograms of the differences reveal a clear deviation from the normal distribution with a long tail towards too high SRTM3 elevations. The evaluation of GTOPO30 shows that the longitudes should be increased by 30 (one block) in Germany. For the shifted GTOPO30 DEM, the standard deviation of the differences with respect to the best national model is 6.8 m, roughly 75 % smaller than for the original model.

title: Alien aquatic plants in a thermally abnormal river and their assembly to neophyte-dominated macrophyte stands (River Erft, Northrhine-Westphalia)
authors: Hussner A.; Lösch R.
keywords: Biodiversity | Competition | Egeria densa | Myriophyllum aquaticum | Vallisneria spiralis
abstract: Floristic surveys, vegetation mapping, and detailed transect analyses rendered a macrophyte flora of 14 native and five alien taxa of flowering plants in the River Erft, a contributory of the River Rhine in Northrhine-Westphalia. Water temperatures of this river do not fall below 10 °C all the year round, for reasons of geothermically heated water discharged from nearby opencast mining areas. Macrophyte stand structures, composed of the neophytes Azolla filiculoides and Lemna minuta (floating) and Myriophyllum aquaticum, Egeria densa, and Vallisneria spiralis (rooted in the muddy or sandy ground of the river) are described and the ecological requirements of these taxa are characterized. The alien species can be seen as elements that increase the α-diversity of the aquatic vegetation of the River Erft. They do not replace any of the native species, even if shifts in the competition dynamics occur. The colonization by neophytes of the abnormally warmed River Erft can be appreciated as paradigmatic for trends in the macrophyte vegetation of medium-sized rivers in Central Europe when climate-related or discharge-based heating of the waterbody occurs and propagules of alien plants imported by waterfowl or - more important - plants from aquarium waste will find suitable places of existence and spread. © 2005 Elsevier GmbH. All rights reserved.

title: Landslides with natural pre-existing slip planes - Part 2
source: World of Mining Surface and Underground
authors: Gudehus G.; Pierschke K.J.
abstract: The lateral support in spatial slide movements of landslides with natural pre-existing slip planes, was investigated. One half of a typical opencast mining window with assumed slip planes was depicted, the lower part of which exhibited the sliding bodies separately. A large-scale test on the scale 1:50 was carried out. On an inclined base, a nearly saturated soft layer of clay was placed, and a bank of loose moist sand was tipped on it. For slopes with an opencast mining window, calculations revealed that the window and the lateral support effect compensate each other. The results show that the sliding bodies on opencast mining windows in particular 'straigthen themselves out' by well-controlled deformations.

title: Project planning and scheduling using Pronet
source: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
authors: Samanta D.; Tripathy D.P.
abstract: Project network analysis techniques (CPM and PERT) help in designing, planning, co-ordination, controlling and decision making in order to accomplish the project economically in the minimum available time with the limited available resources. The paper deals with the basic concepts of CPM and PERT techniques and their differences and applications succinctly. Further, an attempt has been made to develop a comprehensive, menu-driven, graphics software package (Pronet) in Turbo 'C', to solve network problems. For planning and scheduling of an opencast mining project under Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL), the utility of the software was verified.

title: Environmental pollution status as a result of limestone and dolomite mining - A case study
authors: Mishra P.; Sahu H.; Patel R.
abstract: Rapid industrial and developmental activities have put the emphasis on opencast mining for greater and economic recovery of minerals. But mining operations not only disrupt the natural ecosystem in a significant way, but also bring about a number of health hazards and socio-economic disturbances to the local people. In the present paper the air and water pollution aspects of limestone and dolomite mines on the nearby locality has been investigated. It was observed that the common parameters of air and water are within the prescribed limits. A number of people in this area are affected by tuberculosis, which may be due to prolonged exposure to dust in mines. Copyright © Enviromedia.

title: Effect of opencast mining on soil fertility
source: Journal of Scientific and Industrial Research
authors: Ghose M.K.
keywords: Microbial | Opencast | Preservation | Sterile | Stockpile | Topsoil
abstract: In the process of opencast mining, several changes occur in physical, chemical, and microbiological properties of soil as a result of mining and storage. Inability to preserve topsoil is one of the basic hindrances to restoration of mined land. The acute problem in preserving mine soil is discussed. Every year large areas are continually becoming unfertile in spite of efforts to grow vegetation on the degraded mined land One large opencast coal project of Eastern Coalfields Ltd. (ECL) is investigated to assess the deterioration of soil properties due to stripping and stockpiling. Different age classes of mine soil dumps are identified for the study. Mine soil characteristics of the dumps are compared with those of unmined soil and analyzed critically to evaluate deterioration of soil properties with respect to time of stockpiling. The changes in soil quality were found to be drastic in the first year and continually deteriorating every year, and ultimately the soil became unfertile.

title: Mechanised spraying device - A novel technology for spraying fire protective coating material in the benches of opencast coal mines for preventing spontaneous combustion
authors: Singh R.V.K.; Singh V.K.
abstract: Spontaneous combustion in coal mines play a vital role in occurrences of fire. Fire in coal, particularly in opencast mines not only causes irreparable loss of national wealth but damages the surface structure and pollutes the environment. The problem of spontaneous combustion/fire in opencast coal benches is acute. Presently over 75% of the total production of coal in Indian mines is being carried out by opencast mining. Accordingly a mechanised spraying device has been developed for spraying the fire protective coating material for preventing spontaneous combustion in coal benches of opencast mines jointly by Central Mining Research Institute, Dhanbad and M/s Signum Fire Protection (India) Pvt. Ltd., Nagpur under Science & Technology (S&T) project funded by Ministry of Coal, Govt. of India. The objective of this paper is to describe in detail about the mechanised spraying device and its application for spraying fire protective coating material in the benches of opencast coal mines for preventing spontaneous combustion/fire. © 2004 Kluwer Academic Publishers.

title: Performance tests on large-hole drilling machines
authors: Schumacher L.
abstract: In the civil engineering industry loose-rock drilling both with and without material excavation forms the basis for many different types of construction project. When setting situ-cast piles the industry now often employs a casing pipe which is installed either by retary or oscillatory means to serve as a support pipe and/or wash pipe. Dewatering and ground water-lowering ahead of opencast mining operations calls for the preparation of filtering wells whose cavity excavations are also produced using cased boreholes. The factional resistance of the casing acts between the pipe and the loose ground and is determined by machineand process-dependent factors as well as by soil-mechanical parameters. The paper presents the main performance-detennining relationships, as obtained by both theoretical and empirical studies, which influence the amount of torque that is required during the casing process in order to overcome the peripheral friction and uses survey measurements to support the findings.

title: Estimation criteria for energy consumption by mining equipment in quarries
authors: Cheskidov V.I.; Kortelev O.B.; Aleksandrov A.N.; Il'Bul'Din D.K.
keywords: Criteria | Equipment | Fuel | Opencast mining
abstract: The regularities of fuel consumption by mining equipment during opencast mining are established. The criteria and procedure are proposed for calculating the rates of fuel consumption for mining equipment with diesel drive. © 2004 Springer Science+Business Media, Inc.

title: Deterioration of soil quality due to stockpiling in coal mining areas
authors: Ghose M.K.; Kundu N.K.
keywords: Opencast mining | Overburden | Reclamation | Stockpiles | Topsoil
abstract: In the process of opencast mining, the area is to be stripped of vegetation to remove the overburden. Several changes occur in the physical, chemical and microbiological properties of soil as a result of mining and storage. One large opencast coal project of Eastern Coalfields Ltd (ECL) was investigated to assess the deterioration in soil quality. The study reveals a major qualitative deterioration in the excavated soil when dumped over a long period of time. This inability to preserve topsoil is one of the basic hindrances to restoration of mined land and overburden dumps. Hence the topsoil should be stockpiled only when it is impractical to redistribute promptly over the affected areas.

title: Loading and transport system at SMC - Optimization
source: Journal of the South African Institute of Mining and Metallurgy
authors: Vemba M.M.D.S.
abstract: Engineering refers to the application of mathematics and other sciences to logically develop solutions to problems. However, in opencast mining, due to the randomness of operations, the use of mathematics is often neglected. Instead, practices that have proven successful elsewhere tend to apply. At the other end of the scale, mathematical models have been developed to identify and quantify all the operational parameters involved in the loading and haulage of ore. These are then used to optimize the operation. Optimization, in this context, refers to the reduction of cost through effective utilization of the available time and resources. Considering these mathematical models, the loading and transport system at SMC (Catoca Mining Society) will be assessed with a view to its optimization. The discussion will be introduced by considering the mine background and other general information, which win highlight the main operational variables.

abstract: A comparative estimation is performed for the up-to-date methods of rock failure with respect to the specific energy consumption of failure. The spheres of application of the methods discussed in executive elements of mining machines are tentatively determined depending on the properties of rocks.

authors: Sklenicka P.; Prikryl I.; Svoboda I.; Lhota T.
keywords: Degraded landscape | Non-productive priorities | Post-mining landscape | Rehabilitation
abstract: Remediation of the environmental (and social) disturbances caused by opencast brown coal mining in the past in north-west Bohemia is a priority for state environmental policy. In order to provide a concept for full restoration of land following disturbance by opencast mining, a special interdisciplinary project supported by a grant from the Czech Ministry of Environment was started in 2000. The initial stage of the project was intended to summarize and evaluate the findings and the works carried out in connection with various reclamation activities in the afflicted area over a period of more than 50 years. The main aims of the three-year project are to make use of the best available landscape environmental management knowledge in order to harmonize the ecological, aesthetic, productive and social functions of new valuable landscape, including the recovery of historical continuity and an understanding of 'landscape memory'. The basic landscape functions were assessed on two different scale levels. On a large scale, the relevant attributes were investigated over the whole area of the Sokolov brown coal basin (220 km<sup>2</sup>). The data and experience acquired were used to define large-scale guiding principles for the rehabilitation of a post-mining landscape. On a small scale, the basic characteristics and functions of the landscape were analysed in the Litov-Chlum model area (2 km<sup>2</sup>). The information derived from this analysis was used to formulate a small-scale approach for the rehabilitation of the model area and also to define general methodological principles.

title: Dust precipitation nuisance in the Rhine lignite basin - Situation analysis, legal assessment and the use of compost recycling for emission-protection purpose
authors: Asenbaum P.
abstract: The paper describes the problem of dust precipitation in the Rhine lignite basin and presents a legal, scientific and technical assessment of how composting can be used for emission protection purposes, along with supporting measures such as the replanting of opencast mining sites. Also examines the benefits, and possible risks, associated with waste recycling projects of this kind. The results of the investigations show that compost recycling for emission-protection purposes can be used to support the emission-protection measures previously deployed at opencast mines in the Rhine lignite basin, including the grassing-over of former mine sites. Such measures are now considered to be technically feasible, environmentally compatible and lawful, and indeed are considered necessary in some circumstances.

title: Competitive lignite thanks to more efficient opencast mining processes
source: World of Mining Surface and Underground
authors: Gärtner D.
abstract: The opencast mining process operations of RWE Power AG, which was formed by merging the RWE Power and the RWE Rheinbraun in Germany is discussed. The range of energy sources used in the generation process of RWE Power AG are lignite and nuclear energy in the base load, hard coal, gas and renewable energies in the intermediate and peak loads. In the year 2002, 147 bn kWh of power was produced in the lignite-hard coal-as well as gas-fired power plants and another 43 bn kWh was also generated on the basis of nuclear and renewable energies. With its broad energy mix, the RWE Power AG is seen to be a competitive, eco-friendly and reliable partner for its electricity customers.

title: Assessment of air pollution indices in opencast coal mining complex - An Indian case study
authors: Ghose M.K.
keywords: Coking coal | Dominant wind | Dragline | Overall air pollution
abstract: India is world's third largest coal-producing country and to meet the future energy demand it will have to produce coal at a faster rate. The coal by opencast mining has been about 80% of the total production. This paper focuses on some of the key air pollution problems arising from increased use of opencast mining. It examines the utility of an Air Pollution Index (API) for tackling air pollution problems. A fact-finding survey was conducted to evaluate the status of air pollution due to opencast coal mining in Jharia Coalfield of Bharat Coking Coal Ltd. The approach for the selection of air monitoring stations, its monitoring programme, data analysis and results are discussed. The Oak Ridge Air Quality Index (ORAQI) was used to evaluate the relative ranking of overall air quality different locations within the mining complex. The paper recommends the use of API data rather than individual air pollution level data when attempting to develop effective air pollution control strategies for mining areas.

title: A methodology for cumulative impact assessment of opencast mining projects with special reference to air quality assessment
authors: Dutta P.; Mahatha S.; De P.
keywords: Air quality | Cumulative impact assessment | India | Opencast mining
abstract: It has been recognized worldwide that consideration of cumulative impacts should be an integral part of the environmental impact assessment process and that sector-specific methodologies should be evolved to address these impacts. A generic methodology for cumulative impact assessment of opencast mining projects has been developed with special reference to air quality assessment. It involved questionnaire checklists and a geographical information system for scoping of the impact assessment study, and the ISCST3 air quality dispersion model for the analysis of impacts. Its use was illustrated by a case study at an opencast iron ore mine. The methodology could identify a number of potentially significant cumulative impacts. Also, the analysis of air quality impact suggested that in some areas surrounding the mine the cumulative pollutant levels could be significantly high even if the effects of project-related impact were low. © 2004 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.

title: Climatic extremes in the linienbandkeramik period (5300-5000 BC) - The interpretation of dendrochronological and archaeological contexts
authors: Schmidt B.; Gruhle W.; Rück O.
abstract: A new dendrochronological method (homogeneity analysis) shows dry phases occuring before the beginning and at the end of the Linienbandkeramik (LBK). During the whole time of the LBK the climate was humid and warm/maritime. For this period three humid phases could be established. The amount of precipitation might have increased, a development which went along with an increase in building activity in the settlements. The site Kaster is situated in the old bed of the river Erft which today belongs to the area of West German opencast mining. The investigation of the site indicated the existence of a bridge over the Erft. The posts of the bridge date to a period around 4700 BC. It is at just this time when the climatic graph shows a distinctive dry phase. At Kaster also three horizons of sediments can be recognized: from the time of the LBK, from the pre-Roman Iron Age and from the Roman period. On the precipitation graph there are peaks for these three periods.

title: Renewal of land damaged by coal mining for its sustainable, beneficial use in the Indian context
authors: Ghose M.K.
keywords: Coal mining | Opencast | Preservation | Sterile | Stockpile | Topsoil
abstract: Mineral extraction processes must ensure the return to productivity of land affected by coal mining. In the process of opencast coal mining and storage, several changes occur in the physical, chemical and microbiological properties of soil. Systematic handling and storage practices can protect the properties of topsoil while in storage after it has been redistributed on regraded areas. The damage to land by opencast mining in the Indian context is discussed. The properties of topsoil were found to deteriorate, ultimately becoming biologically sterile. The issue is the preservation of topsoil (stockpiling) in the restoration of mined land, and large areas are continuing to become unproductive every year. The concept of the shelf-life of topsoil has been developed, and its applicability, likely impact, economic benefit and significance in the field of environmental protection are discussed. The study area is described, and the approach for the selection of soil sampling locations for the assessment of continual degradation of stockpiled soil is discussed. The soil data are critically analysed to determine the optimum period up to which the soil can be preserved by technical reclamation alone. Topsoil preservation and renewal of damaged land for its sustainable, beneficial use is discussed. The methodology may be adopted for use on an industrial scale at a variety of sites. © 2004 EPP Publications Ltd.

title: Environmental Impacts of Blasting and Mitigating Measures: Experience in Indian Surface Coal Mines
source: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
authors: Mishra A.
keywords: Blasting | Flyrock | Ground vibration | Noise | Shock tube initiation system
abstract: Ever growing demand of coal and mineral with sprawl of urbanisation and increased environmental consciousness of human being have compelled opencast mining projects to run under constraints. With increases in stripping ratio, size of equipment has also increased considerably with increase of blast size. This has compelled to use such system of blasting, which will produce either no flyrock, or very less flyrock with minimum projection, ground vibration, noise and good fragmentation. Objective of this research work was to establish knowledge on shock tube in hole delay blasting by studying post blast parameters in open-cast coal mines. In this study one open cast mine was selected and number of blasts were conducted and observed. Ten blasts were initiated with conventional detonating cord while rests of the blasts were initiated with shock tube NONEL system. As the mine and bench, where studies conducted were same, strata conditions were similar. Detailed investigation was done to study influence of shock in hole delay blasting on post blast parameters such as flyrock generation, ground vibration and noise using high speed video camera and ground vibration recorders. On the basis of above study major conclusion has been drawn that the shock tube in hole delay blasting is a better system of initiation over conventional system of initiation with respect to ground vibration, air overpressure and flyrock generation.

title: Rational conditions of application of multi-link cyclic systems
authors: Bakhturin Y.A.; Bannykh S.A.
abstract: In-line (continuous) and cyclic operation of transportation systems at the mining enterprises has been considered. Method of opencast mining has been discussed. Since 1980, the three-link systems were applied. Motor transport, railroad transport, and conveyers are used in the systems. Ore and rock transportation has been considered. Rational conditions of the systems have been determined. Dynamics of transportation of ore and rocks with the use of railroad transport, motor transport, and conveyers has been presented. Mathematical model of transportation of the materials by means of the systems has been developed.

title: Grounding of non-uniformity of load flow and parameters of transient section
authors: Karmaev G.; Tyul'kin A.
abstract: In-line (continuous) and cyclic operation of transportation systems at the mining enterprises has been considered. Method of opencast mining has been discussed. Charging the rocks on conveyers has been described. One point of charging or several points of charging can be provided. More reliable results are observed in case of the second version. This is connected with the fact that presence of several points of charging the materials leads to improvement in conditions of operation of motor transport. Mathematical model of charging the materials on belt of conveyer has been developed. Length of transient section has been determined.

title: Perspective trends in scientific and technical development of in-line technology
authors: Ruban A.; Shenderov A.
abstract: In line (continuous) and cyclic operation of transportation systems at the mining enterprises has been considered. Method of opencast mining has been discussed. Various approaches and technical solutions which makes it possible to improve efficiency of transportation have been described. New advanced wheel excavators have been developed. Efficient hydraulic drives for the excavators have been created. Application of continuous surface miner has been considered. Rational use of various transportation systems has been discussed. The crushing equipment has been described. Efficiency of screw-tooth crusher has been shown.

title: An approach towards the estimation of emission rate from various activities of Noamundi Iron Ore Mine - A case study
source: Journal of Scientific and Industrial Research
authors: Banerjee G.K.; Srivastava K.K.; Chakraborty M.K.; Sundararajan M.
abstract: The major activities of Noamundi iron ore mine in response to serious impact of air pollution in and around the mining area are identified. A mathematical model is developed to estimate the emission rates from various activities or sources. The present model is developed based on the Pasquill-Gifford formula. Detailed studies over processing plant operations, geology, meteorology of the study area are carried out in order to prepare the emission inventory of the opencast mining activity through estimating the emission rates of the significant activities, using the present mathematical model. A few recommendations on the basis of the results of the study are also given.

title: Trends in relief design and construction in opencast mining reclamation
authors: Nicolau J.M.
keywords: Ecological restoration | Mining reclamation | RUSLE model | SIBERIA model | Soil erosion | Topographic reconstruction
abstract: This paper examines trends in topography design and construction in opencast mining restoration. The greatest geomorphological focus is the protection of aquatic ecosystems downstream of reclaimed sites through the construction of topographies and structures that not only reduce sediments and contaminants to a minimum, but which soften the impact of maximum water flows. From the ecological point of view, the most important focus is the integration of the geomorphological component with those of the soil and vegetation, and the formation of a functional ecosystem with the capacity to maintain itself. The conceptual models of relief that have been used in practice are discussed and criticized: these include the platform-bank model (geotechnically but not ecologically stable), faithful reproduction of the original topography (inadequate in steep areas), and understanding the hydrological basin as a restoration unit (now considered the most appropriate). Finally, erosion models are reviewed as tools for relief design. The practically of 'RUSLE 1.06 for Mined Lands, Construction Sites and Reclaimed Lands' is underlined owing to its ease of use. © 2003 John Wiley and Sons, Ltd.

title: Validation of two air quality models for Indian mining conditions
authors: Chaulya S.K.; Ahmad M.; Singh R.S.; Bandopadhyay L.K.; Bondyopadhay C.; Mondal G.C.
keywords: Dispersion modelling | Emission rate | Opencast mine | Suspended particulate matter | Validation study
abstract: All major mining activity particularly opencast mining contributes to the problem of suspended particulate matter (SPM) directly or indirectly. Therefore, assessment and prediction are required to prevent and minimize the deterioration of SPM due to various opencast mining operations. Determination of emission rate of SPM for these activities and validation of air quality models are the first and foremost concern. In view of the above, the study was taken up for determination of emission rate for SPM to calculate emission rate of various opencast mining activities and validation of commonly used two air quality models for Indian mining conditions. To achieve the objectives, eight coal and three iron ore mining sites were selected to generate site specific emission data by considering type of mining, method of working, geographical location, accessibility and above all resource availability. The study covers various mining activities and locations including drilling, overburden loading and unloading, coal/mineral loading and unloading, coal handling or screening plant, exposed overburden dump, stock yard, workshop, exposed pit surface, transport road and haul road. Validation of the study was carried out through Fugitive Dust Model (FDM) and Point, Area and Line sources model (PAL2) by assigning the measured emission rate for each mining activity, meteorological data and other details of the respective mine as an input to the models. Both the models were run separately for the same set of input data for each mine to get the predicted SPM concentration at three receptor locations for each mine. The receptor locations were selected such a way that at the same places the actual filed measurement were carried out for SPM concentration. Statistical analysis was carried out to assess the performance of the models based on a set measured and predicted SPM concentration data. The value of coefficient of correlation for PAL2 and FDM was calculated to be 0.990-0.994 and 0.966-0.997, respectively, which shows a fairly good agreement between measured and predicted values of SPM concentration. The average index of agreement values for PAL2 and FDM was found to be 0.665 and 0.752, respectively, which represents that the prediction by PAL2 and FDM models are accurate by 66.5 and 75.2%, respectively. These indicate that FDM model is more suited for Indian mining conditions.

title: Bring back the miners
abstract: Massive redevelopment of a former colliery in central Scotland hinges on restarting mining of rich coal reserves and extensive clean-up of the contaminated site. The coal worked at Polkemmet was at depth and the site was surrounded by a number of smaller collieries where coal was extracted from near-surface seams. These extensive abandoned workings have presented a problem to developers because of their potential for collapse and the expense of stabilising them using conventional consolidation methods. The new plan involves opencast mining in the potentially unstable areas and backfilling the voids with, as far as possible, on-site materials including colliery spoil and fill. But the main issue for development is the extent of contamination caused by centuries of coal mining and industry. Particular areas of concern are ground and groundwater conditions around the former head works and infrastructure; Eastfield Quarry, which for many years was used as a toxic waste dump; the bings; contaminated minewater and groundwater and their potential connectivity.

Efforts on production and productivity enhancement with LHDs in bord and pillar method in SCCL - A case study
source: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
authors: Rao A.; Reddy R.; Hussain M.
abstract: Coal mining industry in India has undergone a sea change in the post nationalisation era. Many new mining methods and technologies were introduced both in OC and UG scenario. Opencast mining made gigantic strides and still dominating the Indian coal mining industry. In UG scenario, though the performance of longwall is not up to the expected level, other methods such as blasting gallery for thick seams and semi-mechanisation with SDLs/LHDs in bord and pillar mining have been successful. In underground mining, bord and pillar is the predominant method in India. Intermediate technology with SDLs/LHDs being flexible and compatible with B&P method is gaining rapid momentum for improving underground production and productivity as well as replacing the conventional cumbersome basket loading. Though flexible and compatible, LHDs/SDLs require some simple basic planning for tapping performance potential. It is observed that the performance has not been optimum with LHDs loading into tubs or chain conveyors due to the mismatch of loading and conveying system from the performance statistics of LHDs of Coal India. In this paper, the authors have attempted to present their efforts in introducing various simple techniques for accelerating the performance of LHDs in one of the mines of SCCL The authors noted that LHDs/SDLs loading the coal on pony belt conveyors is the appropriate combination of loading and conveying system and this combination along with the other techniques described in the paper were able to improve the availability and utilisation of LHDs/SDLs which in turn resulted in improved production and productivity.

title: Longwall technology - The need for promotion
source: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
authors: Hanjura C.; Suresh D.; Sudhakar L.
abstract: Though longwall technology was introduced in India in the year 1906-07, it was only since 1978 that the technology has been planned for bulk production by introduction of powered roof supports, DERD shearers and high capacity face conveyors. With reserves amenable to opencast mining depleting, underground mining by conventional bord and pillar method becoming economically unviable, the longwall technology, provides the long term solution for coal production with viable economics to meet the energy demands of the country.

title: Stressed state of ore mass in case of layer system of exploitation
source: Fiziko Tekhnicheskie Problemy Razrabotki Poleznykh Iskopaemykh
